description: An interactive on what is finished, still under construction and what life beside the work looks like.

title: Common ground
description: IT appears that the PML-N, echoing the PPP’s recent offer, is also willing to re-engage with the opposition, at least on counterterrorism policy. Though that may seem like a narrow scope for dialogue, in our vitiated political environment, it does offer an opening. Whether the opposition is interested in taking it up is a different question. The anger over the dismissal of the elected PTI government in KP is still far from subsiding, and the ruling coalition in Islamabad deserves much of the blame for making a negotiated settlement more difficult than it seemed two weeks ago. That said, the opposition also needs to introspect. From the murmurings of resentment within its ranks, it appears that the outcome of its last round of discussions with the government was not what many were hoping for. Yet, its street agitation has delivered even less. An offer for dialogue, even if focused on counterterrorism strategy, is still an opportunity to return to the negotiating table and continue from where the last round of talks left off. Complete disengagement will achieve nothing. Regrettably, the two sides still fail to see the country’s economic, security, and governance crises as challenges that must be solved politically. A nation of 260m can hardly afford such paralysis. The greater onus lies with the government. It is difficult to see how a credible counterterrorism strategy can be framed when the province on the front line of the fight has just been deprived of its elected government. If Islamabad wants its offer to be taken seriously, it should pair it with a real gesture of good faith , starting with a meaningful voice for KP’s elected representatives in any talks. Yet the government seems consumed by the hubris of unchecked power, while the opposition, particularly the PTI, continues to act as if agitation alone can yield results. Instead of evading Pakistan’s challenges through constant jousting and whataboutery, the political leadership needs to confront its failings. Counterterrorism, where the stakes for KP are the highest and broad-based consensus is urgently needed, is as good a place as any to begin. But it must lead to a much wider conversation on national issues. If the two sides cannot find common ground even on the fight against terrorism, the public would be justified in wondering what, if anything, they are capable of agreeing on. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: LHC issues notices to foreign secretary in contempt cases over detention of PTI-linked Pakistanis in UAE
description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday issued notices to Foreign Secretary Asim Iftikhar in two separate contempt petitions over alleged non-compliance with an earlier court order concerning two PTI-affiliated Pakistani citizens detained in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). On September 14, the LHC had directed the foreign secretary to process and decide within 15 days representations concerning the detention of two citizens — Syed Salman Raza Zaidi and Muhammad Junaid Jahangir. Justice Sadiq Mehmood Khurram heard the contempt petitions on Thursday. Barrister Abuzar Salman Niazi appeared on behalf of the petitioners and alleged that the two individuals remained deprived of consular, diplomatic, and legal access. He recalled the court’s Sept 14 directive and contended that the petitioners had not been formally informed of any decision on their representations, even though a considerable amount of time had passed. The counsel urged the court to initiate contempt proceedings against the foreign secretary for non-compliance. After hearing initial arguments, Justice Khurram issued notices to the respondent secretary for submission of his reply by October 29. In the main petitions, the counsel stated that Zaidi went missing from his residence in Sharjah on Sept 27, 2024, and was subsequently taken into custody by UAE authorities. He said despite nearly two years having passed, the petitioner, Faryal Zainab, had still not been provided clear information regarding the charges against her husband Zaidi, the judicial proceedings, any sentence, or the complete court record. Meanwhile, Advocate Niazi said Jahangir was allegedly detained on Sept 24, 2024, at Dubai airport on his return from Saudi Arabia. Muhammad Ibrahim, Jahangir’s father, filed the petition challenging the alleged failure of the federal government and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) to provide effective consular protection and legal assistance. The counsel for the petitioners submitted that despite representations having been filed regarding the detention of both citizens before the foreign secretary, the representations had not been processed. Both petitioners had asked the court to direct that legal and consular assistance be provided to Zaidi and Jahangir, that their judicial records be obtained and that diplomatic-level steps be taken toward their return to Pakistan.

title: Karachi judicial magistrate rejects bail plea of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan
description: KARACHI: A local court on Thursday rejected TV anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan’s bail plea in a cybercrime case pertaining to the alleged dissemination of anti-state content. Hassan was arrested last week for allegedly disseminating anti-state, false and defamatory content through his official social media accounts. He was booked under multiple sections of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). According to an order issued by the judicial magistrate, a copy of which is available with Dawn , “the order disposes of the bail application filed under Section 497 of the CrPC on behalf of the applicant/accused, Syed Iqrar Ul Hassan, son of Syed Muhammad Ismail, who has been arrested in connection with FIR No. 101/2026 registered at Police Station NCCIA, Cyber Crime Reporting Centre, Karachi, under Sections 9, 10, 20, 24 and 26-A of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (as amended in 2025)”. The notice of the bail application was served on the NCCIA’s additional director (legal), the order states. Earlier this week, Hassan was sent to prison on judicial remand after the NCCIA sought an extension of his physical remand by another eight days. However, Karachi (East) Judicial Magistrate-I Gulraiz Memon observed that the agency had been given “sufficient time of physical custody”. “No cogent reason has been given by NCCIA for extension of physical custody; therefore, the accused is remanded to judicial custody till Oct 26,” the judge stated in his order. The court also issued notices to the NCCIA on a bail application filed by Hassan’s defence counsel, Barrister Mian Ali Ashfaq, and fixed the matter for hearing on Oct 21. On Oct 17, Hassan was produced before Judicial Magistrate Memon upon the completion of his initial four-day physical remand. The NCCIA sought a further 10 days of custody for questioning, but the magistrate rejected the request and granted the agency two more days. The magistrate also dismissed a plea filed by Hassan’s counsel under Section 63 of the CrPC seeking his discharge from the case. In its remand report, the NCCIA said the investigation had progressed but several important aspects remained to be examined in light of the forensic analysis of Hassan’s seized digital devices and records from other departments, including the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra). The agency said digital devices containing 1,145.89 gigabytes of data had been handed over to its forensic team for analysis to identify relevant applications, social media accounts, email accounts, stored files and communications linked to the alleged content. The NCCIA also sought further custody to trace the “origin, relation, financial correlation and cross-border linkages (if any)” of the posts. In his earlier order, the magistrate observed that collecting digital footprints, technical data and forensic evidence required reasonable time, adding that discharging an accused while the investigation was under way could hamper the process. The NCCIA alleged that the content was intended to incite the public against constitutional implementation and could cause panic, disorder and unrest. Hassan was booked under sections 9 (glorification of an offence), 10 (cyberterrorism), 24 (cyberstalking) and 26A (Punishment for false and fake information) of Peca. He had been critical of the government’s policies on social media.

title: Saudis intercept more drones as conflict with Houthis spirals
description: • Coalition downs six drones launched towards cities, including Madina, as interception debris kills two • Rebels deny ‘deep operations’ in Saudi territory • Iran says Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ • Macron arrives in Riyadh for ‘surprise solidarity visit’ RIYADH: As the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement continues to escalate, the Saudi-led coalition on Wednesday said it had intercepted six drones launched towards the kingdom, including in the Madina region. “Four drones launched towards the kingdom have been intercepted and destroyed,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X, adding in a second post that the interceptions took place in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern region as well as Madina. Al-Malki, who did not specify who was behind the launches, later said drones had been intercepted, also in the eastern region. The Houthis denied having targeted the kingdom, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying their forces had not carried out any “deep” operations in Saudi territory. The Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility “resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others”. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Within Yemen, the Houthis claimed an attack on Wednesday on a military camp near the airport in the southern city of Aden, where the Yemeni government is based. “Our armed forces were able to target the Saudi enemy’s operations room in the Badr camp in Aden with a ballistic missile,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a statement. A government military source and a local official told Reuters the group also attacked Riyan airport in the southeastern coastal city of Mukalla. “The Houthis used missiles and drones to target a military base housing forces from the Saudi-led coalition at Al Rayyan airport,” one of the officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP. Saree said the group had targeted “military equipment transported by the Saudi enemy via military cargo planes to Al Rayyan airport”. Egypt to support Saudis Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen,” state-linked media reported. Al-Qahera News , which is closely linked to state intelligence and is to broadcast a speech by Sisi, reported that he also said “the stability of our brothers in the Gulf concerns Egypt’s national security”. The speech itself has not yet been aired by Wednesday night. Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. Iran warns against interference However, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Mr Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”. The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July. Macron meets MbS Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Riyadh in a surprise “solidarity” visit, and met Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Macron is the first Western leader to visit since the Houthis intensified their attacks on the kingdom this month. The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: ‘Letting roots of Pak-India conflict fester invites more danger’
description: ISLAMABAD: Failure to address the underlying disputes that engender crises between Pakistan and India could lead to more dangerous confrontations in the future, a former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee warned on Wednesday. “Terminating a crisis without addressing its root causes only sets the stage for the next, more dangerous conflict,” retired Gen Zubair Mahmood Hayat said at the concluding session of the second Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference, organised by the Strategic Vision Institute (SVI). Ex-CJCSC warns against ignoring Kashmir dispute, Indus treaty suspension He said that in the subcontinent, the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir could not be wished away or reduced to an administrative matter. “Similarly, water cannot be converted from a shared necessity into an instrument of power and pressure,” he said while stressing the need for resolution of the Kashmir dispute and restoration of the Indus Waters Treaty. Gen Hayat warned that repeated crises between the nuclear-armed neighbours could become increasingly dangerous if unresolved disputes, diminishing restraint and the absence of sustained political dialogue continued to undermine regional security. Referring to the May 2025 conflict , he said Pakistan had demonstrated its military capabilities and political control through a calibrated response that denied India a unilateral fait accompli without pursuing an unlimited war. “The larger lesson is not that conflict between two nuclear-armed neighbours can be made routine; it is that there is no tested and certified safe space for war,” he said, warning that future crises would involve different leaders, emerging technologies and shorter decision-making timelines, heightening the risk of miscalculation. He said South Asia lacked an inclusive regional security framework, effective crisis-management mechanisms and sustained political dialogue. “The region lives between deterrence that prevents the worst and disputes that repeatedly regenerate danger,” he said. Gen Hayat warned unverified allegations could trigger conflict before the facts were established, with a future confrontation potentially arising from an accident rather than a deliberate state decision. He cited the continuing Operation Sindoor in this context. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: PTI leadership ‘turns on itself’ after protest debacle
description: Salman Akram Raja • Raja ‘rebukes’ move by KP lawmakers to nominate Gandapur as interim KP president • Ex-CM fires back, demands apology from secy gen over ‘name-calling’ PESHAWAR: The debacle that befell the PTI’s recent protest march has led to serious fissures within the core committee, with demands emerging from within for chan­ges at the leadership level that can steer the party out of its current crisis. The bad blood became public on Wednesday as two senior party leaders — Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur — traded accusations of betraying the party cause. Meanwhile, a woman parliamentarian from Peshawar echoed the sentiments of many within the core committee when she demanded accountability over the failure of the party’s much-touted protest march, which resulted in the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, and created more problems for their jailed leader, Imran Khan. The Salman Akram-Ali Amin spat on X (formerly Twitter) followed reports that a group of lawmakers from the KP Assembly had met to endorse the latter’s nomination as acting provincial president in place of MNA Junaid Akbar, who has been missing since the imposition of governor’s rule. The handwritten text, addressed to interim party chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and seen by Dawn , said that the meeting “unanimously” proposed to nominate Mr Gandapur as the acting provincial president in the absence of Junaid Akbar, calling the ex-CM “the right man for the right job”. The Oct 14 meeting, which according to one participant was held via Zoom and WhatsApp, was attended by around 55 provincial lawmakers. Their four-pronged agenda included party organisation issues; the status of negotiations with the government; the party’s plan for further protests; and legal issues. The main outcome that invited derision from Mr Raja, however, was the resolution demanding that Mr Gandapur be appointed the acting provincial president immediately. This prompted the secretary general to take a dig at “the narrative” regarding a possible announcement by a group of party MPAs, nominating a new provincial president without permission from their jailed leader Imran Khan, or the party’s political committee. He put the number of these dissidents at 68. Ali Amin Gandapur The secretary general accused the group of cutting off contact with Sohail Afridi and his team in the final days of the protest march, paving the way for state coercion, emergency and governor’s rule in the province. He asserted that Ali Asghar, the party’s provincial general secretary, remained the acting provincial head and Mr Afridi continued to be the chief minister, in accordance with the law and Constitution. “Those spreading doubts — the snakes and the serpents — will be defeated,” he wrote while concluding his post on X. Subsequently, an angry Mr Gandapur took to X to hit back at the secretary general’s claims; in a series of tweets and audio messages, he took strong exception to Mr Raja’s tone and tenor. Demanding that he bring to an end “the spectacle” that had been made of the party, the former KP CM said that the secretary general had no right to accuse others of conspiracy, or call them names like “snakes and serpents”. “Do you understand this? We know how to make others understand if they don’t get this,” he said in an angry tone. Accusing Mr Raja of “hiding” during the party’s protest movement, he asked what sacrifices he had rendered for the party, and demanded the secretary general apologise for his remarks. “At a time when the party is facing unprecedented political challenges, levelling vague accusations and using mocking language against your own elected representatives does not befit responsible leadership,” he wrote on X. “I don’t know who has fed Salman Akram Raja and what the purpose of his tweet was”, Mr Gandapur continued. He also wondered why Mr Raja and Barrister Gohar did not attend parliamentary party meetings, despite repeated invitations to discuss the fallout of the decisions they had taken, which had brought the party to this juncture. “If the parliamentary party of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa wants to seek a constitutional and political solution to the current crisis through consultation within itself, who has given a few individuals the authority to label these elected representatives as traitors, conspirators, or undemocratic?” Incidentally, this is not the first time that both men have taken to social media to air their internal party grievances. In 2025, ahead of a nationwide protest, Mr Gandapur and then-PTI Punjab organiser Aliya Hamza Malik had become embroiled in a similar argument over social media. At the time, the argument had prompted a censure from the jailed party founder, who had strictly instructed senior officeholders and junior members alike to avoid expressing “internal differences on social media, electronic media, print media, or any other platform”. “Publicly airing internal matters or individual concerns before the media is entirely unacceptable,” Imran Khan had said at the time. The latest exchange between the two party leaders also harkened to an outburst from MPA Mashal Yousafzai — former spokesperson to Bushra Bibi — who has blamed the former chief minister and a few other party leaders for the failure of the protest march and subsequent imposition of governor’s rule. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: PTI asks govt to ‘rebuild trust’ if it is serious about talks
description: • Demands reversal of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency measures, release of political prisoners and Imran’s access to his personal physicians • Claims party’s ‘popularity’ still intact despite ‘coercion’ ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Wednesday called on the government to take confidence-building measures (CBMs) to pave the way for meaningful dialogue, demanding the reversal of what it described as “unlawful” measures, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and release of political prisoners. In a statement, PTI Central Infor­mation Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said meaningful negotiations required concrete action rather than political statements. “If the government was genuinely serious about dialogue, it should take steps to build trust,” he added. Mr Akram demanded the reversal of measures the party considered unlawful, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate and release of political prisoners whose continued detention, he said, could not be legally justified. He also called for the protection of PTI founder Imran Khan’s constitutional and fundamental rights, including lawful meetings with his lawyers and family, fair and timely proceedings in his and his wife’s cases, and medical treatment under the supervision of his personal physicians in accordance with applicable court orders. Mr Akram condemned raids on homes, detentions and pressure on elected representatives and party workers in Punjab and KP, alleging that these actions were intended to intimidate political opponents. PTI’s ‘popularity’ Rejecting Information Minister Attaullah Tarar’s remarks about the party’s political standing, Mr Akram challenged all ruling coalition parties to contest elections against the PTI under a single banner. He said they would suffer a “crushing defeat in a free and fair contest, even today”. On Tuesday, Mr Tarar had said a formal ban on the PTI was no longer needed after the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in KP, arguing that the party had “lost po­­w­er” in the province because of security and counterterrorism failures. Mr Akram said the government’s use of “coercive measures and political pressure” had failed to diminish the PTI’s public support. He described the party as Pakistan’s “leading federal political force” and its founder, Imran Khan, as the “only leader enjoying widespread public support across the country”. Rejecting governor’s rule and the emergency in KP, he described the measures as an “attempt to undermine the province’s electoral mandate”. He said the party’s strength stemmed from its connection with the people rather than its control of government offices. He added that no “handpicked administration should be allowed to dictate” the political future of around 50 million residents without respecting their democratic choices and constitutional rights. Mr Akram insisted that decisions concerning the province’s governance, resources, and future must involve its elected representatives and local population. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Draft auto policy revs up hopes for cheaper vehicles
description: • PHEVs may see price reductions of over 20pc under proposed tax changes • Petrol, hybrid vehicles may become around 8-10pc cheaper • Parts makers warn rising CBU imports, lower tariffs to hurt local industry KARACHI: The draft Auto Policy 2026-31 could trigger one of the biggest shake-ups in the country’s automobile market, with prices of some vehicles potentially falling by more than 20 per cent. However, the prospect of cheaper cars may create an unusual predicament, as buyers are likely to hold back purchases in anticipation of lower prices, causing anxiety among automakers over the value of their existing inventory. According to Topline Securities, the new draft maintains the 1pc general sales tax (GST) rate on battery electric vehicles (BEVs), while setting rates at 9pc for plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) and 6pc for range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs). The earlier draft had proposed a uniform 1pc GST across all new energy vehicles (NEVs), while the previous policy imposed rates of 8.5pc to 12.75pc on PHEVs. This points to the government’s priority to incentivise the rollout of NEVs, particularly BEVs. Preliminary industry estimates suggest conventional petrol vehicles could become approximately 8-10pc cheaper, while hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) may see reductions of around 9pc. PHEVs could benefit even more, with estimated price reductions exceeding 20pc. Among BEVs, models with import values below $15,000 could see reductions of approximately 22pc compared to around 8pc for higher-priced BEVs. However, REEVs may become around 3pc more expensive under the proposed tax structure. The new draft proposes reducing tariffs on localised completely knocked-down (CKD) parts to 15pc by FY31 from 25pc previously. Topline Securities said the reduction could be detrimental to the local vendor industry, adding that the benefits were likely to be passed on to consumers amid intense competition. Parts makers sound alarm Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (PAPAAM) Chairman Abdur Rehman Aizaz said the new auto policy amounted to a “conspiracy to destroy several industries”. He said rising imports of new and used cars were already hurting the developed local auto parts industry, which now faced the threat of closures because of government policies. Mr Aizaz pointed out that imports of completely built-up (CBU) new cars rose to 2,407 units in September from 391 in August, while imports of used cars increased to 2,454 units from 1,185 over the same period. He said every new or used imported vehicle reduced potential volumes for the country’s 1,200 local auto parts manufacturers. Locally produced parts accounted for approximately Rs1.5 million of the value of each domestically assembled vehicle, he added. On that basis, the 4,861 CBU vehicles imported in September represented an estimated Rs7.3 billion in lost revenue for local parts manufacturers, Mr Aizaz said. Industry representatives said the GAC Aion UT, currently priced at around Rs6.4m, could fall to Rs5m-Rs5.2m. Higher-priced electric SUVs such as the BYD Atto 3 and GAC Aion V, priced at around Rs9m, could also see meaningful reductions. They said popular petrol and hybrid models could become more affordable as well. Industry estimates indicate potential savings of around Rs600,000 to Rs800,000 on selected variants of the Honda HR-V e:HEV, Haval Jolion and Toyota Corolla Altis. The biggest absolute reductions could emerge in the PHEV segment. A Jaecoo J7 PHEV, priced near Rs10m, could potentially fall to around Rs8m, while the Kia Sorento PHEV, which has already witnessed substantial price adjustments, could face further downward pressure from changes in GST and import duties. Sania Irfan of Topline Securities said the new draft proposed a zero per cent automotive development levy (ADL) on fossil fuel-driven vehicles below 1,000cc, 2pc on 1,000-2,000cc vehicles and 10pc on those above 2,000cc, replacing the earlier draft’s rates of 4.5-5.5pc across engine categories. Kalbe Ali in Islamabad also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Nvidia boss criticises 'cheap' AI doomsday warnings
description: AI chip giant Nvidia’s boss Jensen Huang said on Thursday that warnings that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity were “cheap” attempts to grab headlines. “When you say that it will be the end of the human civilisation, first of all, it’s not true,” he told a conference organised by his company in Berlin. While such statements generate “headlines”, they were “made up” and “cheap”, added Huang, whose visit to Berlin is the final stop of a European tour. After incidents of the technology getting around controls during tests, there has been a heated debate about whether AI presents an existential risk to humanity. In September, a researcher resigned from Anthropic with a stark warning that leading AI labs were “ gambling with our lives ”, and the bosses of Anthropic and fellow industry giant OpenAI have called for a slowdown . Huang, however, is firmly in the opposing camp, and has advocated for development of the technology to move full steam ahead. Speaking in Berlin, he urged the world to approach AI with “responsible optimism”. “If you care about the future, past our own lives, if we care about the future of sustainability, this is the perfect time — build AI,” he said. “Don’t try to stifle AI.” US regulators are seen as unlikely to intervene when it comes to AI development. President Donald Trump opposes strict regulation and said in September that the US government would rename the technology “ super intelligence ” in official communications. During Huang’s European tour, Nvidia pledged nearly $10 billion in investments in the continent’s tech sector and urged Europe, which is lagging behind in the AI race, to move faster.

title: Lockheed, US Pentagon strike initial deal to produce 850 F-35 jets
description: Lockheed Martin has entered an initial production and sustainment agreement with the United States Department of Defence for at least 850 F-35 Lightning II fighter jets over the next 10 years, they said on Thursday. The defence contractor will self-fund at least $7 billion in initiatives that support the F-35 programme, the department said in a statement. The F-35, built with stealth technology that allows it to evade enemy detection, is considered the world’s most advanced fighter jet and is at the core of Lockheed’s aeronautics division that forms close to 40 per cent of its quarterly revenue. Under the agreement with the Department of Defence, which US President Donald Trump calls the Department of War , Lockheed aims to maintain annual production at 156 aircraft. The agreement does not constitute an order but is counted as a prearranged long-term contract. “If granted multi-year authority in the coming months, the F-35 Joint Programme Office and Lockheed Martin will work to finalise contract terms, pricing and schedules through a formal contract award,” the company said. The agreement also covers international orders for the F-35, as well as initial spares and modification kits, Arlington-based Lockheed said in a statement. “We have fundamentally changed how we stabilise the American defence industrial base to produce at speed and scale,” said Under-Secretary of Defence Michael Duffey. “This agreement with Lockheed Martin proves it. By aligning financial incentives with actual performance, we are ensuring our warfighters are equipped with the lethal capabilities they need to fight and win.” Lockheed and its peers across the US have benefited from increased global defence spending as geopolitical conflicts remain unabated. Lockheed estimates the agreement will support 317,000 US jobs and generate nearly $79bn in annual economic activity over the next decade. It also expects the arrangement to lower production costs and ease supply-chain constraints from raw materials to finished parts.

title: Australian fast bowler Megan Schutt suspended over medication breach
description: Star Australian fast bowler Megan Schutt was suspended for two matches on Thursday for breaching prescription medication rules. The 33-year-old, who was a standout in Australia’s recent one-day series against Bangladesh, apologised for “failing to meet the standards” expected of her. Cricket Australia said in a statement she breached “requirements under the Sports Science and Sports Medicine guidelines with regard to prescription medication”. “This relates to a single incidence which occurred while out of competition and was not for performance enhancing purposes,” it added. “We will continue to provide appropriate support to Megan and reinforce the standards and responsibilities expected of everyone representing our game.” Her two-match ban will see Schutt miss Thursday’s third and final T20 against New Zealand and the Adelaide Strikers’ opening game of the Women’s Big Bash League later this month. “I fully accept the penalty handed down and apologise for failing to meet the standards expected of me,” said Schutt, who has played 114 ODIs and 126 T20s for Australia. “I’m sorry for the attention this has caused and appreciate the support I’ve received.”

title: Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticised manager Michael Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes is the latest United player to publicly break ranks. Defender Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid last week. Martinez said Carrick had been left with an understrength squad. He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.”

title: Verstappen bids to delay Antonelli's F1 coronation in US
description: Max Verstappen is set to be a party-pooper this weekend as he seeks to delay Kimi Antonelli’s title celebrations by notching a third consecutive win with another triumph at the United States Grand Prix. Red Bull’s four-time world champion won both the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and then the Singapore Grand Prix to emerge as a leading contender for more success just when Mercedes’ precocious 20-year-old Italian moved within reach of the title. The 29-year-old Dutchman, who has acknowledged Antonelli’s generational talent, won from pole at the Circuit of the Americas last year and is chasing a fifth win at the Texan track where Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton was won five times. But Verstappen has been reluctant to claim that Red Bull’s recovery in form and results will automatically translate to more success. “It’s difficult to say - I don’t want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin,” he said after his Singapore win. “But the last few weekends have been great. I just take it race by race and we’ll see how it goes there. It’s another very different kind of track.” After a run of seven podium finishes in his last eight races, including two wins and three second places, Verstappen, 119 points adrift in fourth, may well scupper hopes that Antonelli can win and, with the stars aligning, become Italy’s first champion since 1953 and the youngest in F1 history. Title within reach To seize the title in Texas, the Italian, who leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 102 points, needs to win the race and see Russell fail to finish in the top nine and Hamilton outside the top four. Antonelli was only four years old when Sebastian Vettel took the record as youngest champion, with Red Bull, in 2010, and he knows he must stay focused and race to win, as he always does. “I know it’s very close and I know it’s there, but I need to make sure I keep doing my best and go out and win and perform in my best way,” he said. Italy’s last champion was Alberto Ascari for Ferrari. McLaren’s deputy team principal Bradley Lord drew upon tennis when he described Antonelli’s position by saying: “We’re in that uncomfortable phase where you have to navigate the media with everyone saying ‘you can do it - you’ve got first match point.” Russell’s hopes of reining in Antonelli may be aided by Verstappen while Hamilton could also be a threat as he returns to one of his favourite circuits seeking a record sixth win and seventh in the United States GP. Both Mercedes drivers will run the team’s latest updates package as they go into a decisive triple-header of races in Texas, Mexico and Brazil, but it may be that Ferrari and Red Bull can steal the initiative. These races may be run on bumpy tracks and in hot conditions that deliver unexpected results, a prospect that Verstappen has anticipated. “From what I saw in the world endurance championship race in Austin, the track is incredibly bumpy and I will probably need to order a new spine after the weekend - or become like Robocop. It’s crazy.”

title: Wrong anthems played at Asian Para Games after mishap-marred Asian Games
description: Wrong national anthems were played three times at the Asian Para Games in Japan’s Nagoya this week, prompting the mayor to apologise just days after the city hosted the mishap-plagued Asian Games. The Asian Para Games is taking place in the central Japanese hub city through Saturday, featuring around 4,000 athletes and officials in 18 sports. Nagoya Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa apologised on Wednesday for the latest error, which occurred despite officials’ pledges to implement steps to prevent mistakes, including playing the correct national anthems. “These things happened during the Asian Games, so of course the operations were reviewed and examined based on the lessons learned. The fact that it happened again is really just unacceptable,” the mayor told a press conference. On Monday, a Taiwanese athlete won a men’s para taekwondo competition, but the Iranian anthem was played in its entirety, according to Nagoya officials at the mayor’s press conference. Officials realised their mistake after the ceremony, they said. On the same day, the Iranian anthem was played again during a women’s para taekwondo ceremony, where a Mongolian competitor was receiving the gold medal, according to the city. The incorrect music was stopped after the Mongolian delegation pointed out the error. Organisers then played the Mongolian anthem after the music was provided by the delegation, Nagoya officials said. Separately on Monday, officials broadcast the South Korean anthem for about five seconds, instead of the Chinese one, before a sitting volleyball match between China and Iran. “It is unacceptable, or rather, it’s painful. I am very sorry about it,” the mayor said, adding that he felt the tournament was otherwise progressing smoothly. The Asian Games, which concluded in early October, faced heavy criticism for shortcomings ranging from inadequate accomodations for athletes to the playing of wrong national anthems. On September 18, organisers played North Korea’s national anthem for the South Korean hockey team.

title: Kharmang celebrates colour, taste and aroma of Suspolo apples
description: GILGIT: The vibrant colours, sweet taste and captivating aroma of indigenous Suspolo apples took centre stage at the 7th National Suspolo Festival 2026, held in Pari Valley of Kharmang district, celebrating the region’s unique agricultural heritage and hardworking farmers. Organised by the district administration with the support of the Gilgit-Baltistan Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries Department, the festival brought together Governor Mehdi Shah, Forests Minister Raja Nasir Ali Khan, locals and domestic and foreign tourists. Suspolo, a distinctive apple variety grown in Pari, has gained popularity for its juicy sweetness, vibrant colour and powerful fragrance. Locals say its aroma can fill an entire room, while the fruit can be preserved until March. Speaking to Dawn , Deputy Commissioner Kharmang Nisar Ahmed Khan said the annual festival, held during the harvest season for the past seven years, aims to promote the indigenous apple, showcase local culture and help farmers find better markets for their produce. Colourful stalls featuring Suspolo apples, homemade delicacies, traditional foods and locally produced goods attracted visitors. Students added to the festive atmosphere with cultural performances, while women and local entrepreneurs found opportunities to showcase their products. For stallholder Akbar Ali, bringing apples from remote areas remains a challenge, with some villages lacking proper road access. Growers say improved transport, market access and government incentives could help expand production and open doors to international markets. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Islamabad High Court seeks evidence against NAB officials’ appointments
description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Wednesday issued notices to the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), the Ministry of Law and other respondents on a petition challenging the appointments of the bureau’s Deputy Chairman Ihtesham Qadir Shah and Prosecutor General Sohail Nasir, while directing the petitioner to produce documentary evidence that the two did not meet the legal requirements for their posts. Justice Umair Majid Malik, who heard the petition filed by Advocate Dr G.M. Chaudhry, observed that the petitioner had “completely ruined the entire case” after he argued that Mr Nasir had improperly described himself as a former judge despite having served only as an additional judge of the Lahore High Court (LHC). Justice Malik remarked with a smile, “In that case, you might as well remove our badges too, as we are also currently serving as additional judges.” ‘Lack qualifications’ In his petition, filed in the nature of quo warranto, Dr Chaudhry challenged the appointments of the NAB deputy chairman and prosecutor general, arguing that Mr Shah did not meet the qualifications prescribed under Section 7(aa) of the National Accountability Ordinance (NAO), 1999. The petitioner contended that Mr Shah had previously served as NAB prosecutor general, a position that did not qualify him as a federal government officer in Grade 21 or its equivalent. He also argued that Mr Shah was neither an armed forces officer holding the rank of major general nor its equivalent. Regarding Mr Nasir, the petitioner argued that he did not meet the criteria under Section 8(a) of the NAO, which requires a NAB prosecutor general to be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge. He said Mr Nasir had served as a sessions judge before being appointed an additional judge of the LHC, but was not confirmed. The petitioner maintained that he therefore did not meet the requirements under Article 177(2) of the Constitution. Notices were also issued on miscellaneous applications seeking to restrain the NAB deputy chairman and prosecutor general from performing their duties and to summon the records of their appointments. title: Over 670 govt schools in Bannu lack basic facilities
description: BANNU: Government schools across Bannu district require an estimated Rs4.509 billion to address infrastructure deficiencies and provide essential facilities, according to official data. The data gathered from the district education office identified 711 classrooms in need of repairs across 672 government schools, while 209 schools require washrooms. Boundary walls at 33 schools have also been identified as damaged or missing, making their construction or rehabilitation necessary. As per the school-level infrastructure assessment and estimated financial requirements, primary schools accounted for the largest share of the deficiencies, with 585 institutions requiring more than Rs3.72 billion to address their infrastructure needs. The data provided details of requirements and estimated costs by school category, tehsil and subdivision. Official data shows Rs4.5bn needed to improve infrastructure The findings highlighted the urgent need for investment in school infrastructure, as dilapidated classrooms, inadequate sanitation facilities and missing or damaged boundary walls directly affect the learning environment, students’ comfort and their safety. According to the figures, 630 classrooms in 585 primary schools required repairs, while 188 washrooms and 22 boundary walls needed to be constructed or rehabilitated. The estimated cost of addressing these deficiencies stands at Rs3.720 billion, accounting for approximately 82.5pc of the total funding requirement. At the middle-school level, 35 institutions require repairs to 12 classrooms, seven washrooms and five boundary walls. The estimated cost of meeting these needs is Rs342.95 million. The assessment identifies 39 high schools requiring repairs to 59 classrooms, along with 11 washrooms and five boundary walls. The estimated expenditure for these works is Rs394.52 million. Meanwhile, 13 higher secondary schools require repairs to 10 classrooms, three washrooms and one boundary wall. The estimated cost of these interventions is Rs51.56 million. Bannu tehsil has 417 government schools, where 227 classrooms require repairs. The area also needs 158 washrooms and the construction or rehabilitation of 33 boundary walls. All 33 boundary-wall requirements recorded in the district fall within Bannu tehsil. In Wazir subdivision, 250 classrooms across 108 schools have been identified as needing repairs, while 32 washrooms are required. No boundary-wall requirements have been recorded for the subdivision. Miryan tehsil has 56 schools, with 99 classrooms requiring repairs and 11 washrooms needed. In Domel tehsil, 49 classrooms across 42 schools need repairs, while four washrooms are required. In Kaki tehsil, 60 classrooms across 30 schools require repairs. However, the report records no additional requirements for washrooms or boundary walls in the tehsil. Similarly, 16 schools in Bakakhel tehsil require repairs to 26 classrooms and the construction of four washrooms. The need to repair 250 classrooms in Wazir subdivision and provide 158 washrooms in Bannu tehsil stands out among the identified deficiencies. The estimated funding requirement of more than Rs4.5 billion highlights the need for the relevant education authorities and the provincial government to prioritise school infrastructure in development planning and allocate resources to address the most pressing needs. MNA SHIFTED TO HARIPUR JAIL: Deputy Commissioner Zia-ur-Rehman ordered the detention of MNA Maulana Syed Naseem Ali Shah for 30 days at Haripur Central Jail over allegations of inciting illegal protests, blocking roads and obstructing the performance of official duties, citing concerns over the maintenance of public order. According to the detention order, a report was submitted by the district police officer on Oct 19, alleging that Mr Shah, a resident of Ghoriwala, Bannu, was involved in activities described by the authorities as anti-state and had been encouraging residents to participate in illegal protests. The order stated that the alleged activities could lead to the closure of public roads and deliberate obstruction of government officials in the discharge of their duties, potentially disrupting peace and public order in the district. The order further stated that the detention period will commence from the time of his arrest and placement in custody, unless the order is withdrawn earlier. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Bannu remains polio hotspot, warn experts
description: PESHAWAR: Experts have warned that Bannu Division is a major concern for global polio eradication efforts alongside Afghanistan. The warning comes as authorities prepare to launch a fractional inactivated polio vaccine (fIPV) campaign following confirmation of the virus in a 10-year-old boy in Khyber tribal district. The drive slated to cover the two districts will begin on Nov 2, according to officials. They said since 1988, when around 350,000 polio cases were reported worldwide annually, the virus had been eliminated from 125 countries, leaving Pakistan and Afghanistan as the only countries where it remains endemic. Fractional inactivated polio vaccine drive to be launched They said the latest case reported in Khyber district was the fifth in the province and the seventh in Pakistan this year. The officials said the affected child, aged 10, had apparently completed the routine immunisation course but no record of vaccination was available. World Health Organisation member Dr Sardar Alam sought the media’s support in building community trust and addressing misconceptions about vaccine acceptance. He said all 49 polio cases reported globally this year so far had been recorded in Pakistan and Afghanistan, with seven and 42 cases, respectively. Dr Alam said poliovirus had been detected in 24 children aged over 60 months across 14 districts, including Khyber and Peshawar. He added that children above five years accounted for five of the 31 polio cases reported in Peshawar in 2025, representing 17pc of the total. Presenting an overview of the province’s polio situation, Dr Alam outlined the major challenges to eradication and stressed the need for sustained vaccination campaigns and collective efforts to protect every child. He said children above five years could lose immunity, allowing the virus to continue circulating. A booster fIPV dose for children aged four months to 10 years was important to strengthen their immunity and reduce transmission within this age group, he added. The WHO member said such interventions were introduced on the advice of the Technical Advisory Board after technical analysis to determine the appropriate age groups and timing of vaccination. Jahanuddin, a social and behaviour change specialist at Unicef, stressed the importance of understanding community perceptions, addressing misconceptions, building trust and encouraging positive attitudes towards polio vaccination and essential immunisation. Unicef communication officer Shadab Younas highlighted the importance of accurate health reporting in protecting and improving public health and urged media organisations to address vaccine hesitancy through human-interest stories, documentaries and the use of neutral, trusted voices to help change public perceptions. PPC vice-president Ziaul Haq said media collaboration was essential to generate demand for vaccines and protect children until polio was eradicated. He said the media supported efforts to counter misinformation and communicate accurate information about vaccination, adding that effective cooperation between journalists and health organisations was necessary to secure a healthier future. Emergency Operations Centre coordinator Sarah Rehman said polio was a preventable but crippling childhood disease, so parents should ensure vaccination of their children during every campaign. She said the administrative machinery, law-enforcement agencies and health department officials were actively involved in eradication efforts but the government could not overcome the challenge alone. “There is a need for support from all segments of society, including the media,” she said. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Peshawar High Court seeks govt response to petitions about school collapse
description: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Wednesday directed the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government and relevant officials to respond to petitions seeking a transparent inquiry into the recent Peshawar school building collapse and compensation for the victims’ families under the Shuhada Package. A bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Farah Jamshed directed the respondents, including the chief secretary and several administrative secretaries, to submit their comments about the pleas within a fortnight. The court was hearing two petitions filed by the Peshawar High Court Bar Association (PHCBA) and lawyer Usman Alam, who asked it to declare that the respondents’ failure to ensure the safety of the school building and protect students’ lives violated various constitutional provisions. The petitioners sought orders for the immediate provision of compensation and benefits equivalent to the Shuhada Package to the legal heirs of every deceased student, along with free medical treatment and appropriate compensation for the injured students. They also called for the formation of a judicial commission within a timeframe set by the court to determine the cause of the building collapse, fix responsibility on officials, owners and school management and produce its findings. The petitioners also sought a province-wide structural, fire-safety and building-compliance audit of all public and private schools by qualified engineers and fire-safety experts and requested the court to direct authorities to submit a comprehensive report identifying unsafe buildings and highlighting corrective measures taken to date. They also sought orders for the formulation, notification and strict enforcement of the Safe Schools Policy and mandatory minimum standards for school buildings, including seismic resistance, fire exits, firefighting equipment, evacuation drills and periodic third-party inspections. PHCBA President Aminur Rehman Yousafzai and lawyer Fawad Jan appeared on behalf of the petitioners and told the court that the building of a private school, Al-Khair Education System, near Ring Road collapsed on Oct 15, killing 31 students and a teacher. They said the incident required an investigation to determine responsibility, review the roles of the relevant institutions and introduce effective measures to protect children in educational institutions. The counsel alleged that negligence by authorities led to the tragedy as an effective check and balance didn’t exist for monitoring buildings of private schools in the province. They also alleged that unregistered schools were operating in streets and neighbourhoods without effective regulatory oversight. Mr Yousafzai said some private schools operated in rented buildings, so effective measures were required to ensure structurally safe premises and a secure learning environment. He said the school building collapse had shaken the province and the country. Citing information available in public reports, the petitioners claimed that the school building was not constructed or maintained according to approved plans, structural standards, fire-safety requirements and emergency exit regulations. They questioned whether the school had valid registration, building approval and safety certification, claiming that deficiencies were properly flagged in the past. The counsel argued that the tragedy pointed to broader weaknesses in the regulatory framework governing school registration and inspection, approval and monitoring of building plans, land-use compliance and administrative oversight. They also complained that authorities hadn’t announced adequate compensation for the bereaved families, while no independent, transparent inquiry had been made public by the time the petitions were filed. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: 17 sugar mill workers abducted in DI Khan
description: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Seventeen employees of a sugar mills were reportedly abducted here after armed men intercepted their bus on the Indus Highway in the early hours of Wednesday, police said. According to police, the incident took place in the Prova area, where around 15 to 20 armed men had reportedly set up a roadblock and stopped the bus carrying employees returning from the night shift. The attackers checked the identity cards of the passengers before taking 17 employees with them, police said. Most of those abducted were reportedly security personnel. Police said the incident was reported at around 1am. Initial information suggested that the incident was linked to a dispute over extortion demands, while police were investigating the circumstances surrounding the abductions. Following the incident, police cordoned off the area and launched efforts to trace and recover the abducted employees. Contingents of the army were also dispatched from Dera Ismail Khan to assist the police in the recovery operation. Further details about the identity of the attackers and the whereabouts of the abducted employees were not immediately available. Meanwhile, relatives of kidnapped employees blocked the Indus Highway at Chowdhwan Morr to demand the immediate recovery of the hostages. The protest disrupted traffic on the highway, with long queues of vehicles on both sides, causing inconvenience to commuters. The protesters demanded that the authorities intensify efforts to recover the abducted employees. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Five men charged with PPP UC chairman’s murder in Karachi's Orangi Town acquitted
description: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Wednesday acquitted five accused allegedly involved in killing of a union committee (UC) chairman belonging to the Pakistan Peoples Party in Orangi Town. The UC chairman, Amir Bhashani, was gunned down on April 17, 2025 by armed motorcyclists in a suspected targeted attack near Bismillah Chowk in Orangi Town. The case was registered under terrorism and murder charges by the Pakistan Bazaar police. Later, the police claimed to have arrested Shehzad, Muhammad Aleem, Muhammad Jameel Zia, Muhammad Hammad Siddiqui and Shahbaz and submitted a charge sheet against them. After hearing arguments of state prosecutor and defence counsel Abid Zaman and Hyder Farooq Jatoi, the ATC-VI judge acquitted the accused persons for lack of evidence against them. According to the prosecution, the accused Shahbaz and Shehzad were arrested in an illegal weapon possession case and during interrogation, they had allegedly confessed to their involvement in the murder of the UC chairman. In their alleged confessional statements to the police, they implicated the other accused, claiming that, at the instigation of their elders, they had conducted recce of the deceased and provided information to their accomplices. The police had earlier claimed that the murder was planned a week before the killing over “land and financial matters”. A case was registered at the Pakistan Bazar under Sections 302 (premeditated murder) and 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code read with Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act of 1997. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Rawalpindi lawyers boycott courts over FIR against advocate for ‘assaulting’ judge
description: RAWALPINDI: The contents of a sealed first information report (FIR) registered against an advocate for allegedly hitting a civil judge with a glass, injuring his head and fingers, in his chamber at the judicial complex on Tuesday have emerged. Protesting against the registration of the FIR against the advocate, the Rawalpindi Bar Association boycotted court proceedings and staged a protest at the judicial complex on Wednesday. The FIR was registered under eight sections of the law, including Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA), Section 506(ii) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) for issuing threats of dire consequences, Section 353 PPC for using criminal force against a public servant or deterring him from performing his lawful duties, Section 324 PPC for attempting to commit intentional murder (qatl-i-amd), and Sections 186, 147 and 149 PPC. Syed Tahir Abbas Shah, reader to the court of Malik Ali Miran, Civil Judge Class I, lodged a complaint with the Civil Lines police, stating that he was sitting in his office and attending to court work when advocate Muhammad Aslam Khan Niazi, accompanied by advocate Muhammad Farooq Aslam Khan and seven other lawyers, entered the courtroom and tried to force their way into the judge’s chamber. Their actions were visible in the CCTV footage, he said. He said he tried to stop them from entering the judge’s chamber, but Muhammad Aslam Khan Niazi and Muhammad Farooq Aslam Khan started verbally abusing him and scuffling with him before forcibly entering the chamber. He added that he and other court staff members followed them into the chamber. Once inside, Mr Niazi allegedly used abusive language against the civil judge and shouted at him, questioning why the application against them had been entertained. According to the FIR, the judge calmly replied that the application had been decided purely on merit and that the case file had been forwarded to the ahlmand (court record room). “If you are still not satisfied with the court’s decision, you can file an appeal in accordance with the law,” the complainant quoted the judge as saying. The FIR stated that, in response, the advocate threatened the judge with dire consequences, picked up a glass from the table and struck him above the eye with the intention of killing him, injuring the judge. The complainant further stated that advocate Muhammad Farooq also picked up a piece of the broken glass, pointed it at the judge, threatened to kill him and started assaulting him. When the judge tried to stop him with his right hand, he sustained injuries to his fingers, the complaint said. The complainant added that when he and other court staff members tried to rescue the judge, Muhammad Farooq Aslam Khan and his companions assaulted him, causing him to fall to the ground. The FIR further stated that the two advocates and their colleagues threatened the judge with dire consequences and warned him that they would see how he would sit in court in the future. The incident created panic and fear among judges, court staff and members of the public, the complainant said. He added that the incident was motivated by the previous day’s court decision regarding a stay order. The Civil Lines police registered the FIR against the advocates under eight sections of the law, including Section 7 of the ATA and Sections 353, 324, 506(ii), 186, 147 and 149 of the PPC. Meanwhile, lawyers protesting against the registration of the FIR staged a demonstration and took out a rally at the judicial complex on Wednesday, chanting slogans. The protesters forced litigants to leave courtrooms, as no lawyer appeared before any court on Wednesday. The protesters strongly condemned the registration of the FIR against a member of the Rawalpindi Bar Association and what they described as the police’s partial attitude. The district bar announced a complete strike for October 21, 2026. Meanwhile, efforts to reach a settlement were underway, sources said. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Japan-funded girls’ school inaugurated in Tarnol
description: ISLAMABAD: Akamatsu Shuichi, Ambassador of Japan to Pakistan, inaugurated the Tine Girls Model Primary School in Tarnol, Islamabad, built under a project implemented by a non-governmental organisation. The Government of Japan provided $44,025 in financial assistance for the project through its Grant Assistance for Grassroots Human Security Projects (GGP) programme. Officials of the Japanese embassy, CSP representatives, teachers, students, parents and community members attended the inauguration ceremony, according to a press release. CSP has completed the construction of the school, which comprises eight classrooms and other essential facilities, including a principal’s office, washrooms, a levelled playground and 250 student chairs. CSP also contributed additional resources to install a solar power system, an underground water storage tank with an electric water cooler, and an interactive smartboard for digital learning. Addressing the ceremony, Ambassador Akamatsu congratulated CSP on completing the project despite challenging weather conditions. He said education was not only a fundamental human right and a core pillar of human security but also the foundation of a better and more prosperous society. He added that girls’ education was particularly important for Pakistan’s future. This was why education remained a key priority of Japan’s development cooperation in Pakistan, he said. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: NAB seeks lowering of graft threshold to Rs50 million
description: ISLAMABAD: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) has urged the government to review the law under which the bureau could not take up corruption cases involving an amount of less than Rs500m. This was stated by NAB Chairman retired Lt Gen Nazir Ahmed Butt during a recent media interaction with other senior officials of the bureau. “We have demanded of the government to reduce this threshold to Rs50m so that NAB can lay its hands on individuals involved in mega corruption cases,” he said during the briefing arranged to inform the media about the recent successes of the accountability watchdog. The NAB chairman claimed to have recovered state land worth trillions of rupees from encroachers, including 235,622 kanals of Pakistan Railways (PR). Chairman says current Rs500m limit hampers action against corruption; Railways land worth Rs6.78tr recovered He said the bureau was also concentrating on the cases of money laundering, criticising Western countries for not investigating the source of money being invested by Pakistani diaspora in their countries. “We have learnt that more than 147,000 Pakistani students were staying abroad, with heavy fees being paid by their parents and no authority in the West asking them about the source of money,” Lt-Gen Nazir Ahmed Butt said. He further said a committee had been formed to address complaints from investors, who believed they were not receiving adequate protection. Recovery claims According to NAB’s Director General (Operation) Amjad Aulakh, the bureau had retrieved state land worth Rs9.18 trillion in the third quarter of the current year, bringing the total recovery of the bureau to Rs11.524 trillion since 2023. According to him, due to NAB’s sustained initiatives, the year 2026 has so far witnessed an aggregate recovery of valuable state lands and other assets worth Rs14.6 trillion. He further said the bureau distributed Rs908 million to 4,280 affected people through deposits in their bank accounts. He was of the view that after the recovery of 235,622 kanals of PR land, the organisation will soon become self-reliant and will be able to launch mega rail projects. According to the NAB chairman, the value of recovered PR land is Rs6.78tr. The recovery has been made at a time when the government was seeking foreign loans for executing the ML-1 project, under which an additional rail track will be laid from Karachi to Peshawar. The NAB chairman said after making a record recovery of PR land, the bureau’s next target was to unveil corruption in the power sector, Evacuee Trust Property Board, state-owned enterprises, mines and minerals. Secretary Railways Syed Mazhar Ali Shah while talking to Dawn confirmed that NAB had retrieved huge encroached land. He said a proper and foolproof procedure was being devised to sell recovered assets so that the money could be spent on future projects and upgradation of railways and its services. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Man sentenced to death for raping stepdaughter by Islamabad sessions court
description: ISLAMABAD: An additional district and sessions court has sentenced a man to death for sexually assaulting his stepdaughter over a period of about a year, resulting in the birth of a child, and ordered him to pay Rs3 million in compensation to the victim and the child. Judge Mohammad Sohail, who presided over a court dealing with gender-based violence cases, convicted Iftikhar Ahmed Khan under Section 376(1) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) and also imposed a fine of Rs500,000 on him. The death sentence is subject to confirmation by the Islamabad High Court (IHC), to which the trial court has referred the case. The convict will remain in Adiala Jail pending confirmation of the death sentence. In its written judgement, the court observed that the prosecution had established its case through the victim’s testimony, the DNA report and other corroborative evidence. The court noted that the victim’s statement was corroborated by medical evidence and the DNA findings, adding that the prosecution’s evidence was credible. The convict, however, denied having sexual relations with the victim. According to the judgement, the accused sexually assaulted his stepdaughter over approximately one year, leading to her pregnancy. The victim’s mother was employed and often left her alone at home for extended periods, during which the assaults took place. In her statement, the victim said she could not inform her mother or siblings about the assaults because she was afraid. The judgement stated that the last incident occurred on February 1, 2025, while the victim gave birth to a child on July 2, 2025. The case was registered with Shahzad Town police station on February 5, 2025, on the complaint of the victim’s mother. Besides sentencing him to death, the court imposed a fine of Rs500,000 on the convict, directing that failure to pay would result in an additional six months of imprisonment. The court also ordered him to pay Rs1 million in damages to the victim and Rs2 million in compensation to the child born as a result of the assault. According to the verdict, failure to pay the amount awarded to the victim would entail a further six months of imprisonment, while failure to pay the compensation awarded to the child would result in another six months behind bars. The court directed that the Rs2 million compensation awarded to the child be recovered from the convict’s assets. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Girl allegedly kidnapped, raped in Pindi
description: RAWALPINDI: A young girl was allegedly abducted by a man and raped in the limits of Westridge police area, police said on Wednesday. Father of the rape victim, a resident of Allabad, registered an FIR with the police saying that he had six children. He said his 17-year-old daughter who was under matric who also lives in the house narrated her ordeal when he returned home in the evening. He said that his daughter told him that a man trapped her and took her to his house and forcibly raped her. He said he left his house at 7am to earn his livelihood, while his daughter left her house at 7.15am. He said after he started searching for her for the whole day, she returned back to her house at 7.30pm and narrated her story. Police have registered an FIR under sections 376A and 376 for rape. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Crackdown on ‘ghost’ employees launched in Swat
description: SWAT: The Malakand division administration on Wednesday launched a crackdown on ‘ghost’ employees, unauthorised occupation of government property and politically influenced postings in Swat, with more than 400 employees reportedly marking attendance at their offices after years of absence. The Water and Sanitation Services Company, Swat, has dismissed 13 employees who failed to report for duty. The employees were reportedly recruited by MPAs over the past 13 years and had been drawing salaries while staying at home or working at the residences and hujras of lawmakers. Malakand division commissioner Iqbal Hussain has directed the anti-corruption establishment to investigate the matter and recover the public money paid to the employees found guilty of wrongdoing. In a separate development, the administration has retrieved a government bungalow in Swat that had reportedly been occupied by Kaleem Saeed, brother of former federal minister Murad Saeed, for several years. The bungalow, located on the premises of the tehsil municipal administration, was only a few steps away from Kaleem Saeed’s private residence. According to reports, the authorities had repeatedly asked him to vacate the government property, but the requests went unheeded. The administration eventually initiated legal proceedings and secured possession of the bungalow. Meanwhile, the Swat deputy commissioner has transferred another 22 patwaris (revenue officials) allegedly posted under political influence. The transferred officials included Asad Khan, Hazrat Khan, Jawad, Jawad Khan, Saeedullah, Rashid Ali, Hameedullah, Fazal Ghafoor Shah, Syed Sohail Ahmed, Haq Nawaz, Nasir Khan, Sajjad Ali, Abbas Khan, Faheem Khan, Arifullah, Ajmal Khan, Shah Faisal, Habibullah, Jamal Ahmed, Fawad Khan, Naimatullah Khan and Syed Hakeem Jan. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: ATC acquits three Muttahida activists in May 12 violence cases for want of evidence
description: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Wednesday acquitted three men associated with the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) in three identical cases related to the May 12, 2007 carnage for lack of evidence. At least 45 people were killed and dozens wounded when the MQM held a rally on the day the then deposed chief justice of Pakistan, Justice Iftikhar Mohammad Chaudhry, landed at the Karachi airport to address the Karachi Bar Association on May 12, 2007. Three men — Mirza Naseeb Baig, Umair Hussain and Raees-ud-din, aka Mama — were charged in three identical cases registered at the Ferozabad and Airport police stations for rioting and attacking buses carrying people to a rally in support of the then chief justice near Malir Halt, Baloch Colony and FTC on May 12. After hearing arguments and examining the record, the ATC-V judge, who conducted the trial at the Judicial Complex inside Central Prison, acquitted the three MQM-P workers as the prosecution failed to establish its case against them. Defence counsel says accused Mirza Naseeb and Raees Mama will remain behind bars as other cases against them are pending trial At the hearing, Umair appeared on bail, while the other two accused, Mirza and Raees, were produced from jail. The court directed the jail authorities to release them if they were not required in any other case. Speaking to Dawn, defence counsel Mushtaque Ahmed said Mirza and Raees would remain in jail as cases against them were still pending in court. He said he had argued before the court that the accused were innocent and had been falsely implicated in the cases by law enforcement agencies with mala fide intentions. He further contended that Raees was initially arrested at the Karachi airport and implicated in the cases at the behest of high-ups due to his “political affiliation”. He added that Umair was apprehended by the Rangers during an “operation against the MQM” and kept in their custody for 90 days before being handed over to the police, who subsequently booked him in other cases. The counsel argued that the police had only one piece of evidence against the accused persons, which was the statement recorded in custody of the co-accused, which he argued was inadmissible before the court. Three separate cases were registered at the Airport and the Ferozabad police stations under Sections 147 (punishment for rioting), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object), 324 (attempt to murder), 302 (premeditated murder), 427 (mischief causing damage to the amount of fifty rupees) and 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code read with Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Man flees after allegedly raping minor girl in Vehari
description: BAHAWALPUR: A man allegedly raped a minor girl in Suleman Town in the limits of Burewala Saddar police precincts in Vehari district on Wednesday. According to the police sources, the daughter of the complainant, Naeem, a resident of Suleman Town, was playing in the street when the suspect, who lived in the same locality, lured her to a deserted house, where he allegedly raped her. The suspect, after committing the crime, fled the scene. The girl, on returning home, informed her father about the incident, who reported the matter to Burewala Saddar police. The police have registered an FIR and begun investigation into the complaint. The sources say that the girl was referred to the Burewala THQ Hospital, for medico-legal examination and the report was awaited. MURDER CASE ‘SOLVED’: Gaggo Mandi police claimed to have solved the blind murder case of a young girl, who was allegedly killed for “honour” by her father and his accomplices at Chak 229/WB. According to SHO Hassan Aftab Kiani the police traced the suspect, who turned out to be the victim’s own father, with the help of geofencing. About the motive of the murder, the SHO says that the girl’s father suspected she was having an affair with someone, and he, along with his accomplices, killed her in the name of “honour.” Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: The Trump rally: a slice of 'Americana' politics, coming to an end
description: Young students attending their debut political gathering, longtime supporters coming since 2015, or curious onlookers witnessing a presidential spectacle, they all agree. As Donald Trump runs his final campaign, no one will be able to replace his rallies. “There’s a lot of Americana. There’s a lot of, you know, happy people,” a Trump fan named Bart told AFP of Tuesday night’s outdoor campaign event in Greenville, North Carolina. Trump has been barnstorming across multiple US states ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, with his party at serious risk of losing their majorities in Congress. Attendees cheer as US President Donald Trump leaves after speaking at a campaign rally at T. Ed Garrison Arena in Pendleton, South Carolina on October 21, 2026. —Reuters In this rural corner of the eastern United States, “we don’t have stuff like this happen very often,” said Bart, attending with his wife Courtney and their two children, ages 10 and 12. Bart, who declined to give his last name, walked past a “MAGA” souvenir stand and rows of red, white and blue bunting before finding his seat on an airport tarmac where the rally was held. It was a familiar feeling. He attended his first Trump campaign event in 2015.
