Iranian officials also raised concerns over the closure, while Field Marshal Munir told them that the border closure was temporary and due to technical reasons and that the crossings had reopened on Tuesday. Importantly, Iranian officials reportedly shared with the field marshal their response to a US proposal, reiterating that Tehran would not make concessions under pressure and that Washington must meet its conditions before trust could be restored. While there was no official word from Pakistan’s Foreign Office or Inter-Services Public Relations, Iranian media described the response as “clear, serious, and explicit”. An Iranian source said the visiting Pakistani army chief was told that “Iran has nothing new to say to the Americans” and it was for them to return to Islamabad Memorandum. Although not many details about President Pezeshkian’s meeting were released to media, in a post that was unrelated to his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, the president said that Iranians may endure hardship, but they will not surrender their land. Speaker Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir that the US could not regain Iran’s trust without fulfilling the seven conditions Tehran had presented during meetings in New York. He said Washington’s past actions, including what Iran considers a violation of the Islamabad understanding, had only deepened its distrust of the US administration. “Threats and military manoeuvres cannot influence the strategic decisions of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Mr Ghalibaf said, according to an Iranian account of the meeting, adding that it was now up to Washington to take the necessary steps to extricate itself from the conflict. Mr Rezaei, meanwhile, said Iran would not surrender its enriched nuclear material, describing it as a national asset intended for domestic use. He said Iranian officials were united in their view that negotiations could not proceed without steps by Washington to meet Tehran’s conditions. The inflexible Iranian response has thrown a challenge for Pakistan, which has sought to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran after an earlier diplomatic breakthrough failed to produce a lasting settlement. Islamabad brokered a ceasefire in April and hosted direct talks that led to the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June. The agreement outlined steps towards easing the conflict, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing economic and nuclear issues, but the process subsequently stalled after disagreements. Despite the breakdown of the peace process, Pakistan has continued to offer its good offices to both sides for preventing another round of fighting. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Trump urges Ukraine to make deal to end war with Russia
description: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump called upon Ukraine on Tuesday to make a deal to settle the war with Russia, saying Moscow wanted to end the conflict. “Ukraine has to want to settle this war,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. Trump suggested Moscow had the upper hand in the fight because “Russia is a big machine - they just keep grinding forward, and that’s what they’ve done. They’ve taken a very large piece of land”. Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff was in Oslo, Norway, on Tuesday for talks with Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky in the search for an end to the war. Witkoff will now travel to Moscow on Wednesday to brief Russian officials about the discussions in Oslo. US envoy Steve Witkoff meets Zelensky in Norway, will travel to Moscow today Zelensky travelled to Oslo in a bid to repair relations with Washington, which have sunk to new lows as Trump has courted Moscow. Earlier on Tuesday, Zelensky spoke by phone with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Zelensky said Ukraine was again receiving early warnings of Russian missile attacks. This followed complaints by Kyiv that Washington had stopped sharing intelligence about Russian air strikes. “Now it works, it’s great,” Zelensky said, adding he and Rubio had also discussed supplies of Patriot missile interceptors and the US-provided satellite-based Starlink system, which Kyiv earlier said did not work when mounted on fast-moving objects such as drones. Trump’s recent gestures toward Moscow, including a deal to buy Russian diesel and waiving new sanctions, have sparked bipartisan pushback in the US Congress and worry in European capitals. Zelensky said he expected to talk to Rubio again in 48 hours. He said he had discussed security guarantees for Ukraine in Oslo, including “Article 5-like” guarantees, referring to the Nato stipulation that an attack on one ally is an attack on all. “I am thankful to the American side that they underlined again that it will be strong,” he said. “There are different kinds of security guarantees which are in the paper, in the document, which Steve (Witkoff) will share with the Russians,” he said. “And we will hear his feedback one day after.” Zelensky reiterated that Ukraine hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting of leaders of Ukraine, Russia and the US. Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere said the Oslo meeting had been good and constructive. “Steve Witkoff will fly tomorrow to Saint Petersburg where he will be meeting the Russian leadership, and exchange ideas from this meeting and the proposals that have been worked on by European and American colleagues, and possibly pave the way for a meeting at leaders level,” Stoere said. “I think the (peace) process is back on track,” Finnish President Alexander Stubb told the news conference, in which Witkoff did not take part. Earlier the US envoy and Zelensky clasped one another in a hug as they went into the talks that Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner joined remotely. Request for Patriot interceptors The US has largely stopped providing weapons directly to Ukraine, but lets European countries buy US weaponry on Kyiv’s behalf under the “prioritised Ukraine requirements list” (PURL). It has also provided intelligence and technology that Europe cannot match. A source familiar with the matter said most weapons deliveries under PURL continued to flow, but US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has not approved Ukraine’s latest requests for Patriot interceptors. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: French PM accuses radicals of forging ‘insurrectionary plan’
description: PARIS/ROME: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Tuesday vowed a  “massive” police presence at fresh protests called for the coming weekend, as he faced criticism over the handling of recent street violence. The eurozone’s second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron. Facing angry lawmakers in parliament, Lecornu acknowledged th­­­­­­­­at the security response had fall­­en short and promised a stronger ap­­p­­­­r­­oach ahead of a new wave of protests. “The deployment for next Sat­u­­­rday will be massive,” Lecornu said. He accused ultra-left radical groups of forging an  “insurrectionary plan” that led to the riots, which erupted on the sidelines of nationwide protests over the cost of living. Images of clashes, mobs looting stores and public buildings set ablaze last weekend prompted several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France. Italy to send 500 troops to Milan after clashes French authorities on Monday announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities, and Lecornu said fresh curfews would be imposed on Tuesday where needed. The nighttime curfew in the capital, from 2100 GMT, applied to Republique square in the centre east and the Les Halles district in the centre that is full of shops. A ban on public gatherings was also ordered for the Champs-Elysees, near several public buildings, and at train stations. Paris police also ordered a temporary ban on people carrying cans or bottles of petrol or gas, after mobs set fire to government buildings and shops last weekend. Milan clashes Italy was on Tuesday preparing to send 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes as fuel price protests hit pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy. Some luxury brands have kept their shops shut in the centre of Italy’s fashion hub after looting and riots over the weekend by mostly young protesters that left dozens of police officers injured. The government is also considering a wider crackdown, including easing laws on detaining minors and measures to punish parents. Hun­dreds of protesters were detained during two days of clashes in Milan and more protests are expected. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the violent perpetrators were  “thugs who exploit demonstrations to spread chaos, attack those who guarantee security, and hold entire cities hostage.”  “To demonstrate is a right. To lay our cities to waste is not,” she wrote on X. Hard-right leader Meloni faces elections next year in which the state of the economy, security and immigration are likely to be the key issues. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Drone attack by Sudan’s army kills 53 in disputed region
description: KHARTOUM: A drone strike by the Sudanese army killed 53 people at a market in an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan, local authorities said on Tuesday, the latest in a wave of deadly attacks. Authorities in Abyei district said the strike hit Amiet market on Monday. They accused the army of launching 22 munitions during the attack, which also wounded at least 27 people. “The casualties comprise vulnerable civilian populations, including women, children, the elderly, local merchants, members of the host Ngok Dinka community, South Sudanese returnees, and Sudanese refugees who had sought sanctuary from the broader regional conflict,” the authorities said. The United Nations condemned the attacks in Abyei,  “where at least 28 civilians were killed at Amiet Market, with many injured and many unaccounted for,” spokesman Stephane Dujarric said, calling escalating drone strikes  “part of a deeply concerning pattern”. On Sunday and Monday, strikes across Sudan killed more than 100 people. The country is in the grips of a brutal war between the regular army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that began in April 2023. Abyei district is claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan, which split from its northern neighbour in 2011 following decades of conflict. Parts of the district are controlled by a faction of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), a splinter from the organisation that fought for Juba’s independence. Juba’s foreign ministry said it had summoned the Sudanese ambassador over the attack. It accused the Sudanese army of striking multiple locations within the market, which is used as a transit point for goods to areas controlled by the RSF. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Sikh referendum in Canada draws 23,000 votes, expands campaign against Modi
description: WASHINGTON: More than 23,000 votes were reportedly cast in Edmonton, Canada, on Sunday in a referendum-style exercise organized by Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), which seeks an independent Sikh homeland in India’s Punjab. Voting was extended beyond the scheduled closing time to accommodate people waiting in line, organizers said. Held on Oct 18 at the Alberta Legislature Grounds, the non-binding exercise was part of SFJ’s international campaign for Khalistan, an independent Sikh state. It had no official standing. The more consequential development was SFJ general counsel Gurpatwant Singh Pannun’s announcement of a three-pronged strategy to challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government: continue overseas referendums, support political and youth movements opposing the government inside India, and press foreign investors to withdraw from Indian markets. Describing the initiative as “Fifth-Generation Warfare,” Pannun declared that “toppling Modi’s regime” was his immediate political objective. “Toppling Modi’s regime is a step forward” in SFJ’s struggle, he said, adding, “Our struggle continues.” Pannun, a US-based lawyer and prominent advocate of Sikh separatism, is a dual US-Canadian citizen. India designated him an individual terrorist in 2020 and has banned SFJ under its anti-terrorism law. He has also been the target of an alleged assassination plot in the United States. In February 2026, Indian national Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty in a US court to charges connected with a plot to murder a US citizen at the direction of an Indian government employee, according to the US Justice Department. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Meta’s board signals ‘recurring’ failures in oversight of election content
description: PARIS: The oversight board for social media giant Meta said on Tuesday it found “recurrent enforcement failures” in content moderation related to the US midterm elections and Brazil’s presidential election. The identified failures were often cases of “over-enforcement that suppresses political speech, and under-enforcement that undermines electoral integrity,” said the board, which independently checks moderation on Meta’s Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook platforms. Social media is a go-to source of electoral information for many voters, raising fears in several countries that it could swing results in favour of certain interests. Meta’s oversight board, in a statement, noted “the removal of political activist accounts during protests in the US ahead of the midterm elections” and “technical restrictions that hit the accounts of a presidential candidate in Brazil leading to allegations of electoral interference”. Global affairs officer Joel Kaplan to leave company after 15 years It added: “It’s clear that Meta must do more to ensure that its enforcement practices during elections are transparent and consistent, and that political speech is protected rather than stifled.” Brazil election controversy Brazil’s top electoral court on Monday gave Meta 24 hours to prove it is treating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his right-wing opponent Flavio Bolsonaro equally. The order came after Lula’s campaign alleged that Meta was suppressing his online content on Instagram and WhatsApp to boost Bolsonaro ahead of a runoff election round on Sunday. Meta has denied taking any actions to favour one side in Brazil’s election, but previously said that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors not isolated to Brazil. On Monday, the group run by billionaire Mark Zuckerberg apologised on X over another controversy in the United States. An Instagram account called “No Kings” — after citizen groups protesting what they saw as unconstitutional power grabs by President Donald Trump — was temporarily deactivated on Saturday. “We sincerely apologise,” Meta spokesman Andy Stone said on X, blaming “automated systems” for taking down accounts that had “very high frequencies” of posts, shares or comments. Meta’s oversight board reiterated a call for the company to fulfil its promises to make fewer moderation mistakes around elections and political debate. Joel Kaplan to leave company Meta Platforms’ chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan will leave the company next year after 15 years there, a spokesperson said on Tuesday. President and Vice Chairman Dina Powell McCormick will add external affairs to her portfolio, the spokesperson said. The move comes ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections. McCormick was part of the Donald Trump administration during his first stint as US president. Kaplan was elevated to Meta’s top policy role in January last year, as the social media giant rolled back US fact-checking, ended diversity initiatives and sought closer ties with Trump. A longtime Republican strategist, Kaplan served as deputy chief of staff for policy in the administration of George W. Bush. Meta is among the tech companies facing questions over AI’s impacts, as concerns mount over safety and the industry’s growing footprint among local communities. Trump recently said tech executives, including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, had agreed to establish voluntary AI standards. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Export sector warns of losing competitiveness
description: • Commerce minister admits pressure from energy, freight and tax costs • PHMA seeks reinstatement of EFS in its original form ISLAMABAD: As exporters warn of declining competitiveness, Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan on Wednesday acknowledged mounting pressures from rising energy, transport and freight costs, higher taxation and shifting global trade conditions. During a meeting, Mr Khan told leading exporters that the government was engaging directly with industry stakeholders to identify practical solutions through coordinated efforts involving relevant ministries and regulatory authorities. An official announcement said Mr Khan emphasised the need to diversify Pakistan’s export basket, promote value-added products, explore new international markets and remove structural barriers affecting exporters. Business representatives appreciated the Exim Bank scheme for exporters, calling it a positive initiative to improve access to export financing and support businesses seeking to expand internationally. However, they highlighted concerns about high energy costs, the captive power gas levy, provincial infrastructure levies, and rising production expenses. Petroleum Division officials clarified the gas levy mechanism. The exporters also discussed international shipping delays, port facilitation, tax refunds and banking regulations, and proposed greater flexibility in payment settlement periods due to disruptions in global logistics. During the meeting, representatives of the meat and livestock sector highlighted challenges relating to foot-and-mouth disease, international sanitary requirements, border restrictions and access to Gulf markets. The meeting was also informed of plans for a dedicated, private-sector-led livestock board. Mineral exporters raised concerns regarding restrictions on mining explosives and withholding taxes, while representative of surgical instruments sector emphasised the need for technological advancement, skilled human resources, industrial investment and modernisation to enhance Pakistan’s export competitiveness. FBR officials briefed participants on measures to improve tax refund processing and digital invoicing, while exporters highlighted difficulties relating to outstanding refunds, business visas and international compliance requirements. The meeting was also attended virtually by Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar, while State Minister for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, Coordinator Ihsaan Afzal Khan, secretaries of ministries concerned and senior officials from relevant departments participated. Most business representatives joined virtually, while others attended in person. Meanwhile, Central Chairman of the Pakistan Hosiery Manufacturers & Exporters Association (PHMA) Syed Zia Alamdar Hussain has urged the government to reinstate the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS) in its original form. However, the PHMA emphasised that the recent decline in exports must also be examined in the context of policy changes that have increased the cost of doing business and created serious cash flow challenges for textile exporters. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, ups high-speed diesel rate by Re0.31
World Bank to support Pakistani start-ups
description: ISLAMABAD: The Wor­ld Bank will help Pakistan mobilise private investment and broaden access to risk capital for innovative, high-growth firms. The “Pakistan Entrepr­eneurship and Private In­­v­­estment Catalyst Proj­ect”, expected to be app­roved by the World Bank Executive Board in early 2027, will help the government establish and capitalise a $50 million Fund of Funds (FoF) to catalyse Pakistan’s nascent innovation and venture capital ecosystem. The FoF will invest in professionally managed venture capital funds, helping expand the supply of early-stage and growth capital for innovative, high-growth firms, according to the project document made available to Dawn on Wednesday. By crowding in domestic and international private investors, the operation will address a long-standing mar­ket gap in innovation financing and strengthen the foundation of the country’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. Over time, the document says increased acc­ess to private capital is exp­ected to support firm gr­o­wth, innovation, productivity, and the creation of more and better-quality jobs. The operation has a national scope and, at the concept stage, no fixed geographic footprint. Paki­stan’s environmental and social context is therefore relevant to the anticipated FoF investment portfolio. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: NHA eyes public-private partnership model for roads
description: ISLAMABAD: The Nati­onal Highway Authority (NHA), Privatisation Com­m­­ission and Public-Private Partnership Authority (P3A) discussed on Wedne­sday the potential of developing four major road projects under the PPP model. The consultative meeting was co-chaired by Federal Minister for Communications Abdul Aleem Khan and Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatisation Muhammad Ali. During the session, participants evaluated the financial feasibility and commercial prospects of various highway networks for prospective private sector engagement. Among the proposals discussed, the 169-kilometre section of the M-10 Motorway was considered for execution under the Public-Private Partnership framework. The meeting also explored constructing the Mansehra-Naran-Jhal Khand-Chilas Motorway to link the route to the Chinese border. Mr Khan pointed out that the proposed Guru Nanak Expressway could play a vital role in facilitating religious tourism for the Sikh community, making it a strong candidate for development under the PPP model. He also highlighted that expanding the Murree Expressway to Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) could significantly boost tourism and trade across the region. To further assess these options, the minister directed NHA officials to prepare a formal business plan and bring forward market-ready projects. Citing the ongoing construction of the Sialkot-Kha­rian Motorway (M-12) under a public-private partnership as an existing model, the minister noted that NHA’s growing revenues reflect progress tow­ard financial self-reliance. He expressed his vision to transform NHA into a financially autonomous entity valued between Rs500bn and Rs1,000bn, thereby lessening reliance on federal PSDP funding. Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatisation Muhammad Ali assured full support and facilitation from the Privatisation Commission and P3A in evaluating these initiatives. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Cotton sector faces complete paralysis
description: LAHORE: The country’s cotton and ginning sector faces complete operational paralysis as factory owners threaten nationwide shutdowns and strikes after the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) conducted unannounced raids and record seizures in Sindh. The aggressive tax enforcement actions, carried out without prior notice in key cotton-producing hubs, including Sanghar, Tando Adam, and Shahdadpur, have triggered widespread panic across industry, forcing several ginning factories to abruptly halt production amid an already severe economic slump. Addressing a press conference at PCGA House in Multan, Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) Chairman Sohail Mehmood Harral, flanked by central leadership, warned that the business community would have no choice but to shut down all operating facilities if the harassment under the Regional Tax Office (RTO) Hyderabad jurisdiction is not halted immediately. Ginners protest unannounced FBR raids, record seizures in Sindh Expressing grave concerns, PCGA officials reported that tax authorities forcibly broke factory locks and confiscated financial records, bypassing legal notice procedures. Cotton Ginners Forum Chai­rman Ihsanul Haq confirmed that these heavy-handed tactics have sent shockwaves across bo­­th ginning and oil mill operations nationwide, threatening to derail the ongoing harvest season. The crackdown comes as the sector is already crippled by exorbitant electricity tariffs, rising production costs, and a crushing sales tax burden of 18 to 22 per cent. Industrialists pointed out that over 100 ginning factories have become non-functional in 2025-26 alone, bringing the cumulative total of closed facilities to over 500 ginning units, nearly 700 oil mills, 175 textile mills, and hundreds of power looms across Pakistan. While praising RTOs in Multan and Bahawalpur for choosing dialogue over coercive action, Mr Harral urged the government to replace raids with standard legal notices, giving mill owners a fair opportunity to comply without disrupting industrial activity. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Afghan trade halt hits pharma exports
description: KARACHI: After contracting by 30.26 per cent in FY26, the country’s pharmaceutical exports continued to decline, falling 25.53pc in value in the first quarter of 2026-27. The industry largely attributes the drop to disrupted trade with Afghanistan, once one of the country’s main medicine markets. Pakistan Bureau of Statistics data showed that pharmaceutical exports fell to $319.012m in FY26 from $457.456m in FY25, a drop of $138.444m, while export volumes declined 26.14pc to 83,104 tonnes from 112,517 tonnes. Pharmaceutical exports remained under pressure in the first quarter of FY27, with proceeds falling 25.53pc to $73.301m from $98.428m in the same period last year. Proceeds fall 25pc in 1QFY27 Export volumes fell 31.40pc in the first quarter of FY27, dropping from 23,924 tonnes to 16,410 tonnes, a reduction of 7,514 tonnes, showing a sharper decline in quantity than in value in both periods; average export value per tonne rose about 8.6pc in the first quarter, from around $4,115 to $4,469, but fell 5.6pc in FY26, from roughly $4,065 to $3,838, with these averages reflecting changes in the mix of products exported rather than necessarily changes in medicine prices. Exports of surgical goods and medical instruments, which are not included in these figures, rose 8.8pc to $121m in the first quarter of FY27 and remained unchanged at $451.527m for FY26. Afghanistan was once a major market for Pakistani medicines. Data on TDAP’s Pakistan Pharma Portal, sourced from PRAL, showed that Pakistan exported $155.68m worth of medicines to Afgh­anistan in FY25, accounting for about 34.1pc of the country’s total pharmaceutical exports of $457.456m that year. Former Pakistan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (PPMA) Chairman Tauqeer ul Haq said the suspension of trade with Afghanistan had caused heavy losses for pharmaceutical companies and the national exchequer. He added that Afghan patients were also suffering as they had to turn to more expensive medicines. He said the PPMA had raised the issue with the government, and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal had promised to discuss it with the relevant authorities and look for ways to restart Pakistani medicine exports. However, he said there had been little serious follow-up. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: Stocks stage mild recovery on selective buying
description: KARACHI: The Pakis­tan Stock Exchange (PSX) posted marginal gains on Wednesday before falling below the 165,000 mark as cautious trading continued amid persistent economic and political uncertainty. Topline Securities Ltd said the KSE-100 index staged a recovery, gaining 779.35 points, or 0.47 per cent, to close at 165,930.99 after two consecutive sessions of losses. The benchmark traded between an intraday low of 164,732 and a high of 166,242, with selective buying emerging at lower levels. The rebound reflected renewed buying interest following recent selling pressure. However, the recovery remained measured amid macroeconomic uncertainty, elevated international oil prices, and persistent geopolitical concerns. United Bank, Hub Power, Habib Bank, Oil and Gas Development Company and Mari Energies were the main contributors to the index’s gains, collectively adding approximately 493 points. Auto stocks lift market on draft policy optimism The auto sector remained the talk of the town, closing in positive territory amid optimism about the new draft Auto Policy 2026-31, which lifted investor interest in automotive stocks. Meanwhile, the refinery sector remained under earnings pressure after the government reduced the high-speed diesel crack spread from $41.89 to $38 per barrel for three months. Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd, said the market gained momentum amid renewed institutional buying, fuelled by optimism about intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict and expectations of easing geopolitical tensions. Additionally, the proposed five-year roadmap for the automotive sector aims to boost automotive exports to $6bn through tariff rationalisation, localisation and EV incentives. The draft also envisages export-linked incentives and stricter safety standards, subject to the requisite approvals, including IMF clearance. Despite a bullish trend, market activity weakened as trading volume dipped 14.98pc to 379.9 million shares. However, turnover rose 9.54pc to Rs21.2bn. Pakistan Refinery topped the volume chart with 49.4m shares. Analysts say institutional buying, optimism about US-Iran diplomacy and renewed interest in auto stocks may sustain the market’s positive momentum. However, geopolitical uncertainty and evolving macroeconomic risks could keep volatility elevated, favouring a selective investment approach. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

title: JI announces third wave of anti-levy protests across country on Friday
description: LAHORE: The Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) announced on Wednesday that it will launch the third phase of its nationwide protest movement against the petroleum levy on Friday, with sit-ins planned in all districts across the country, according to a press release by the party. The government currently levies Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. The Centre and JI had agreed to form committees in early September — when the latter had planned a nationwide strike — to recommend measures to reduce the levy. Wednesday’s press release by JI said the new phase of demonstrations would begin on the instructions of party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, and that the party’s clear and firm demand remained the complete abolition of the petroleum levy. JI claimed that the government had made no further contact regarding a planned meeting between Rehman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, which the latter had offered to hold. The press release recalled that Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and the PM’s adviser on political affairs, Rana Sanaullah, had contacted JI Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch to convey the premier’s message seeking a meeting. “Both sides had agreed that their respective committees would meet to work out a schedule for the proposed meeting,” it read, noting, however, that the government had made no further contact after that. The party stressed that Rehman had already clarified that the agenda of any meeting with the prime minister would be the abolition of the petroleum levy. “The JI emir has warned that if the government continues to delay action and refuses to provide relief to the public, the matter will be decided through street protests.” It added that the JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy would continue nationwide until its demand was met. On Aug 16, the JI announced sit-ins in all the provincial capitals of Pakistan against the petroleum levy and had called for a nationwide strike on Sept 3. On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government. However, on Sept 22, the JI emir said his party, whose convoy had reached Multan, was postponing its long march at the request of PM Shehbaz, pending a meeting with him.

title: Profit rates on National Savings schemes increased from Oct 21
description: ISLAMABAD: The government has increased profit rates on several national savings schemes, including those for pensioners, senior citizens and families of martyrs, with the revised rates taking effect from October 21. According to the revised schedule issued by the Central Directorate of National Savings (CDNS), the profit rate on Behbood Savings Certificates, Pensioners’ Benefit Accounts and Shuhada’s Family Welfare Accounts has been raised to 12.96 per cent from 12.72pc. The increase will raise the monthly profit on an investment of Rs100,000 under these schemes to Rs1,080 from Rs1,060. Similarly, the profit rate on Regular Income Certificates has been increased to 12.12pc from 11.76pc. The revised rate will provide a monthly return of Rs1,010 on an investment of Rs100,000, compared with Rs980 previously. The profit rate on Special Savings Certificates has been increased to 12pc from 11.6pc for the first five profit payments. Under the revised schedule, investors will receive Rs6,000 on an investment of Rs100,000 every six months, while the sixth and final profit payment will be Rs6,400 at a rate of 12.8pc. The government has also raised cumulative profit rates on Defence Savings Certificates across different maturity periods. For six-year certificates, the cumulative return has increased to 88pc from 86pc, while the seven-year return has risen to 113pc from 109pc. Similarly, the eight-year return has increased to 142pc from 136pc, while the nine-year return has been raised to 176pc from 168pc. The cumulative return on certificates held for 10 years has increased to 215pc from 205pc. Profit rates on Short Term Savings Certificates have also been revised upwards. The rate on three-month certificates has increased to 11.12pc from 10.80pc, while the revised schedule provides rates of up to 11.72pc for longer maturities. The government has also increased returns on Sharia-compliant savings schemes. Profit rates on Sarwa Islamic Term Accounts now range between 11.84pc and 12.12pc for different maturities, while the rate on Sarwa Islamic Savings Accounts has been raised to 11.84pc from 11.33pc. However, the profit rate on ordinary Savings Accounts has been maintained at 10pc per annum. According to the official schedule, profits on national savings schemes are subject to withholding tax at 15pc for filers and 30pc for non-filers, while Zakat deductions apply where prescribed under the relevant rules.

title: IMF urges Pakistan to move beyond fiscal targets
description: ISLAMABAD: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has called for Pakistan’s fiscal policy to go beyond achieving primary balance targets and protecting debt sustainability by reinforcing policy credibility, fostering economic recovery and creating space for public investment and social spending to support stronger long-term growth. Speaking at a workshop on “Reforms for a Modern and Growth-Friendly Tax System in Pakistan”, IMF Middle East and Central Asia Department Director Jihad Azour said tax refo­rm was critical to Pak­is­tan’s economic growth agenda and rema­ined central to the objectives of the Extended Fund Facility (EFF). The workshop was organised by the Ministry of Finance and Revenue in collaboration with the IMF. Finance Minister Muha­mmad Aurangzeb also spoke at the workshop, highlighting achiev­ements over the past two years. Mr Azour said Pakistan had made important progress towards restoring macroeconomic stability, rebuilding confidence, strengthening external buffers and supporting a gradual economic recovery despite an era of shocks and uncertainty. Jihad Azour calls for broader, more predictable tax system The IMF official said Pakistan’s recent stabilisation gains had created an opportunity that needed to be strengthened through transformative reforms, with tax reform at the heart of the process. “A stronger, broader, fairer and more predictable tax system can support fiscal sustainability while reducing distortions that hold back investment, productivity, growth and formal job creation,” he remarked. He said broadening the tax base, strengthening revenue administration, reducing tax expenditures, protecting priority spending and improving public service provision were Pakistan’s priorities. He credited Pakistan for the progress made. However, he said the next milestone was to turn stabilisation into stronger and more durable growth by moving beyond cycles of adjustment towa­r­ds a more competitive, inv­e­s­tment-friendly and inclusive economy. Mr Azour said the IMF remained committed to supporting the authorities in building an economy capable of delivering hig­her productivity, led by a stronger private sector, and creating better opportunities for younger generations. He warned that the highly uncertain external environment had made these objectives more urgent. Fiscal policy, he said, must do more than achieve primary balance targets and protect debt sustainability. It must reinforce policy credibility, foster recovery and create space for public investment and social spending needed to support long-term growth and public welfare. Outlining four themes for discussion during the two-day workshop, Mr Azour identified credibility, growth, fairness and implementation as central to the reform process. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: BYD to rely on imports initially, Hubco says
description: KARACHI: Hub Power Company (Hubco) has said that BYD vehicle production will initially rely entirely on imported raw materials and components, with localisation increasing gradually over time. The long-term objective is to localise up to 80 per cent of the vehicle, which should improve cost competitiveness and reduce reliance on imports, Hubco management said during a corporate briefing held on October 20, 2026. Topline Securities said the BYD plant is expected to commence operations within the next 4-5 weeks, by mid-December. The management is targeting an initial sales run rate of approximately 1,000-1,500 BYD vehicles per month as production ramps up. BYD plans to introduce additional models through a phased approach, focusing on segments that can generate meaningful sales volumes, the brokerage house said. According to Topline Securities, Lucky Cement told analysts on Tuesday that competition in the EV segment remains intense, particularly from Chinese completely built-up (CBU) vehicles. The company aims to begin local production of EV models by the first quarter of calendar year 2027, with volumes and model offerings expected to increase gradually in subsequent quarters. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Draft auto policy sent to cabinet
description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday approved the draft Auto Policy 2026-31, which aims to increase auto sector exports to $6 billion and boost local production, competitiveness and electric vehicle (EV) adoption. Although the Prime Minister’s Office did not issue an official statement, sources in the federal government shared the final draft, which was presented to the premier by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Adviser on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar. The draft policy will be presented to the federal cabinet for in-principle approval, then it will need parliament’s nod. The policy aims to bring the auto sector to open competition by significantly reducing tariffs on completely built-up units (CBUs) and completely knocked-down (CKD) kits up to 15pc by 2030-31. PM ‘okays’ five-year roadmap; policy targets $6bn exports, tariff cuts by 2031; proposes 1pc sales tax on EVs Under the proposed draft, battery electric vehicles will be subject to a 1pc sales tax during 2026-31. The document proposes a 6pc sales tax on range-extended electric vehicles and a 9pc on plug-in hybrid vehicles. A 10pc federal excise duty has been proposed on electric vehicles valued more than $75,000. The policy also envisages lower tariffs on smaller electric vehicles priced below $15,000. To encourage EV adoption, the government has approved proposals to raise the financing limit from Rs3 million to Rs10m and extend the repayment period from three to five years, making smaller vehicles more affordable for low-income consumers. The government has set the total export target of $6.01bn during the five years of the policy, which includes combined exports of parts and vehicles amounting to $256.6m for 2026-27, $671.8m for 2027-28, $1.11bn for 2028-29, $1.17bn for 2029-30 and $2.19bn for 2030-31 the fifth year of the auto policy. The policy also proposes mandatory export targets for vehicle manufacturers, with incentives for companies that increase exports. Under the proposed incentive mechanism, manufacturers would receive compensation equivalent to 5pc of export value for boosting exports, along with an additional 10pc incentive on exports exceeding the previous year’s level. Companies that fail to meet their export targets would face penalties, and manufacturing certificates could be cancelled if targets remain unmet for two consecutive years. The policy also sets new targets to increase the use of locally manufactured auto parts. Companies failing to meet local production targets could lose their incentives. The government expects to collect more than Rs232bn through the Automotive Development Levy over five years. The proceeds would be used to finance export incentives and industrial development programmes, including funding for technology upgrades by auto parts manufacturers. The policy proposes levying the Automotive Development Levy on vehicles with engine capacities exceeding 1,000cc. To strengthen quality assurance and regulatory oversight, the government plans to establish the Pakistan Automotive Testing Institute. The policy also provides funding for research, certification, and third-party audits, as well as the adoption of international safety standards for locally manufactured and imported vehicles. Meanwhile, Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (Paapam) Chairman Abdul Rehman Aizaz said the new policy, by lowering the import tariff on parts to 15pc, would phase out local parts manufacturers and benefit assemblers, warning that assemblers could eventually be phased out as imported cars take over.“This policy will make Pakistan an import destination country with no local industrial base in the auto sector,” he remarked. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Govt ups petrol price by Re0.88 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.53
description: The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Re0.88 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.53. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs382.02 per litre while HSD will cost Rs389.80 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 21 (Wednesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

title: LPG hits record Rs600 a kg amid shortages
description: ISLAMABAD: A serious shortfall, amid negligible supplies from Iran, has driven a record surge in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices in the country’s open markets, and the situation could worsen as winter approaches. LPG prices have surged to record levels in colder parts of the country, with prices reaching up to Rs600 per kg in hilly areas and Rs500 per kg in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Daily LPG consumption is around 4,000-4,500 tonnes, but it rises to 6,000-7,000 tonnes per day during peak winter. Incidentally, the official rate fixed by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) for October is Rs279 per kg, and the price of a domestic cylinder is set at Rs3,350. Domestic cylinder price surges to Rs7,200 from Rs3,350 Whereas, the price of a domestic LPG cylinder has reached Rs7,200 in hilly areas and Rs6,000 in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Demand surges not only in remote areas for heating and cooking but also in settled areas of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL) and in some parts of Sui Southern Gas Ltd, mainly due to gas load-shedding in the winter months. Pakistan produces between 2,000 and 2,500 tonnes of LPG daily, and an equal amount is both imported and smuggled from Iran. The recent surge in open-market prices is due to the sudden closure of all trading points with Iran. LPG Distributors Association Chairman Irfan Khokhar warned that prices could rise further in the coming days, adding to the financial burden on households that depend on LPG for cooking and heating. He accused Ogra of remaining a silent spectator to what he described as billions of rupees in overcharging, despite the significant gap between the regulated and prevailing market prices. “The entire situation stems from the regulator’s mismanagement and lack of oversight,” Mr Khokhar said. “While immediate LPG imports are needed to improve supply, Ogra must amend the required notifications and determine the basket price for both imported and locally produced LPG.” He said the price of local LPG was Rs279 per kg, while the average market price was around Rs450 per kg across the country. “The sellers were fleecing consumers with huge margins even on local LPG.” He added that Ogra should address the wide gap between official rates and market prices, and that the government should devise a mechanism similar to petrol and diesel, where locally produced and imported prices are balanced, so the price is determined by mixing local and imported LPG. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: PSX extends losses for second session
description: KARACHI: The Pakis­tan Stock Exchange (PSX) remained under selling pressure for the second straight session on Tuesday, as elevated oil prices stemming from the ongoing Middle East conflict and political instability following the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa continued to fuel uncertainty and doubts about macroeconomic stability amid an upward spiral in inflationary pressures. Topline Securities Ltd said the benchmark KSE-100 index extended its decline, shedding 814.44 points, or 0.49 per cent, to close at 165,151.64 amid cautious investor sentiment and lingering macroeconomic and geopolitical concerns. The benchmark remained volatile throughout the session, trading within an intraday range of 165,111–166,425, as selling pressure continued to weigh on overall market performance. Attock Refiner, Engro Holdings, Systems Ltd, Habib Bank, and Hub Power led the index’s decline, collectively dragging the benchmark down by about 348 points. Weakness in these key stocks further reinforced the prevailing bearish sentiment. Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd, noted that the market opened positively, reaching an intraday high of 166,426 before reversing and touching a low of 165,111. Index sheds 814 points amid oil, political concerns Rising international oil prices weighed on investor sentiment, prompting a cautious trading approach and pushing the index lower throughout the session. On the corporate front, Attock Group companies announced their 1QFY27 results. Pakistan Oilfield reported a profit after tax of Rs8.2bn (EPS: Rs28.86), up 51pc year-on-year, while Attock Petroleum’s earnings rose 74pc year-on-year to Rs6.64bn (EPS: Rs53.36), supported by higher petroleum prices, inventory gains and improved other income. Meanwhile, Attock Refinery reported a sharp 13-fold year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs18.6bn, up from Rs1.45bn in the same period last year. Market activity improved slightly, with trading volume rising 20.46pc to 446.84 million shares and total turnover slightly dipping 0.69pc to Rs19.3bn. Cnergyico PK topped the volume chart with 46.5m shares. Analysts say the market may remain volatile amid rising oil prices and political uncertainty. Cautious sentiment and selective buying could support a recovery, while investors should prioritise fundamentally strong stocks and monitor geopolitical developments. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: Fertiliser availability for Rabi reviewed
description: ISLAMABAD: The Ministry of National Food Security and Research has expressed its satisfaction with the overall fertiliser supply situation nationwide. The Fertiliser Review Committee meeting, chaired by National Food Security Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain, assessed fertiliser availability, market prices, distribution arrangements, and supply requirements for the ongoing Rabi cropping season on Tuesday. The minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to maintaining sufficient stocks to meet farmers’ requirements throughout the Rabi season. He said the government was fully committed to ensuring fertiliser availability, discouraging market exploitation, and supporting farmers during the Rabi season. Official statistics estimate urea consumption during Rabi 2026-27 at around 3,596,000 tonnes based on provincial demand, up from 3,563,000 tonnes in the previous Rabi. DAP offtake is projected at around 838,000 tonnes based on the last five-year average, up 0.4 per cent from Rabi 2025-26. Total fertiliser offtake during Rabi 2026-27 is expected to rise 0.8 per cent from the previous season. Total urea availability during Rabi 2026-27 is estimated at 3,950,000 tonnes, comprising 765,000 tonnes of opening balance and 3,185,000 tonnes of domestic production. Urea offtake is expected to be around 3,596 thousand tonnes. Total DAP availability will be 766,000 tonnes against expected offtake of 838,000 tonnes. Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

title: At SCO, Dar calls for promoting use of national currencies to help offset global economic shocks
description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday encouraged members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to use national currencies for “mutual settlement” and establish other financial mechanisms to “offset international financial shocks”. He made the remarks while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting in Tajikistan’s capital Dushanbe, where he arrived a day earlier. The SCO comprises 10 member states, namely Pakistan, China, India, Iran, Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The two observer states are Afghanistan and Mongolia. The CHG is the SCO’s second-highest decision-making body and provides guidance on economic, financial, trade, connectivity and socio-economic cooperation, as well as the organisation’s budgetary matters. Addressing the SCO meeting, Dar highlighted the “need to accelerate efforts to promote the use of national currencies for mutual settlement”, as well as to establish the SCO Development Bank, SCO Development Fund and SCO Investment Fund. “Such tools are measures which will advance development initiatives and help the SCO region to offset international financial shocks,” the former finance minister noted. Dar reiterated his call to accelerate local currency settlements in a later address to an expanded-format session of the meeting. Two members of the SCO, Russia and Iran, face Western sanctions restricting their access to international markets and stifling their economic growth. In the joint communiqué for the Pakistan-chaired 2024 CHG meeting , SCO member states had reaffirmed the need for consistent implementation of a roadmap on gradual increase in the share of national currencies in mutual settlements. It underlined the need to protect and promote the World Trade Organisation’s multilateral trade system for inclusive global growth and reduce reliance on the American currency for international trade transactions. At that summit, PM Shehbaz Sharif had noted “growing consensus among the member states on the use of mutual currencies for settlements” and said such a transition would “shield us from global financial disruptions”. Speaking in Dushanbe, Dar highlighted that the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) offered “every SCO partner a compelling opportunity to participate in and accelerate our shared journey towards comprehensive economic integration”. “For our region to achieve seamless economic integration, targeted investment in core sectors, most notably in energy and transport, is vital,” he stressed. The foreign minister criticised “protectionist policies and unilateral coercive measures”, saying they contradicted the principles of international law, “suppress economic growth, block technological progress and increase inequality”. “Therefore, reform of the global financial architecture and trade regimes is essential for achieving equitable global development,” the deputy PM declared. He said Pakistan strongly advocated for “expanding investments into high-potential industries, including agriculture, mining and minerals, and information technology, to build a resilient and interconnected economic future”. He expressed Pakistan’s “belief that artificial intelligence, digital transformation, innovation, energy cooperation and international information security should become important pillars of future cooperation within the SCO”. Dar then recalled the priority areas identified by PM Shehbaz for the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) summit that Islamabad is set to host in 2027. These comprised peace, security and mutual trust; regional connectivity and trade; innovation, AI and digital transformation; climate resilience and sustainable energy; and people-to-people exchanges. He emphasised that strategic investment in transport and energy infrastructure was not merely beneficial but “absolutely imperative for true regional economic integration”. At the outset of his speech, Dar extended his appreciation to the Tajik government and people for their “very warm and generous hospitality”. “For the past 25 years, the SCO has remained anchored in the Shanghai spirit of mutual trust and respect for diversity and expanded its mandate to encompass trade, infrastructure, culture and innovation,” he noted. Dar went on to state that Pakistan’s journey within the SCO highlighted its commitment to the Shanghai spirit, recalling that the country’s chairmanship of SCO’s Reg­ional Anti-Terrorist Structure (SCO-RATS) and the SCO Working Group on Poverty Alleviation. He said Pakistan intended to highlight the role of small and medium enterprises in reducing poverty. ‘Pakistan wants peaceful, regionally integrated Afghanistan’ During his speech at the CHG summit, DPM Dar also raised the issue of cross-border terrorism emanating from Afghanistan. Noting that sustainable economic development cannot be guaranteed without durable peace and security in the region, he said ensuring stability in Afghanistan was “imperative” for safeguarding regional peace. “Pakistan continues to be desirous of a peaceful, stable, regionally integrated and prosperous Afghanistan, which is at peace with itself and its neighbours.” The deputy premier pointed out that Islamabad had only one expectation from the “Afghan Taliban regime: that Afghan territory should not be used for terrorism against Pakistan and the world”. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to a peaceful and stable neighbourhood as an essential foundation for regional development and prosperity. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. Concluding his address, Dar congratulated Tajikistan and the heads of SCO’s permanent bodies on the successful completion of the CHG meeting, and congratulated Uzbekistan for taking over the chair. He also commended the SCO national coordinators for their help in finalising documents. He stated: “The fundamental strength of the SCO is anchored not only in our deeply intertwined histories, but more importantly, in the resilient, shared future that we collectively choose to forge. “Pakistan stands resolute in its commitment to serve as an active architect of this shared destiny, and to shape the next decade of Eurasian connectivity and economic prosperity.” Recommendations to deepen intra-SCO cooperation Addressing an expanded-format session of the CHG meeting later, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to regional harmony, trade, transit connectivity and economic integration as “a natural bridge connecting South Asia, Central Asia, and Eurasia”. “Pakistan firmly believes that dialogue and diplomacy offer the most effective path to resolving regional tensions,” he said, highlighting the country’s efforts for de-escalation in the Middle East. To this effect, Pakistan remains engaged in mediation efforts between the US and Iran, he added. “We will continue to support all efforts for dialogue and peaceful resolution of disputes for lasting peace and stability,” the foreign minister said. “Our diplomatic strategy is guided by our firm belief that regional challenges require collective, cooperative, and sustainable multilateral solutions.” He went on to highlight that SCO had transformed from a regional confidence-building platform into a premier transcontinental organisation representing over 40 per cent of humanity. Dar further highlighted that the intra-SCO trade had expanded significantly, proving that cooperative multilateralism can effectively drive stability and sustainable development across our shared continent. “The future prospects of the SCO remain bright,” the deputy premier remarked, noting that the region was situated at the crossroads of major international trade corridors. By leveraging our vast natural resources, technological advancements, and vibrant human capital, the SCO could lead digital transformation, industrial growth, and sustainable economic development across Eurasia, he emphasised. To realise this vision, the foreign minister also proposed recommendations to deepen economic cooperation among SCO countries and expand international partnerships. Firstly, Dar called for empowering the SCO Chambers of Commerce and Business Council by establishing direct business-to-business links and organising joint trade expos. He also urged member states to streamline customs procedures to support SMEs. Secondly, he proposed the strengthening of the SCO Interbank Consortium (IBC). “We must accelerate local currency settlements and enhance the SCO Interbank Consortium framework to mitigate external financial risks, harmonise cross-border payment systems, and facilitate seamless trade financing,” he said. Pending the establishment of the SCO Development Bank, the IBC can play a more active role in financing infrastructure upgrades, Dar added. He underlined that Habib Bank Limited (HBL), the current chair of the IBC, can help advance this agenda through close coordination with fellow members. At last, the foreign minister recommended expanding international partnerships. “The SCO should actively expand structured partnerships with international organisations including the United Nations, Asean, the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO), and other international and regional financial institutions, to reinforce an open, rules-based, and inclusive regional order,” Dar underscored. He added: “Pakistan recommends that the SCO adopt a forward-looking strategy focused on joint technological innovation, climate resilience, energy security and secure supply chains. “We must also operationalise Eurasian energy and transport corridors while deepening people-to-people ties, cultural exchanges, and educational partnerships.” Concluding his speech, Dar said Pakistan looked forward to welcoming the heads of state at the SCO CHS summit in Islamabad in August 2027. “Pakistan remains steadfast in its resolve to foster a peaceful, interconnected, and prosperous SCO community. Together, let us forge a shared future of enduring prosperity for all our people,” he resolved. Dar meets Tajik top leadership Ahead of the SCO meeting, DPM Dar called on Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, along with other heads of delegations. “President Rahmon welcomed the leaders and emphasised the importance of strengthening regional economic cooperation under the SCO to promote connectivity, stability and shared prosperity,” the Foreign Office (FO) said. He, along with other delegates, was then welcomed by PM Qohir Rasulzoda. Later in the day, Dar met with Tajikistan’s FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin on the sidelines of the meeting. The two ministers “reaffirmed the longstanding brotherly ties between Pakistan and Tajikistan, rooted in shared history, culture and faith”, FO said. They underscored the need to further expand trade and economic cooperation, enhance regional connectivity and strengthen cooperation in energy, security and people-to-people exchanges. The foreign ministers also exchanged views on regional and global developments and underscored the importance of continued coordination at regional and multilateral forums to advance shared goals of peace and prosperity, FO added. The deputy premier then returned to Islamabad in the evening after concluding his “productive visit”, FO said. During his visit, Dar also held bilateral meetings with his counterparts from SCO member states on the sidelines of the SCO moot, according to FO. On Monday , Dar held a meeting with the Tajik premier. He also met with China’s PM Li Qiang and Mongolia’s First DPM Jadambyn Enkhbayar on the sidelines of a banquet dinner hosted for the delegates. Pakistan, which hosted a CHG meeting in October 2024, is now scheduled to host the CHS summit in 2027 after it assumed the chairmanship last month. On Sept 30, Dar reviewed preparations for the CHS summit as SCO national coordinators , who were in Islamabad for a meeting, called on him. In July, Pakistan hosted the 12th meeting of the Heads of Border Services of the Competent Authorities of the SCO.

title: PM warns against resistance to FBR reforms
description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday warned tax officers that resistance to the ongoing reforms in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) would not be tolerated, directing the authorities to implement proposed measures to minimise the country’s tax gap. The prime minister’s warning came during a weekly briefing on tax reforms, following a call for a pen-down strike by the Inland Revenue Officers Association. The strike call was later withdrawn after intervention by senior FBR officials. FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial briefed the prime minister on the pilot project for faceless assessment and audit. A source privy to the meeting told Dawn that the prime minister expressed displeasure over the strike announcement. “We will not tolerate any resistance against the ongoing reforms in the FBR,” PM Shehbaz was quoted as saying, adding that officers unwilling to work would be asked to leave. The prime minister reminded tax officers that their salaries had been increased fourfold and that they had been provided with vehicles and accommodation. “We have extended every facility to these officers,” he said, adding that it was now their responsibility to deliver results and justify the incentives granted to them. The FBR has established the National Faceless Centre (NFC) in Islamabad, where dedicated wings will handle audits and assessments through a faceless system aimed at reducing official discretion and direct contact between tax officials and taxpayers. Initially staffed by 27 officers, the centre has been tasked with auditing and assessing third-party data relating to 300,000 to 400,000 individuals under a pilot project that became effective on October 1. The data will be referred to the NFC in phases after the completion of initial compliance checks. According to an official announcement by the Prime Minister’s Secretariat, PM Shehbaz directed that the pace of FBR reforms be accelerated, noting that the initial results of the ongoing measures were encouraging. He emphasised that the institution’s capacity must be continuously strengthened to bridge the tax gap. The prime minister directed the FBR chairman to expedite the rollout of the faceless system in tax collection. “These reforms are in the larger interest of the state and will continue under all circumstances,” he said, adding that indiscriminate action should be taken against corrupt officials. He further directed that officers and staff showing improvements in conduct and performance be given opportunities to reform, while those persisting in corruption and inefficiency would have no place in the organisation. Meanwhile, the FBR suspended two Inland Revenue Service officers, one in BS-20 and the other in BS-19, and repatriated two other BS-20 officers to FBR Headquarters for further investigation over an unauthorised press statement and a call to suspend official work. Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

title: Govt unveils hi-tech system to manage loadshedding
description: • Asset Performance Management System pilot project to be launched from Lahore, Kasur • APMS to be synced with smart meters to monitor power consumption in real-time • System will help authorities triangulate point of loss, theft with greater accuracy LAHORE: The government is all set to introduce the Asset Performance Mana­gement System (APMS), also known as the Advanced Power Management System, to control power theft and load management across the country in a phased manner. Minister for Energy (Power Division) Awais Leghari, while speaking at a ceremony in Dera Ghazi Khan on Monday, revealed the government’s plan to introduce modern technology to combat power theft and curtail line losses. According to him, the APMS will identify specific transformers in high-theft areas, enabling targeted disconnections so that thousands of paying consumers on an entire feeder are not penalised for the actions of electricity thieves. The minister reiterated that loadshedding will continue on feeders reporting 30 percent or higher losses, emphasising that no leniency will be shown toward electricity thieves or chronic defaulters. According to power experts, the APMS will enable more targeted identification of high-loss consumers, improve energy accounting, enhance operational visibility, and support equitable load management through data-driven decision-making. As the Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC), the technical arm of the Mini­stry of Energy (Power Divis­ion), is playing a central role in supporting the planning, des­ign, and effective implementation of this sector-wide reform, the APMS will serve as a key enabler in achieving these obje­ctives through transformer-le­vel monitoring, analytics, digi­tal oversight, and enforcement mechanisms across Discos. The APMS works alongside Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) and Automated Meter Reading (AMR) rollouts, enabling two-way communication and remote cutoff capabilities. “The APMS pilot project is all set to be launched in Lahore and Kasur soon, as the necessary work is underway by the Lahore Electric Supply Company (Lesco). Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will inaugurate this pilot project soon,” confirmed an official source in Lesco while talking to Dawn. Talking about the background and launch of the APMS, he said the Discos have been implementing, for the last few years, the Power Division’s policy under which loadshedding is observed, keeping in view the loss category of 11kV feeders. According to him, loadshedding (both scheduled and forced) is being observed at loss-making feeders categorised as 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Two hours of loadshedding are observed in areas falling within the service jurisdiction of category-1 feeders, followed by four, six, eight, and 10 hours on category 2, 3, 4, and 5 feeders, respectively. “The problem is that if we observe loadshedding in the areas falling within the service jurisdiction of such loss-making feeders, all consumers, including those paying their bills regularly, also bear the brunt of those stealing electricity. So this system will soon be in place, gradually, to protect the rights of law-abiding consumers,” he explained. He said that under the new arrangement, the APMS would be installed on transformers of various capacities currently placed on poles. After the APMS installations, the existing conventional electricity meters would be replaced by AMI meters (smart meters). After replacement, the APMS would be synced with the smart meters and start monitoring the real-time consumption of electricity users. “Suppose there are 200 consumers receiving power from one transformer in any area. The APMS at each transformer will record the total number of units received from the power distribution system and the actual number of units used by the consumers. If the units received from the system are 100,000 and the number used by the consumers is less than that, it would mean that the remaining units have been stolen through unfair means. In this way, it will be easy for the Discos to detect power-stealing consumers,” he explained. “At present, it is difficult to detect power thieves in a vast area (2,000 to 3,000 consumers or even more) covered by a feeder. With the APMS, the area would be narrowed from the feeder to the transformer (150 to 200 consumers),” he said, adding that this would help Lesco stop power theft and reduce line losses more effectively. According to another Lesco officer, the APMS would be installed in a 2/4-foot iron box at transformers. “The APMS would automatically report the theft, line losses, etc. to the officials concerned, enabling them to respond quickly to fix the issue,” he maintained. Similarly, he said, if someone touched the AMI meter with the intention to tamper with it and steal electricity, the meter itself would report to the system monitored by the officials. Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

title: GDP growth revised down to 3.65pc as country falls short of target
description: • Industrial, services sector slowdown drags down economic growth in FY26 • Per capita income ‘lowest in region’; economy reaches $450.4bn ISLAMABAD: The government on Monday revised the gross domestic product (GDP) growth slightly downward to 3.65 per cent for the outgoing fiscal year (FY26), attributing the adjustment to a mild slowdown in the industrial and services sectors. The country’s GDP registered modest growth alongside an increase in per capita income in dollar terms, reflecting a sluggish pace of recovery in the country’s overall output compared with the previous year, the government said. In May 2026, the government had projected the economy to grow by 3.70pc in FY26, revising its earlier estimate of 4pc. The downward adjustment now indicates that the country fell short of its GDP target. The revised growth rates in agriculture, industry and services in FY26 are 3.50pc, 3.34pc and 3.81pc, respectively, compared with earlier growth rates of 2.89pc, 3.51pc and 4.09pc. The revision came during the 118th meeting of the National Accounts Committee (NAC), which was held on Monday at the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. The NAC estimate places Pakistan broadly in line with the outlook of multilateral lenders, though with some variation. The International Monetary Fund has projected GDP growth at 3.6pc for FY26, the World Bank at 3.7pc and the Asian Development Bank at 3.7pc, while the State Bank of Pakistan expects growth to remain close to 3.7pc. The committee approved the incorporation of revised imports data in the national accounts estimates from FY21 to FY25, quarterly GDP growth rates for Q1 (revised), Q2 (revised), Q3 (revised), and Q4 during FY26 and updated annual growth rates for FY25 and FY26. The size of the economy rose to $450.4 billion in FY26 from $410.96bn in FY25, mainly driven by growth in the services sector, followed by industry and livestock. Per capita income slightly increased to $1,896 in FY26, the lowest in the region, up from $1,824 in FY25. The projection is based on the 2023 census. However, it was $1,551 in FY23, $1,766 in FY22 and $1,677 in FY21. This suggests a deterioration in the standard of living and well-being acro­ss almost all segments of society, with no tangible increase in personal incomes due to unprecedented inflationary pressures, which reduce disposable income and limit individuals’ ability to afford goods and services, save, or invest. Updated growth rates Meanwhile, the NAC also approved the updated growth rates for Q1, Q2 and Q3 of 2025-26 at 3.89pc, 4.31pc and 4.42pc, respectively, compared with 3.92pc, 4.05pc and 3.99pc, presented at the 117th meeting of the NAC. The fourth quarter of FY26 recorded a 2pc growth in GDP. The committee approved the updated annual growth of 3.11pc for FY25, which was estimated at 3.18pc in the previous meeting. In agriculture, important crops improved from 0.65pc to 1.59pc due to wheat and maize, other crops have witnessed significant improvement from 2.43pc to 4.28pc due to higher production of pulses (6.3pc), fruits (1.3pc), tomato (44pc), oilseed (5.4pc), and green fodder (2.4pc). Livestock decreased slightly from 3.75pc to 3.71pc because of increased fodder inputs. Updated growth rates in forestry and fishing are 10.80pc and 1.39pc, respectively. The committee revised growth in industry during FY26 to 3.34pc from 3.51pc estimated previously. The mining & quarrying industry has improved from 0.38pc to 1.52pc due to improvement in gas (2.84pc), crude oil (5.12pc), and coal (2.73pc). Large-scale manufacturing (LSM), which is measured through the Quantum Index of Manufacturing (QIM), has declined from 6.11pc to 5.01pc. The major LSM groups with positive contributions are food (7.03pc), tobacco (12.61pc), petroleum products (9.7pc), rubber products (14.19­pc), electrical equi­pment (14.25pc), automobiles (57.77­pc), transport equipment (42.36pc), furniture (22.69pc), and other manufacturing (foot­ball) (16.62pc). The construction industry has improved from 5.73pc to 6.30pc because of increased construction-related expenditure in the public sector. However, some LSM groups posted negative growth, e.g., pharmaceuticals (-8.87pc), iron & steel products (-7.84pc), chemicals (-2.53pc), and leather products (-1.95pc), electricity (-10.24pc) in FY26. The services industry has declined from 4.09pc to 3.81pc in FY26, with positive contributions from all the constituents. The growth in wholesale and retail trade posted at 2.37pc as against the previous growth of 3.71pc due to decrease in manufacturing and imports. Transport and storage industry growth improved to 3.23pc from 2.31pc due to upward revisions reported in railways, water transport, and air transport. Similarly, information & communication growth increased from 7.52pc to 9.53pc, the finance & insurance also improved from 0.32pc to 4.23pc in FY26 due to improvement in the insurance industry. The slowdown was also reported in public administration and social security to 5.67pc from 8.54pc, education 4.17pc from 5.23pc, and human health and social work 5.52pc from 6.85pc.
