title: KP has vast potential for industrial growth: governor
description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Monday said the province had vast potential for industrial development, so there was a need for a comprehensive and practical strategy to fully explore it for creating employment and strengthening the provincial economy. He was chairing a meeting of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Economic Zones Development and Management Company (EZDMC) at Governor House here. Officials briefed the governor on the EZDMC’s administrative structure, performance, achievements, future targets, economic zones, revenue generation and other related matters. Adviser to the governor on industries Mohammad Irshad, secretary of the industries department and other senior officials attended the meeting. Officials said that 15 economic zones were currently functional across the province, while plans were under way to establish seven more. They added that the company had so far facilitated the creation of around 107,000 employment opportunities. Officials highlighted issues confronting various economic zones, including the Yaka Ghund Marble City, Katlang Economic Zone and other proposed industrial projects. Governor Kundi said promotion of industries could generate thousands of employment opportunities for the people and play a vital role in ensuring sustainable economic growth. He emphasised encouraging private sector investment by providing a business-friendly environment and facilitating investors under the Ease of Doing Business Policy. Mr Kundi directed authorities to resolve functional issues of economic zones on a priority basis and asked them to consult the Finance Department regarding land acquisition and payment-related matters for new economic zone projects and present practical proposals. He also instructed officials to convene immediate meetings with relevant federal and provincial departments to address the issues facing economic zones, ensuring all stakeholders were taken into confidence for effective and practical solutions. The governor said matters relating to federal departments should be taken up with the federal government for timely resolution and stressed the need to address security concerns, site selection and other administrative challenges affecting economic zones. He said that some economic zones were located in areas facing law and order challenges. He called for a comprehensive review to devise workable solutions so that industrial activities could be initiated there. Mr Kundi directed authorities to expedite action for resolving financial issues and legal disputes, remove all obstacles affecting the functionality of economic zones and ensure early progress on pending matters. Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

title: Industry calls for easier rules as FBR urges export growth
description: KARACHI: Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chief Langrial urged exporters to expand the presence of Pakistani products in international markets, as industry leaders raised concerns over complicated regulations, digital invoicing difficulties and the tax burden on already compliant businesses. During a meeting with a delegation from the Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (Kati), led by its president, Sheikh Umer Rehan, FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial called on exporters to make effective use of available resources to increase national exports. He said the FBR would soon hold meetings with major exporters to review their concerns, identify obstacles to export growth and take necessary measures to address them. The FBR chairman also said the authority was pursuing tax system digitalisation and automated mechanisms to bring non-filers into the tax net. Kati flags costly regulations, digital invoicing; Langrial pledges action on concerns Mr Rehan, however, said digitalisation of the tax system was essential, but practical difficulties faced by industries during the implementation of digital invoicing needed to be resolved. He called on the government to provide businesses with proper guidance and technical assistance and establish effective coordination mechanisms to address implementation challenges. He said tax transparency should be strengthened without disrupting industrial and commercial activities. Mr Rehan also stressed that broadening the tax base required bringing all individuals and businesses legally liable to pay taxes into the system. The tax burden, he said, should not remain concentrated on already compliant businesses. He called on authorities to identify untaxed sectors and ensure uniform enforcement of tax laws across all relevant segments. The Kati president also highlighted tax and duty-related issues affecting industries in the Korangi Industrial Area, particularly the ghee and edible oil sector. He urged the government to review unnecessary statutory regulatory orders (SROs) and complicated regulatory requirements that obstruct business operations and increase production costs. Such rules, he said, should be simplified and made practical to improve the competitiveness of local industries. Responding to the delegation’s concerns, Mr Langrial assured its members that necessary steps would be taken to resolve the issues. Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs5.16 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs7.69
description: The government on Monday cut the price of petrol by Rs5.16 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.69. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs381.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs389.27 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 20 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

title: SECP probes discrepancies in SE Fruits IPO
description: ISLAMABAD: The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has launched an investigation into the initial public offering (IPO) of SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited after an anonymous complaint revealed major financial discrepancies in the company’s audit report, officials said. The commission is also looking to strengthen the Audit Oversight Board after discrepancies were detected in the company’s audit report. The inquiry will examine whether any gaps, omissions or negligence occurred during the IPO approval process and determine responsibility where warranted. The inquiry follows an anonymous complaint received on Sept 11, two days after the SECP approved the company’s prospectus based on its audited financial statements. A preliminary review flagged differences between reported sales and sales tax returns for 2022-26, local sales that were not reflected in the company’s 2024 income tax return and a gap between reported sales, after accounting for closing receivables, and bank credits. The complaint questioned the sales figures disclosed in the prospectus, which were based on the company’s audit report. The SECP asked SE Fruits and Vegetable Ltd., its consultant to the issue and its auditors to provide documents and explain the discrepancies. The company submitted additional material following a meeting with the parties concerned. The inquiry will examine the information and explanations provided to determine whether the differences resulted from inaccurate disclosures, accounting treatment or other factors. The IPO process was suspended while the concerns were examined, and the company later withdrew its application. The investigation will review the Pakistan Stock Exchange’s role as a front-line regulator, the consultant to the issue’s due diligence, its role in preparing the prospectus and certifying its accuracy, and the auditor’s examination of the company’s financial statements. The inquiry will also assess the SECP’s internal procedures for reviewing IPO applications and handling the complaint. Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

title: Equities falter below 166,000 amid selling pressure
description: KARACHI: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) opened the week on a depressed note amid persistent regional and political turmoil as investors remained cautious in a directionless market due to lack of positive triggers. Topline Securities Ltd said the KSE-100 index remained under pressure, closing at 165,966, down 453 points or 0.27pc, reflecting cautious investor sentiment. The absence of positive triggers, coupled with elevated international oil prices and political instability in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, continued to weigh on market sentiment, keeping investors cautious and limiting recovery attempts. Index-heavy stocks remained under pressure, with United Bank, Engro Holdings, Systems Ltd, Hub Power and Sazgar Engineering Works emerging as major laggards, collectively shaving about 273 points off the benchmark. Investor participation remained subdued as trading volume dipped to 370 million shares. However, turnover edged up to Rs19.5bn. Pakistan Refinery topped the volume chart with 52m shares. Ali Najib, deputy head of trading at Arif Habib Ltd, said the PSX witnessed a lacklustre session as jittery conditions forced the index to close below the 166,000 level. The brokerage noted that the index opened on a negative note and touched an intraday low of 165,918 before staging a recovery to a high of 166,698. However, the recovery proved short-lived as selling pressure intensified in the second half, erasing gains and dragging the index back towards its intraday low by close. On the corporate front, Engro Fertiliser reported net profit of Rs9.1bn (earnings per share Rs6.83) for 3QCY26, up 57pc year-on-year, supported by stronger fertiliser offtakes. The company announced a cash dividend of Rs5.50 per share, compared with Rs4.50 per share in the same period last year, implying an 80pc payout ratio. The relatively measured payout may reflect a cautious capital allocation approach amid potential liabilities. Analysts expect the market to remain volatile and range-bound between 164,000 and 168,000 amid cautious sentiment and evolving macroeconomic and geopolitical developments. Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
description: LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said. A statement by the KP police said law enforcers had initiated a search and strike operation in the Charpara area at noon, where terrorists had set up a blockade on Wednesday night. The operation was led by Banda Daud Shah and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) deputy superintendents of police (DSP), in which bomb disposal unit (BDU) personnel, a drone team, Rescue 15 personnel and Rapid Response Force personnel also participated, the statement said. “During the operation, the law enforcers raided the hideout of a terrorist commander, Qaiser Iqbal, where an exchange of fire took place,” the police said, adding that two terrorists were killed in the encounter. CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan, Latambar Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector (SI) Afzal Awan, Constable Kazim and Head Constable Amjab from the BDU were martyred in the exchange of fire. The statement said the operation was ongoing. It added, “The brave martyred personnel of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police have set a shining example of dedication to duty, courage, and a commitment to public safety by sacrificing their lives in the fight against terrorism.” The statement said the sacrifices of the martyred policemen reflected the police force’s “unwavering resolve” to continue making every possible effort to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace in the region. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the incident and expressed sorrow over the martyrdom of four police personnel. “The sacrifices of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police in the fight against terrorism are unforgettable. The blood of our martyrs will not go to waste; our resolve against terrorism will be further strengthened, and the struggle for the establishment of peace will continue,” he said. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time, including attacks on police personnel. Thursday’s operation comes around 20 days after several terrorist hideouts were destroyed during a joint search and strike operation in Karak. In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

title: ‘Hit them hard’: CDF Munir vows to continue campaign against Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits
description: Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir has said the armed forces will continue the counterterrorism campaign against Indian sponsored terrorsts groups “to the fullest”, vowing to “hit them hard wherever they are,” the military’s media wing said on Friday. CDF Munir made the remarks during a visit to the Corps Headquarters in Peshawar, where he was briefed on the security situation, ongoing counterterrorism operations, border management measures and operational preparedness of formations deployed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a statement issued by the Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. Upon arrival at the headquarters, CDF Munir was received by the Peshawar Corps commander. During his visit, he lauded the morale and professionalism of the armed forces and directed them to continue “vigilance and [the] highest standards of operational readiness to effectively counter threats”. ISPR added that CDF Munir vowed that the armed forces will “continue the campaign against Indian sponsored terrorist outfits to the fullest and hit them hard wherever they are”. He also paid tribute to the martyred security personnel, affirming that “with the support of the people, Pakistan will surely inflict total defeat [on] the terrorists and their perverted ideology”. A day earlier, CDF Munir attended a meeting of KP apex committee held at the Governor House, where the province’s overall security situation was reviewed. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif who chaired the meeting, said that the federal government, which now runs KP under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc. The increased terrorist activity has prompted security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations. A day earlier, four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in KP’s Karak. On October 19, an army major was martyred and four terrorists were killed during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan. A day before that, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBOs conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.

title: DPM Dar departs for Istanbul ahead of R-4 bloc, European E3 diplomats’ meetings
description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has departed for Istanbul to attend a meeting of R-4 bloc foreign ministers and an R-4+E-3 meeting on Friday, the Foreign Office (FO) said. The R-4 group, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran. The E-3 group comprises three European powers — France, the United Kingdom and Germany — that established the grouping more than 20 years ago to advance diplomatic coordination on Iran’s nuclear programme. The FO said DPM Dar will be attending the meeting on October 23 (today) at the invitation of Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan. Following the R-4 meeting, the ministers would participate in a meeting with the foreign ministers of the European E-3 bloc, consisting of the UK, France and Germany, the statement added. “This will be the first meeting of the seven countries in this format,” FO said. “The meetings will focus on key regional developments and explore coordinated diplomatic approaches to address shared challenges and advance regional peace and stability,” FO added. DPM Dar is also set to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts during his visit as well. “Pakistan’s participation reflects its continued commitment to constructive diplomacy, regional cooperation and the peaceful resolution of disputes,” FO said. A Turkish diplomatic source told Reuters a day earlier that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran , Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security. The ministers are expected to discuss the Israeli-Palestinian issue, the latest situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments related to Yemen, efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, and opportunities for closer cooperation between the regional and European countries, the source added. Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, they said. The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

title: Lahore tops global pollution ranking as air quality turns ‘hazardous’
description: Lahore ranked as the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with its air quality classified as “hazardous”, according to air quality monitoring platform IQAir. In the past few years, air pollution has become one of the most pressing public health and environmental crises facing Pakistan. Various cities of the country, most notably Lahore , deal with smog, especially in the winter months. The phenomenon is attributed mainly to industrial emissions, vehicular pollution , stubble burning and air movement . Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted cities on Friday morning, with an air quality index (AQI) of 410, according to the IQAir live tracker. The reading fell under the ‘very unhealthy’ category. India’s New Delhi followed with an AQI of 203, while Senegal’s Dakar ranked third at 196. Figure shows the top ranked polluted cities according to IQAir on Friday morning. — Screengrab via IQAir The provincial capital was the only Pakistani city to rank among the 20 most polluted cities on Friday morning. Karachi was the only other Pakistani city on the 21-city list, with an AQI of 110. According to IQAir, in Lahore , “PM2.5 concentration is currently 45.2 times the World Health Organisation annual PM2.5 guideline value”. PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particles, with diameters generally 2.5 micrometres and smaller. Of all air pollution measures, PM2.5 pollution poses the greatest health threat, according to IQAir. According to the website, PM2.5 can enter the circulatory system and even the brain, causing serious health complications if long-term exposure occurs. For those in Lahore, IQAir recommended avoiding outdoor exercise, keeping windows closed to prevent outdoor air from entering, wearing a mask outdoors and installing an air purifier indoors. Lahore air quality map. —IQAir The Punjab government’s air quality monitoring platform, meanwhile, recorded an AQI of 339 for Lahore at 11am on Thursday, classifying the air as ‘very unhealthy’. The reading was based on data from 10 monitoring stations across the city. The difference between the readings on the two platforms may be due to variations in monitoring stations, averaging periods and methodologies. However, both indicated severe air pollution in the provincial capital. Human rights activist Sheikh Saqib told Dawn that both his children were suffering from throat infections due to smog. He criticised the government for what he described as empty claims about measures to curb air pollution. He said school attendance could drop by half as parents stopped sending their children to school amid deteriorating air quality. Saqib also disputed the chief minister’s claims that smog had been controlled over the past three years, saying he continued to witness crop burning while travelling on motorways towards Islamabad and Karachi. “Vehicles emitting smoke are still running on Lahore’s roads,” he said, questioning the effectiveness of the government’s measures to tackle air pollution. On Oct 2, Lahore also topped IQAir’s list of the world’s most polluted cities, with an AQI of 167, classified as “unhealthy”. At the time, CM Maryam said the government was making efforts to address environmental issues. Earlier this week, a new analysis released by the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) ranked Lahore among cities whose ozone levels were “extremely poor”.

title: China orders 'all-out' rescue after Tibet quake kills 16
description: China ordered an “all-out” rescue effort in Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured dozens and flattened hundreds of homes, state media reported. Footage showed rescue workers with torches clambering in the dark through some of the more than 300 houses that Xinhua said collapsed in the 7.0-magnitude quake on Thursday evening. Diners ran out of restaurants and items fell off wobbling supermarket shelves as the tremor struck, according to clips on state broadcaster CCTV , which said 65 people were injured. One resident told local media that her family had just gone to bed when her home shook, knocking over objects, and that they “rushed outside without even taking the time to get dressed.” “My legs were shaking the entire time I was heading downstairs and by the time I reached the bottom, I was so terrified that I burst into tears,” the woman said. Local residents “are afraid to return to their homes,” she said. “They set up tents along the roadside or spent the night in their cars.” A man told the Beijing News that the “very strong” quake left his home “creaking and rattling”. “I was asleep when it hit. Everyone has run outside now and is too afraid to go back in. I’m currently driving to an open area to sleep in my car,” he said. Broadcaster CCTV also showed emergency personnel with helmets carrying a person and shining flashlights on damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs. Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information. ‘Significant casualties’ President Xi Jinping said the tremor caused “significant casualties” and took place at a “high-altitude location” in cold weather. “(We) must go all-out to carry out search and rescue operations and do our utmost to treat the injured, so as to minimise casualties,” Xinhua quoted Xi as saying. He called for assistance for residents and rescue equipment to be sent to the area promptly. The epicentre was in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said. It struck at 10:33 pm (7:33 pm PKT) on Thursday at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres. Lhawang Dagpo, a local official in the Maru township, the quake’s epicentre, said it put cracks in the walls of his office, according to Xinhua . Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said. Baqing County has mobilised more than 1,600 people to help in the relief operation, CCTV reported. The municipal fire and rescue brigade has dispatched 25 vehicles and 110 personnel, and the Nagqu Armed Police Detachment sent 225 officers and soldiers and 18 vehicles, CCTV said. As of 4:30 am (1:30 am PKT) on Friday, relief supplies including 1,000 prefabricated houses, 3,239 tents, four generators and 1,000 flashlights had been delivered, it added. President Zardari, PM Shehbaz extend condolences President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, in separate statements on Friday, extended their condolences to the Chinese president, the bereaved families and the people of China. Both leaders also reaffirmed Pakistan’s solidarity with China and prayed for the swift recovery of those injured. In a statement shared by his office, President Zardari “expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives”. PM Shehbaz said he was deeply saddened by “the tragic loss of precious lives and injuries caused by the devastating earthquake”. He added that Pakistan was “ready to extend every possible support”. Earthquakes in China are relatively common. In January 2025, a quake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county killed at least 126 people. The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media. That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan . A massive tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left about 90,000 people dead or missing, including around thousands of schoolchildren.

title: PCB opens direct signings window for PSL teams, announces pre-season roadmap
description: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday opened the direct signings window for all eight HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchises and unveiled the pre-season roadmap for the 12th edition of the tournament, which will be held from March 18 to May 2 next year. The player-movement cycle has begun with immediate effect, with the Player Auction scheduled for Jan 23 next year. HBL PSL 12 will feature 44 matches, comprising 40 league fixtures and four playoffs, over 46 days. For the first time in the league’s history, matches will be played across five to six venues. Under the direct signings rules, each franchise will be allowed to sign one marquee player who did not feature in either HBL PSL 10 or HBL PSL 11. The window will remain open until Nov 23. A workshop involving the franchises next week will finalise retention deadlines, the pre-auction trade window, auction regulations and playing conditions. In a significant development for domestic cricket, the PCB has formally aligned the National T20 Gold and National T20 Silver tournaments with the PSL pre-season calendar. The two competitions will now serve as the primary talent-identification pathway, providing outstanding domestic performers with a clearer route into the franchise league and potentially earning them selection for the national team. PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi described the upcoming season as the league’s most ambitious edition yet. “HBL PSL is Pakistan cricket’s biggest stage, and Season 12 will be its most ambitious yet. HBL PSL 11 ended before a record crowd, and we are building on that momentum by taking the league to more cities than ever before,” he said in a statement. “The roadmap we have finalised and are partially announcing today gives every stakeholder, from franchises and players to commercial partners and broadcasters, the certainty to plan at the highest level. With the foundations now in place, we are looking forward to an exciting season.” HBL PSL Chief Executive Officer Salman Naseer also highlighted the league’s expanded geographical reach, saying the move to multiple venues would bring the competition closer to fans across the country. “For the first time, HBL PSL will go to five to six venues, bringing the league closer to fans across Pakistan and giving more cities the chance to host the best of T20 cricket,” he said. “From today, the race to build the best squad for HBL PSL 12 is on. Every Direct Signing, every trade, every retention decision over the coming weeks will shape the teams that take the field in March. We look forward to a season that takes this league further than it has ever gone.” The announcement builds on the landmark 2026 season, when the PSL expanded to eight teams with the inclusion of Hyderabad Kingsmen and Rawalpindiz. Peshawar Zalmi claimed their second title after defeating debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen in the final at Gaddafi Stadium, which drew a record crowd of 32,461. The season, however, was also affected by regional tensions and fuel shortages, forcing organisers to concentrate most of the matches in Lahore and Karachi. Further details regarding venues, the complete schedule and commercial arrangements are expected to be announced in the coming weeks as franchises begin assembling their squads for the tournament. The PCB hopes the next edition will deliver a broader and more accessible experience for fans of Pakistan’s premier T20 competition.

title: Peshawar High Court bars arrest of KP Assembly deputy speaker
description: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has restrained the authorities from arresting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suriya Bibi until Nov 10, while allowing her to retain access to her official residence. A bench comprising Justices Ijaz Anwar and Muhammad Faheem Wali ordered that the Oct 14 order to vacate her official residence remain suspended. It also provisionally allowed her to occupy the accommodation until the next hearing. “The respondents are further restrained from arresting the petitioner till the date fixed,” the bench ruled in its three-page order sheet. The court fixed Nov 10 for the next hearing of Ms Bibi’s petition against the sealing of her official residence and her anticipated arrest under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. Court also allows Suriya Bibi to retain official residence, suspends order to vacate it The bench observed that the proclamation imposing governor’s rule in the province did not mention the speaker or deputy speaker among the functionaries who ceased to hold office. “Apparently, the presidential order does not find mention of the position of speaker/deputy speaker. Similarly, even the vacation order makes reference to those categories (of ministers and advisers) but it nowhere mentions the position of speaker/deputy speaker, which prima facie suggests that the same is not covered by the proclamation order,” it observed. The bench noted that Advocate Gen­eral Sanaullah had argued that in “view of Federal Government Order-1 of 2026, read with Federal Government Order-2 of 2026 and the Oct 11 proclamation” for an emergency, the government had every authority to have official accommodation vacated by advisers and provincial ministers, including the deputy speaker. He also contended that the petitioner had been named in an FIR registered on behalf of the Chitral deputy commissioner on Oct 12 under Section 406 of the Pakistan Penal Code. The bench reproduced the proclamation order regarding the cessation of certain categories of the public representatives. “The chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and the advocate general of the province of KP shall forthwith cease to hold office,” one of its provisions said. The court also referred to arguments by the petitioner’s counsel, Yasir Khattak, who cited Section 8 of the KP Province Speaker and Deputy Speaker’s (Immunities, Privileges, Salaries and Allowances) Act, 2026. It entitles the speaker and deputy speaker to use official accommodation with­out paying rent until they are replaced and their substitutes are chosen. The lawyer also cited Section 27(2) of the act, which provided that the deputy speaker could not be arrested, detained or confined, and that her official residence could not be searched, entered or raided by a law enforcement agency during her term in office. He claimed that after governor’s rule was imposed in the province, pol­ice raided his client’s official residence “without any reason and justification to harass her and unlawfully arrest her”. He added that at midnight on Oct 14, the respondents and other officials again raided the residence and locked it. The petitioner asked the court to direct the provincial government and the ins­pector general of police to immediately unseal her residence and restore her access to and possession of the property. She also sought directions restraining the KP police chief and Peshawar deputy commissioner from raiding her residence or arresting or detaining her under any order issued pursuant to Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance. Following the imposition of governor’s rule, a case was registered against the deputy speaker for allegedly “refusing to return an official vehicle”. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: ATC indicts PAF officer’s murderer, summons witnesses
description: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Thursday indicted an accused arrested in connection with the murder of Group Captain Asim Tariq, and summoned prosecution witnesses to record their statements. Judge Abual Hasnat Mohammad Zulqarnain of the ATC conducted the hearing, during which the accused, Saad Abbasi, was produced before the court. The judge read out the charges against the accused, who pleaded not guilty and opted to contest the case. After the indictment, the court summoned the prosecution witnesses for the next hearing and adjourned the proceedings until November 2. Police have registered a case against the accused at Margalla Police Station in connection with the murder. On July 5, the PAF Group Captain was martyred in Islamabad in a bid to save a woman as the suspect was trying to take her away “forcefully”. As Tariq intervened, Abbasi opened fire, which hit the officer. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives
description: • Rebels claim targeting Saudi defence ministry, Aramco installations, Dammam airport • Coalition downs four drones above Riyadh, Madina • Egypt urges talks as its parliament weighs military backing for Saudi campaign in Yemen • IRGC warns US against escorting ships thru Hormuz • Pakistan warns pilgrims travelling between Iran and Iraq RIYADH: Yemen’s Houthi forces said on Thursday they had launched attacks on Saudi Arabia’s defence ministry in Riyadh, Aramco facilities in Yanbu and the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, where Saudi authorities said two people were killed. Meanwhile, Iran’s Revolu­tio­nary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. The strike on the airport in the kingdom’s eastern oil hub on Wednesday evening killed a Saudi citizen and an Indian national and wounded eight others, according to Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation. It said the injuries ranged from minor to serious, and that operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal. Elsewhere, two people were reportedly killed in a Houthi drone attack on a Saudi oil field. The Saudi-led coalition said separately that it had intercepted and destroyed four drones over the Riyadh and Madina regions. Meanwhile, in a televised speech, the Houthi military spok­es­person, Yahya Saree, claimed attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and on the defence ministry in Riyadh. Saree said Saudi attacks had killed and wounded 562 people in Yemen since mid-July, when the Houthis imposed a naval blockade on the kingdom. The coalition warned at the time that it would respond “firmly”. Following attacks in the region, Aramco told staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran, on the Gulf coast, and work remotely, six people with knowledge of the matter said. Oil prices This would be the company’s first such evacuation since the Iran war began. The Houthis cau­sed extensive damage to the headquarters earlier this month, when a strike on the building sent fire spreading across several floors. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but Saudi Arabia’s benchmark stock index fell 2.5pc on Thursday. Oil prices rose about 3pc to a five-month high. Brent crude fut­ures gained $3.51 to $112.33 a barrel, while US West Texas Inter­mediate rose $2.14 to $99.29. Brent entered technically overbought territory for the third time in a week and is on course for its highest close since 4 May. Analysts said the attacks were outweighing more positive signals on supply. “Reports of Middle East crude oil exports exceeding pre-conflict levels are more than countered by attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and on its oil infrastructure,” said Tamas Varga of PVM Oil. Morgan Stanley estimated that the region’s crude exports ran at about 17m barrels a day last week, compared with an average of about 18m in the 12 months before the war. Egypt urges diplomacy Against this backdrop, Egypt’s foreign minister said Cairo favoured exploring “every opportunity” to resolve the conflict diplomatically, days before a parliamentary vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. Direct involvement by Egypt’s military, one of the region’s largest, would raise the stakes in a front that is increasingly destabilising the wider war. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Saturday for an urgent parliamentary session on the question, but after a closed meeting on Sunday, lawmakers postponed the vote until October 26 to allow further deliberation. On Saturday, Yahya Ali al-Rai, speaker of the Houthi-run House of Representatives, warned against Egyptian involvement and urged parliament to reject the proposal. “Should Egypt slide down this path, it would pose a grave threat to its own national security and internal stability,” he said. Hormuz attacks Meanwhile, the IRGC said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday. The Iranian forces added that three more vessels collided with mines west of the strait, and warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Warning for pilgrims Separately, Pakistan’s Ministry of Religious Affairs has urged pilgrims to either use Iranian carriers or verify “every Iran-Iraq air sector before departure” when travelling between Iran and Iraq. In a notice, the ministry said it received guidance from the Foreign Office and urged travellers to “use Iranian airlines or plan onward travel between Tehran/Mashad and Najaf” and “verify every Iran-Iraq air sector before departure”. Zaireen group organisers have been instructed to “avoid relying on unconfirmed Iranian connections and to maintain alternative land routes or air arrangements, sufficient contingency funds and accommodation plans in case of cancellations”. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: FIA busts illegal kidney transplant racket in capital; five held
description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has busted an organised gang involved in illegal commercial kidney transplants, arresting five persons, seizing Rs1 million in cash besides freezing properties worth Rs87.5 million and impounding three vehicles. According to a press release issued on Thursday, the FIA, along with Human Organ Transplantation Authority (HOTA), raided a premises in PWD Society, Islamabad, and found that recipient Mohammad Qasim had been transplanted a kidney of donor Ramzan Arshad in violation of law. Three suspects were arrested on the spot while two others were rounded up later. A court granted seven-day physical remand of the suspects. An FIR has been registered under Sections 9, 10 and 11(a)(ii) of the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2010 read with Sections 34, 419 and 109 of Pakistan Penal Code. Investigations said that the recipient had paid Rs3 million in cash for the transplant. Agents arranged the donor. The agents had promised Rs400,000 to the donor, of which Rs340,000 was to be given to the donor and Rs60,000 to be distributed among three agents as commission. The suspects had been performing transplants in residential houses without any medical degree or certificate. Necessary tissue typing, cross-match, PRA and HLA tests were conducted illegally through a hospital by agents. Since these tests are conducted only for HOTA-approved close relatives, the suspects would submit donor samples under names of recipient’s relatives with fake referral letters to make it appear as a relative donor case. Dialysis of recipients was arranged through a technician of a hospital in Islamabad, while in case of deterioration of condition after transplant, the patient was shifted to another hospital. The network consisted of agents, a doctor, nurse, anaesthesia provider, medicine supplier, laboratory test facilitator and dialysis provider. The gang had been operating at private places in PWD Society, Bahria Phase-4 and Peshawar. Investigations further revealed that the suspects had purchased properties in Islamabad from illicit proceeds of illegal transplants. One of them had purchased a 10-marla house in Media Town, Islamabad, for Rs62.5 million, while another purchased a 5-marla house in Jinnah Garden Phase-I, Islamabad, for Rs25 million. Transfer of both properties has been frozen by issuing notices under Section 5 of the FIA Act, 1974. Letters have been sent to all banks for obtaining records of the suspects and separate money laundering proceedings against both were under consideration. During search, Rs1 million cash was recovered and three vehicles — one Changan Oshan X7 and two Honda Civics — were seized and their transfer and registration frozen through the excise office. Teams from HOTA, Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA) and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) inspected the illegal set-up and will submit separate reports. The illegal set-up has been sealed. The operation was conducted on directions of Director FIA Islamabad Zone Syed Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari and under supervision of Deputy Director FIA Anti-Corruption Circle, Islamabad, Faizan Mir. Raids were being conducted at various places for the arrest of the remaining suspects and further investigation was underway. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.60 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.64
Three terrorists killed as forces foil attack in Gwadar
description: GWADAR/QUETTA: Security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar, officials said on Thursday. Security sources said forces had surrounded several other suspected terrorists near a hotel, and an operation was underway to thwart another attempted attack. The construction camp that was targeted by terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan was empty, and no casualties were reported, officials said. However, the attackers set fire to several trucks parked along a nearby road, they added. The state uses the term Fitna al-Hindustan for Balochistan-based terrorist groups, such as the BLA, to highlight Indian involvement in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. Officials denied reports of attacks on security forces, intelligence agencies and their camps, describing information circulating on social media as baseless, and urged the public not to treat unverified reports and claims circulated by terrorist organisations as established facts. Security situation Meanwhile, in a joint statement, the Gwadar administration and police said reports circulating on social media about the security situation were inaccurate. The law and order situation in the BP-250 area and its surroundings was under control following timely action by security forces and relevant intelligence agencies, the statement said. The statement urged the public not to pay heed to unverified reports or spread rumours, advising people to rely on authentic information issued by the police and relevant government institutions. Gwadar police assured residents that necessary measures were being taken to maintain law and order. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, in a post on X, lauded security forces for thwarting the attack and praised their professionalism in eliminating terrorists. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Tensions with Karachi Metropolitan Corporation flare as railways calls in armed personnel from other cities
description: • PR police say step taken to protect federal assets following ‘recent incidents’ • Both sides have already lodged cases against each other over scuffle between city wardens and PR policemen KARACHI: In a clear sign of further escalation of tensions between the KMC and Pakistan Railways, the federal institution has called in additional forces from different parts of the country “equipped with arms and ammunition” to protect its assets and key points in Karachi, warning that it will respond with “full force” if any individual or institution challenges its authority. The dispute is the KMC’s Rs780 million road construction project linking Natha Khan Bridge with Pehlwan Goth, as both the federal and municipal authorities claim ownership of the land. The two sides have already lodged cases against each other, accusing one another of serious offences, including terrorism and kidnapping, while senior officials of both institutions have vowed that they would not back down from their respective positions. On Sunday the railways police stopped the construction of the dual carriageway between Natha Khan Bridge and Pehlwan Goth and Habib University, running parallel to Chakor Nullah. The railways maintained that the project encroaches on the land belonging to the Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) and that the construction was without authorisation. A scuffle had also broken out when KMC City Wardens Dire­ctor Saim Imran arrived at the scene, followed by heated arguments between the two sides. The KMC alleged PR policemen assaulted the City Wardens director before taking him to the railways police station. Although the City Wardens director was released after hours of talks between the two sides, the KMC high-ups moved the Sharea Faisal police to lodge an FIR against the PR police officials for kidnapping and assaulting their officer. The matter did not end there, piles of garbage were found the next day outside the PR offices and the residence of one of its senior officials, raising suspicions among the officials that the waste had been dumped by the municipal body’s officials. Later on, a heavy contingent of Sharea Faisal police “raided” the Cantonment Railway Station to arrest suspects allegedly involved in the “kidnapping, torture and illegal confinement” of the KMC City Wardens director. In a tit-for-tat move, the railways lodged an FIR against KMC officials later in the evening, accusing them of offences including terrorism. In a fresh move, Pakistan Railways has decided to call in additional personnel from Sukkur and Multan for deployment in Karachi. It already has a force of more than 500 personnel in the city. In separate letters to senior Pakistan Railways police officials in the two cities, the department has asked them to release a certain number of personnel “along with arms and ammunition” for deployment in Karachi. When contacted, SP Pakistan Railways Police Karachi Khurram Khursheed confirmed the move, saying that the additional force had been called in as a “precautionary measure” following “recent incidents”, including an attack on a railway police station and the dumping of garbage outside railway offices and the residence of one of its senior officials. “The railway police force is usually deployed on trains, at stations, key points, Pakistan Railways offices and the residences of senior officials,” he told Dawn. “The additional personnel will join the existing force to strengthen security. Under its mandate, the railway police are responsible for protecting Pakistan Railways’ assets and key points. We hope the additional deployment will help the force perform its duties more effectively.” Meanwhile, the KMC has continued work on the Natha Khan-Pehalwan Goth road to complete it by the end of this month. “The work was temporarily halted when Pakistan Railways police intervened but it resumed the very next day,” a KMC official said. “Talks between senior officials of the two sides are ongoing but the issue remains unresolved. Pakistan Railways insists that the land belongs to it while the KMC is determined to complete the project without interruption. The KMC has fulfilled all legal requirements before launching the project more than two months ago. This is a major project that will benefit the people and any attempt to undermine its potential or put it at risk would be detrimental to the interests of Karachi’s residents.” Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: National Assembly proceedings succumb to lack of quorum, again
description: • CDA only demolishing illegal structures in Islamabad, assembly told • MNA raises concern over non-rehabilitation of Malir families displaced by ML-1 project • Lower house amends law to make State Life Insurance Company a statutory body ISLAMABAD: Proceedings in the National Assembly remained sluggish on Thursday, with only one bill passed before a lack of quorum forced the presiding officer to adjourn the sitting until Friday morning. The NA’s agenda for Thursday comprised 16 items, but the sitting was adjourned midway after a PTI MNA pointed out the lack of quorum. A headcount confirmed that the required number of members was not present. Abdul Qadir Patel, who was presiding over the sitting, allowed some additional time for the quorum to be completed, but the number of MNAs present remained below the required 88. The House was subsequently adjourned until Friday morning. During the question hour, the demolition of houses and other struc­tures in Islamabad, particularly in Sector E-12, came under discussion. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said the Capital Development Authority (CDA) had demolished only illegally constructed structures and houses. He said the shortage of graveyards was one of the major problems facing the city’s administration and residents. Most private housing schemes and societies, he added, had converted plots reserved for graveyards, schools, parks and mosques into commercial properties. Responding to a question, Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi informed the House that Pakistan Railways had recovered more than 200,000 kanals of land previously occupied through encroachments. Regarding the Main Line-1 (ML-1) railway project, he said Prime Min­ister Shehbaz Sharif would inau­gurate its first phase, involving the laying of 480 kilometres of railway track between Rohri and Karachi, at an estimated cost of $2.5 billion. MNA Syed Rafiullah said several families in Karachi’s Malir area had been rendered homeless by the ML-1 project, but had yet to be rehabilitated. During a question concerning facilities for Haj pilgrims, PTI MNA Shehryar Afridi expre­ssed displeasure when Parliamentary Secre­tary Kesoo Mal Kheal Das responded to the query. “It would have been better if a responsible member of the treasury benches or the minister for parliamentary affairs had answered the question,” Mr Afridi said. Mr Das responded by pointing out that a Hindu minister in India also handled Haj affairs, questioning Mr Afridi’s suggestion that the matter required a more responsible person to address it. Mr Afridi also said some private Haj organisers had made the religious obligation prohibitively exp­en­sive, with packages costing bet­ween Rs4 million and Rs5m. State Life Insurance Company After Question Hour, the National Assembly passed the Life Insurance (Nation­alisation) (Amend­ment) Bill, 2026. The bill provides for the federal government to establish a company, to be known as State Life Insurance Company Limited, under the Companies Act, 2017 (XIX of 2017). It states that the appointment of the company’s chief executive officer and board of directors will be made in accordance with the State-Owned Enterprises (SOE) Act and the Companies Act, 2017. Following the company’s incorporation under the Companies Act, 2017, the federal government will issue a vesting order, to be published in the official gazette, transferring all assets, liabilities, contracts, policies, proceedings and undertakings of the existing corporation to the company on a specified date and under terms and conditions determined by the government. The corporation will stand dissolved on the effective date, according to the bill. The legislation further provides that all employees and officers who have served the corporation continuously for at least one year immediately before the effective date, excluding those employed under project contracts, will be transferred to the new company on the same terms and conditions of service. Their existing rights and privileges, including pension entitleme­nts, post-retirement medical benefits, provident fund and gratuity, will also be protected, the bill states. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Landslide leaves thousands stranded on Baltistan Road
description: Passengers cross a road blocked by boulders in the Shangus area of Skardu’s Roundu Valley.—Dawn • GBDMA warns against travel as road to remain closed • Residents call for safety measures on thoroughfare GILGIT: The Baltistan Road was blocked by landslides near Shangus in Skardu’s Roundu Valley on Thursday morning, leaving thousands of passengers, including tourists, stranded on both sides. Local residents have expressed concern over the failure to implement safety measures on the road, which is frequently blocked by landslides and has witnessed numerous fatal accidents. According to a statement issued by the Gilgit-Baltistan Disaster Management Authority (GBDMA), the road was completely blocked and traffic suspended. The authority said debris continued to slide at the site, while large boulders obstructing the road could not be removed using machinery and required blasting. The GBDMA said the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) was mobilising a blasting team to clear the debris. It advised tourists and the general public to avoid non-essential travel on the road, which would remain closed to traffic at least until today (Friday). It also warned people against attempting to cross the landslide zone due to the high risk of further sliding. “The public and travellers are advised to avoid unnecessary travel and contact the police helpline at 15 before setting out to obtain the latest information about road conditions,” the statement said. The 167-kilometre Juglot-Skardu Road, renamed the Baltistan Road, runs along the Indus River and is considered one of the most dangerous mountain routes in the region. Residents of four districts — Skardu, Kharmang, Shigar and Ghanche — depend on it to access other areas. The reconstructed road was inaugurated in 2021. Frequent landslides, a lack of roadside safety barriers and warning signs, inadequate safety instructions and limited telecommunications facilities at checkpoints have added to the risks for motorists. Local residents have repeatedly complained about the failure to introduce adequate safety measures during the road’s reconstruction and alleged that the original project design was not implemented. Residents said several stretches featured sharp turns and were prone to landslides, making them particularly hazardous. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Residents write to CM Murad, urge halt to construction on Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam
description: KARACHI: The Clifton Neighbourhood Association (CNA) on Thursday wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, expressing concerns over construction at Nehr-i-Khayyam and calling for the complete project report, approved engineering drawings, details of the engineering firm and responsible engineers, and the PC-I, including the project scope, cost and approvals, to be made publicly available. Comprising mostly residents of Clifton Block 5, the CNA questioned the Nehr-i-Khayyam rehabilitation plan and demanded an immediate halt to the construction of the concrete box drain, which it described as an encroachment. Speaking to Dawn, Rasha Tarek, one of the residents, said the construction work was being carried out very quickly. “They are working at night, too.” Earlier, following protests at Nehr-i-Khayyam for two consecutive Sundays by the residents, a meeting with them and project representatives, including a project engineer, a representative of People and Nature Initiative (PANI) and members of Shahid Abdullah’s team, who are a major part of the transformation and rehabilitation at Nehr-i-Khayyam, was convened by the adviser to the CM Syed Najmi Alam at Dr Fareeduddin Sethna Family Park on Wednesday. Clifton Neighbourhood Association seeks disclosure of project documents, an independent drainage study and EIA; demands restoration of waterway to its original width At the meeting, the residents again raised their objections and sought answers from the project representatives. They demanded to see the proposed design of the project, particularly the apparent narrowing of the waterway and the potential implications for stormwater drainage, tidal connectivity, flood risk and the surrounding environment. They expressed dissatisfaction with the incomplete plans presented to them during the meeting and stated that the information provided to them was insufficient to assess the project’s technical and environmental implications. They called for the complete project report, approved engineering drawings, details of the engineering firm and responsible engineers, and the PC-I, including the project scope, cost and approvals, to be made publicly available. Questions were also raised about the proposed treatment plant, including its role in the overall project and the arrangements for its implementation and funding. Shahid Abdullah’s team acknowledged that funding was not available for the project component under discussion. Resid­ents called for clarity on which components were funded, which remained unfunded and how the project was intended to be completed. A representative of PANI stated that the organisation had no involvement in the construction of the drains currently being built. This prompted further questions about which agencies were responsible for the drainage works and how these works related to the wider rehabilitation project. When the issue of an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was raised, project representatives stated that an EIA had not been conducted and that they would look into the matter. Residents stressed that a project involving proposed changes to a major urban waterway must be supported by a proper environmental assessment, independent technical studies and transparent public consultation before any irreversible changes are made. Syed Najmi Alam assured the residents that their demands would be forwarded to the chief minister. He also stated that the CM had asked him to submit a report following the residents’ protests. He further promised that the construction debris causing inconvenience in the neigh­bourhood would be removed within a week. In the letter to the CM, the CNA put forward seven demands, including an immediate halt to construction and encroachment at Nehr-i-Khayyam and the restoration of its original width. It also called for a comprehensive EIA to be conducted and made publicly available, along with the disclosure of all project documents. The association also demanded an independent hydrological and drainage study, opposed the commercialisation of Nehr-i-Khayyam land, and called for no part of the waterway to be covered or any structure to be raised above its level. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Fissures take a toll on PTI internal discipline
description: • Gohar rejects resignation after Firdous Naqvi steps down from additional secretary general post • Mashal Yousafzai quits party WhatsApp groups over disagreements with top leadership ISLAMABAD: PTI’s Additional Secretary General Firdous Shamim Naqvi resigned from his position, while its outspoken senator Mashal Yousafzai quit the party’s WhatsApp groups over disagreements with the top leadership. The PTI, however, did not accept the resignation of Mr Naqvi and reportedly managed to convince the veteran member to withdraw his resignation. Ms Yousafzai, however, had a heated exchange with PTI interim chief Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, which led to her quitting the WhatsApp groups. A source told Dawn that Senator Yousafzai was among the party leaders who expressed a lack of trust in the PTI leadership over its failure to secure the release of Imran Khan. She did so at a recent meeting of the core committee that spanned two days. On Thursday, she raised this issue once again. “Barrister Gohar threatened her that she may be expelled from the group. Over this Mashal Yousaf­zai said that she will quit the party groups and subsequently left WhatsApp groups of the parliamentary party and the core committee,” the source said. On the other hand, Barrister Gohar rejected Mr Naqvi’s resignation. Firdous Shamim Naqvi is an elected representative of the PTI with the authority to issue official notifications. “It was nothing but a disaster for the party…. Although Secretary General Salman Akram Raja has issued some of the notifications, those notifications cannot be accepted by the Election Commission of Pakistan, as the election watchdog had rejected the [intra-party] elections of the PTI and a case is going on in the Lahore High Court,” he explained. PTI leader Sheikh Waqas Akram said Mr Naqvi had resigned, but Barrister Gohar rejected his resignation. “I hope that situation will be controlled as he [Firdous Shamim Naqvi] has not left any Whatsapp group of the party,” he added. About Senator Yousafzai, he said the PTI senator left the groups “in the heat of the moment”, and hopefully the situation would be resolved soon. PTI workers arrested Police arrested three PTI supporters outside the Adiala jail after they arrived with their leaders to meet Imran Khan. Advocate Awais Younas Chaudhry told Dawn that Sardar Sadaqat Hayat, Muhammad Bilal Khan, Malik Asif Mehmood Kashif, Jaleel Shah, Malik Haris Awan and Nadia Khattak were included in the list for meeting with Mr Khan on Thursday. “Eleven of them, along with some workers, reached the Adiala jail, but the administration did not let them meet Imran Khan,” he said, adding that Malik Haris Awan and two workers Ali Raza and Umer Baig were later detained by the police. “I have informed the police that there was no case against Haris Awan and he had come to Adiala as per the directions of the Islamabad High Court, but the police are not willing to release them,” Advocate Chaudhry claimed. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: 'Generational rage': Young Europeans fight to be heard
description: From blockaded schools in Rome to tent camps in Madrid and street protests in France, young people across Europe are turning their anger on a political class they say is not listening. Their demands vary, but they are united in wanting to make their often marginalised voices heard, sometimes even with radical methods in the face of heavy-handed policing. “We are fighting and taking our future in our hands,” said Damiano Fusa, 18, a student at Rome’s Cavour high school, the first to be occupied in a wave of student takeovers that has spread across the Italian capital. “We’re not represented by anyone,” Fusa told AFP, criticising both Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s hard-right coalition and previous centre-left governments for cutting education funding and ignoring young people’s needs. Protesters and students from art and culture schools block the entrance to the Louvre Museum during a demonstration in support of a high school student movement demanding better school conditions and government action, in Paris, France, October 19, 2026. — Reuters Hundreds of thousands of high school and university students have rallied in France, Italy, Spain and other European countries in recent weeks, with some protests descending into violence. Governments have largely focused on restoring order, with France imposing partial curfews and Italy deploying soldiers, responses protesters say obscure their demands and could make things even worse. “Politicians are responding in ways that are completely disconnected from reality, completely absurd,” said Luis Marques, a 19-year-old psychology student in Lisbon. Students are demanding action on soaring rents, more spending on education instead of defence and more job opportunities for young people. But experts say the unrest reflects a broader sense among many young Europeans that they have been shut out of politics and sidelined. “These young people do not just feel like they do not have a place in politics, they feel they are not being heard at all,” said Geoffrey Pleyers, president of the International Sociological Association. Rosario Forlenza, a professor at Rome’s Luiss University, called it a “European generational revolt” rooted in a social and economic crisis “to which politicians cannot give a substantive response”. “Young people are a minority of the population that is shrinking and so their social, economic, cultural, political and electoral weight is becoming ever more irrelevant,” he said. ‘Inspiring other people’ The anger has been particularly palpable in France and Italy, where fresh demonstrations are planned for Saturday. “People are very angry, they’ve had enough. Working hard all day and still not being able to fill up their shopping cart,” a 20-year-old student who gave his name as Eddy told AFP at a protest in Bordeaux last weekend. “Will smashing everything change anything? I think it can be a jolt to wake up the politicians. We don’t know what else to do to make ourselves heard. The ballot box? We don’t believe in it anymore,” he said. Firefighters extinguish a fire in a bar during a demonstration in Paris against the high cost of living. Police estimated nearly 200,000 people took part in protests across France, while organisers claimed a turnout of almost 800,000.—AFP Protest movements across Europe are increasingly drawing inspiration from one another, and even looking to youth-led movements further afield in places like Bangladesh, India and Nepal. In Italy, one student slogan last week urged protesters to “do as in France”, while shared symbols, including the Jolly Roger pirate flag, have become common across youth rallies. Marcos Navarro, 22, a laboratory quality-control technician from Madrid, said protesters across Europe were meeting to share tactics. “They’ve come to ask us: ‘How did you do it? How do you organise yourselves?’ We’ve already exchanged ideas,” said Navarro, who has been camping with hundreds of others in Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol square since September to protest housing costs and evictions. Ayla Herrero, a 26-year-old anthropologist helping at the camp’s infirmary, said it was “inspiring for us to know that we’re inspiring other people, that it doesn’t just stay here”. ‘Not acceptable’ Concern about the rise in military spending in Europe following the Russian invasion of Ukraine has also been a rallying point. Nikos Mavroudis, a 17-year-old high school student in Athens’ Exarchia neighbourhood, said the money could be better spent on his school, where chunks of plaster are falling. “It’s not acceptable for classrooms to be dangerous,” said Mavroudis, who hopes to become a cook and plans to move elsewhere in Europe to “countries where things are better”. Protesting students gather and hold placards as they carry out a blockading action at the Turgot secondary school, in Paris, on October 5, 2026. — AFP At Rome’s occupied Morgagni high school, where students have barricaded entrances with desks, protesters pointed to the crumbling infrastructure as evidence of neglect. An 18-year-old, who did not want to be named, said the media and politicians in Italy were focusing too heavily on looting and vandalism by some protesters. “It turns hatred against the students who are victims of this system,” he said. Asked about the violence, Sabrina Brizzola, 24, coordinator of the Italian University Students’ Union, said organisations like hers should “organise and channel this generational rage”. “We have shared concerns, even if our ways of protesting differ,” she said.

title: How are Ukraine strikes, Mideast war driving US fuel prices?
description: Ahead of next month’s midterm US elections, Donald Trump has increasingly blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for surging energy prices back home, which are causing the president political headaches. However, analysts say the main driver of higher fuel prices remains the US–Iran war. Which Russian sites have been targeted? Ukraine has intensified its drone attacks on Russia’s energy industry over the past 18 months, seeking to cut the Kremlin’s revenues and undermine its ability to finance the war. The strikes have targeted “mostly refineries”, Julien Mathonniere, an economist at Energy Intelligence, told AFP. On average, one Russian refinery was hit every three days during the first eight months of the year, according to the International Energy Agency. “Russia’s net diesel exports fell by approximately 80 per cent year on year in the third quarter of 2026, from around 1.05 million barrels per day to just 200,000 barrels per day,” said Viktor Kurilov, an analyst at Rystad Energy. In response to the disruption in domestic fuel supplies, Moscow introduced a ban on diesel exports from July until the end of October. Why does this concern Trump? Trump has repeatedly condemned the attacks on Russian refineries, saying Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky disobeyed his orders to halt the strikes. By contrast, Trump has not commented on the intensification in recent months of Russian strikes against Ukrainian territory, which have caused a surge in civilian casualties. Trump’s frustrations come as the Republicans face dim prospects in the November midterm elections, partly because of soaring fuel prices. US diesel prices at the pump climbed to a record of $6.53 per gallon at the end of September, up from $3.75 per gallon before the war, according to the American Automobile Association. Energy price rises are also fuelling inflation across the economy. What is the Mideast role? Ukraine’s strikes explain “about one-third of the global diesel shortfall, currently estimated at 1.7 to 1.8m barrels per day”, said Mathonniere. But “the impact of previous drone strikes (by Kyiv) on global product prices before the Middle East crisis was minimal”, James Henderson, a researcher at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, told AFP. Energy exports from the Gulf have plunged since US-Israeli strikes on Iran from February caused Tehran to respond by choking off the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for oil and gas transit. At the same time, maritime freight costs have soared and major refining capacity in the Middle East has been hit, adding to upward pressure on oil prices. Can prices fall before midterms? Relations between Kyiv and Washington soured further this month after Trump announced a controversial agreement with Moscow to lift certain sanctions and allow Russian diesel imports, supposedly to ease prices. The US president said Wednesday that he believed an end to the Russia-Ukraine war could be closer than ever, as the Kremlin said it was willing to restart trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington next month. For now, however, the strikes continue. “There’s not much that can be done in the very short term to lower diesel prices,” said Jorge Leon, an analyst at Rystad Energy. Even if the Russia conflict ended or an energy ceasefire was reached, the impact “wouldn’t really move the needle massively for the US midterm elections”, he added. Repairs to damaged infrastructure take time, while continued hostilities in the Middle East drive energy prices higher.

title: Pakistan, EU flag security risks tied to Afghanistan
description: • At annual counterterrorism dialogue, bloc slams recent attacks in Pakistan • Talks cover online extremism, terror financing • Both sides agree to boost cooperation at multilateral forums • FO cites exploitation of water resources by states, terrorists ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and the European Union on Thursday expressed shared concern over the security threat emanating from Afghanistan at their annual counterterrorism dialogue. “Pakistan and the EU expressed concern at the security implications of the situation in Afghanistan”, both Pakistan and EU said in their statements on the 10th round of the Pakistan-EU bilateral counterterrorism dialogue in Islamabad, where the two sides reviewed the evolving terrorism threat landscape and reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms. The Afghanistan reference in the statement followed more explicit language in the joint communiqué issued after the eighth Pakistan-EU Stra­tegic Dialogue in Islamabad on June 1. In that statement, the two sides had expressed “serious concern over the presence of terrorist entities in Afghanistan”, and said that Afghan territory must not be used to threaten or attack other countries, besides calling on the Afghan de facto authorities to take “effective and verifiable action” against all terrorist groups operating in or from Afghanistan. Although the statements after the counterterrorism dialogue did not repeat those specific demands, its significance lies in the fact that Afghanistan-related security concerns were again acknowledged and this time in the dedicated counterterrorism dialogue, rather than as part of a wider discussion of political and regional affairs. The reference is, moreover, significant because Pakistan has repeatedly urged international partners to press Afgha­nistan’s Taliban authorities to prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan territory to launch attacks across the border. The renewed emphasis on Afgha­nistan also follows recent EU engagement with the Taliban authorities. During a visit to Kabul from Oct 12 to 14, EU Special Envoy for Afghanistan Thomas Frellesen expressed concern over the continued presence and cross-border activities of terrorist groups with regional and global reach and urged the Taliban authorities to prevent Afg­han territory from being used by terrorist groups to threaten other countries. Even though the statements after counterterrorism dialogue and the strategic dialogue did not name any specific terrorist group of concern, Pakistan has consistently identified the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and affiliated groups and Baloch separatist outfits based in Afghanistan as the main threat. Islamabad has repeatedly deman­ded verifiable action by the Taliban authorities to neutralise these groups and prevent such attacks. The language used in EU statements, while expressing concern on the terrorism threat from Afghanistan, indicates continuity with the latest dialogue reaffirming common ground between the two sides on the security risks associated with Afghanistan. The discussions also covered evolving terrorist threats, including the exploitation of cyberspace, information and energy resources. Pakistan and the EU, the statements noted, exchanged best practices on preventing and countering violent extremism, terrorist financing and radicalisation, with particular attention to the use of cyberspace by terrorists. In a post on X, the Foreign Office said the dialogue also explored cooperation to counter the exploitation of water resources, besides other reso­urces, by terrorists as well as by states. The references to water resources and state actors did not appear in the separate official statements issued by Pakistan and the EU. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
description: Turkiye will host an R-4 and an R-4+E-3 meeting of foreign ministers in Istanbul on October 23, the Turkish foreign ministry said on Thursday. The R-4 group, which comprises Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.
