title: Court approves Rs20m plea bargain of contractor in Kohistan graft case
description: PESHAWAR: An accountability court here on Friday approved the Rs20 million plea bargain of an accused in the high-profile case involving the alleged embezzlement of over Rs37 billion from the bank accounts of the Upper Kohistan district accounts office. Judge Mohammad Zafar ordered that accused Saifullah, a private contractor, be released if his custody was not required in any other case. He added that the accused had been discharged from his liability and disqualified from holding any public office under Section 15 of the National Accountability Ordinance, 1999. The judge observed that the accused had acknowledged that his plea bargain agreement with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) had been entered into with his full consent and of his own free will, without any duress, coercion or pressure. Orders his release if custody not required in any other case He pointed out that during the plea bargain proceedings, the accused paid the total liability of Rs20 million on Sept 11, 2026, through two pay orders. In his statement, the accused, a resident of Dasu, Upper Kohistan, acknowledged that he had acted as a contractor in the scam through his sole proprietorship, Kohistan and Company, and had fraudulently operated the company’s bank account. He added that he didn’t carry out any civil work through the company, which was established solely to encash illegal payments through fraudulent means. NAB special prosecutor Manik Shah appeared before the court along with investigation officer SP Inayatullah. The officials submitted an application under Section 25(b), read with Section 15 of the National Accountability Ordinance, 1999, seeking approval of the accused’s plea bargain in the ongoing investigation into embezzlement and misappropriation in the case. They said that the matter uncovered by NAB involved the active collusion of the accused with other co-accused, including officials of the Communication and Works Department in Upper Kohistan, the District Accounts Office Upper Kohistan, employees of the National Bank of Pakistan’s Dasu branch and several private contractors. The officials said that the accused had misappropriated funds from various projects through bogus withdrawals from the national treasury in the names of contractors who had not executed any civil works. They said that the accused, who was in judicial custody, had filed an application seeking a plea bargain with NAB. The officials said thatthe plea bargain had been approved by the NAB chairman on Oct 14, 2026. Until now, the NAB’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chapter has arrested around 40 accused in the case. It claims that it received a source report on April 8, 2025, revealing a massive financial scandal in Upper Kohistan involving the illegal withdrawal and misappropriation of over Rs37 billion from the contractor’s security deposit head of bank account G-10113. It added that the report implicated a network of government officials, bank employees and private contractors in a carefully orchestrated conspiracy that exploited systemic vulnerabilities and violated the Accounting Policies and Procedures Manual. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: JI protests power outages, inflation in KP
description: CHARSADDA: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) staged a protest at Farooq Azam Chowk here on Friday against the petroleum levy, rising inflation, prolonged power outages, farmers’ problems and alleged corruption, demanding immediate relief for the public and measures to address issues confronting the agriculture sector. The protesters warned that if prolonged power outages were not addressed, the party would expand its protest campaign and stage sit-ins outside the relevant government offices. Addressing the demonstration, JI Khyber Pakhtunkhwa deputy general secretary Sohail Ahmad, Charsadda district emir Shah Hussain Advocate, general secretary Fawad Ahmad, District Bar Association president Mujeebur Rehman Advocate, Haroon Khan, Sajjad Ahmad and Abdul Malik rejected the petroleum levy, describing it as an additional financial burden on the people. They said a protest campaign against the levy had been under way for the past three to four months under the leadership of JI emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, as rising inflation had severely eroded the purchasing power of ordinary citizens. The speakers claimed that the country was burdened with Rs999 billion in debt and that every Pakistani owed approximately Rs400,000. They said even newborn babies were burdened with the country’s liabilities. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: ‘Ghost’ employees in Dir, Bajaur health, education depts face action
description: LOWER DIR/BAJAUR: Malakand division commissioner Iqbal Hussain Bacha has ordered strict action against ‘ghost’ employees and absentee staff in the education and health departments, prompting the Lower Dir education authorities to direct school heads to verify staff attendance and cancel unauthorised and need-based transfers. District education officer Mushtaq Ahmad on Friday issued a notification to all male and female principals, deputy district education officers and assistant sub-divisional education officers (ASDEOs) in Lower Dir to immediately cancel staff detailing and need-based transfers. The order warned of departmental action against heads who failed to comply. The directives follow a meeting chaired by the divisional commissioner and attended by deputy commissioners, additional deputy commissioners, district education officers, medical superintendents, district health officers and heads of educational monitoring bodies from across Malakand division. Cancellation of unauthorised, need-based transfers also ordered According to sources privy to the development, the commissioner said nearly 70pc of the provincial government’s budget was spent on education and health, stressing the need for a results-oriented approach to ensure that public spending translated into better services. He announced a zero-tolerance policy towards teacher absenteeism and ‘ghost’ employees, making school principals personally responsible for ensuring daily attendance. If a principal failed to take action against an absent teacher, the relevant ASDEO would be required to initiate departmental proceedings against the principal. The commissioner also directed ASDEOs to conduct regular field visits and monitor schools instead of remaining in their offices. To strengthen accountability, principals have been directed to submit certificates confirming that no ‘ghost’ employee is working at their schools. Deputy district education officers will also submit daily attendance and monitoring reports to their respective district education officers to enable prompt action against irregularities. In Bajaur, authorities have decided to take strict action against ‘ghost’ employees and those not attending to their duties for a long time in the education and health departments, sources said on Friday. They said the decision was taken in light of instructions issued by deputy commissioner Adnan Farid Afridi to the heads of both departments a day earlier. According to sources, the deputy commissioner took serious notice of reports that several employees in both departments were either long-term absentees or non-existent and directed their heads to take legal action against them. A source privy to the development told Dawn that both departments have begun compiling lists of ‘ghost’ employees and those absent from duty. The sources said most of the ‘ghost’ and absentee staff were lower-grade employees and teachers, and a majority of them belonged to influential families. There was no record immediately available showing the exact number of ‘ghost’ and long-term absentee employees, the source added. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Peshawar High Court stops NCCIA from issuing final appointment orders to fill its posts
description: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court has stopped the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) from issuing final appointment orders to fill its different positions. However, the NCCIA was allowed by Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Mohammad Faheem Wali to continue with the recruitment process. The bench issued notices to the respondents, including the directors general of the NCCIA and Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and secretaries of the interior, establishment and finance divisions, seeking their comments within a fortnight on a petition filed by eight NCCIA employees for the completion of their regularisation process prior to any new recruitments. The petitioners include Sub-Inspector Mukhtar Ahmad and seven other contractual employees. Allows investigation agency to continue with recruitment process They requested the court to declare that the case of their regularisation, being already pending before the competent authority, was liable to be considered and decided in accordance with law, prior to undertaking or finalising any fresh appointment against the posts in question. The petitioners sought orders for the continuation of the recruitment process initiated pursuant to an advertisement of Aug 23, 2026, overlapped with or prejudiced the petitioners pending claim for regularisation, to be unlawful, arbitrary and without lawful authority. They requested the court to ask respondents to decide their pending cases of regularisation within a time-bound period, and thereafter proceed with any fresh recruitment, if otherwise warranted, strictly in accordance with law. The petitioners said that any appointment made in derogation of the petitioners pending regularisation claim should remain subject to the final determination of the petitioners’ rights and should not prejudice or adversely affect their seniority or consequential service benefits. The counsel for petitioners, Mian Mohammad Imran, said that the petitioners were initially appointed on a contractual basis and had received extensions from time to time. He said that in view of their experience, the petitioners’ cases had been referred for regularisation and a selection committee had also been constituted. The lawyer, however, said that the posts occupied by them were subsequently advertised for recruitment in Aug 2026. He added that similarly placed employees also approached the Lahore High Court by filing a petition wherein comments had been called and interim relief had also been granted. Mr Imran said that the NCCIA was a specialised agency established by the federal government in 2025 to investigate cyber-crimes within the country. He said that the NCCIA replaced the FIA’s Cyber-Crimes Wing and was set up under the Prevention of Cyber Crimes Act, 2016, with the wing’s posts along with resources transferred to the agency. The lawyer contended that though the petitioners’ initial engagement was described as contractual, the substantive character of their employment had, with the passage of time and in view of the continuing nature of the functions performed by them, ceased to bear the attributes of a genuinely temporary engagement. He argued that through official communication on Jul 2, 2026, addressed to the ministry of interior, it was informed that the DG NCCIA being head of the department proposed to constitute the Departmental Selection Committee for the regularisation purposes of the petitioners along with other employees and the petitioners case received express recognition from the department itself. Mr Imran said the NCCIA declared in that communication that it intended to regularise the services of 216 officers from BPS-1 to BPS-14 presently working on the contractual basis against sanctioned regular posts. The lawyer contended that despite the pendency of the regularisation process of the petitioners and other employees, the government issued the impugned advertisement for fresh recruitment against a number of posts. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Three new dengue cases reported in Rawalpindi, take season’s tally to 70
description: RAWALPINDI: Three more dengue patients arrived in government hospitals in the city on Friday, taking the tally of cases in the last two months to 70. “Total three patients’ reports confirmed suffering from dengue virus on Friday. Only nine patients are admitted in the hospital’s dengue ward,” said Dr Jawad, District Health Officer Preventive. He said that in the last 24 hours, dengue serology reports of three new patients were received confirming that they were suffering from the mosquito-borne disease. “We have sped up the anti-dengue campaign in the areas from where patients have arrived.” He said one patient arrived from the city area, the second from Union Council Qazian and the third from Asghar Mall. District emergency and response committee directs immediate strengthening of field surveillance “In October so far, 37 cases have been reported while 27 had been reported in September and no case emerged in August,” he said. Meanwhile, the District Emergency and Response Committee for Dengue Control directed the immediate strengthening of field surveillance. A meeting of the committee was held at the Deputy Commissioner Complex chaired by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Social Services) Fazail Mudassar. The meeting was attended by the CEO (health), officials from relevant departments and area in-charges. Participants reviewed the current dengue situation across the district, patient screening, larvae surveillance, field activities, monitoring of hotspots and dengue response reports. During the briefing, it was stated that as of October 23 evening, 70 cases of dengue had been confirmed in Rawalpindi district, a figure significantly lower than in previous years, while a total of 5,446 suspected cases were identified during patient screening. Indoor and outdoor surveillance activities remain ongoing across the district to curb the spread of dengue and to ensure the timely detection and elimination of larvae. According to the briefing, more than 5.683 million homes have been checked across the district so far this year, and approximately 1.963 million other locations have been inspected. Upon the detection of larvae during surveillance, anti-dengue measures were implemented at the respective locations to curb mosquito breeding. The meeting also reviewed the progress of response activities related to dengue larvae, conducted between October 12 and 23. It was reported that out of a total of 14,247 planned response activities, 14,206 had been completed. Relevant departments were directed to promptly finalise any pending actions and to ensure the timely completion and effective monitoring of all activities. Furthermore, the meeting reviewed surveillance efforts around identified hotspots, sanitation drives in vulnerable union councils, cleaning of graveyards and open spaces, desilting of drains and public awareness campaigns. The additional deputy commissioner stressed the need for effective coordination and a unified strategy among all relevant departments. He added that no negligence should be shown in surveillance or field activities, and that all pending response tasks must be completed within the stipulated timeframe. During the meeting, an appeal was made to citizens to ensure that water will not accumulate in their homes, on rooftops, in flower pots, or any other locations. They were urged to maintain proper cleanliness and to cooperate with the administration by adopting preventive measures against dengue. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Rain, winds bring temperatures down in twin cities
description: RAWALPINDI: Gusty winds and rain in different parts of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad brought down the temperature. title: Rawalpindi’s unauthorised schools get one week to get registered
description: RAWALPINDI: District Registration Authority of schools on Friday asked private educational institutions in Rawalpindi to get themselves registered within a week, and if they failed, the unregistered premises will be sealed. The decision was taken at a meeting of the District Registration Authority, Rawalpindi, held under the chairmanship of additional deputy commissioner (Social Services) Fazail Mudassar. The meeting addressed various matters, including the registration of unregistered private educational institutions, compliance with legal requirements, and safety audits of educational facilities. It was decided that the unregistered private educational institutions would be granted a one-week window to submit the necessary documentation for registration and fulfill all legal requirements. District Registration Authority warns premises will be sealed in case of non-compliance Institutions that fail to complete the registration process within this deadline will face enforcement action, including the sealing of their premises. During the meeting, registration applications for 35 newly established private educational institutions were presented for approval. One application was rejected due to incomplete documentation, while the registration of the remaining 34 institutions was made conditional upon the submission of IT and Science Lab certificates, which was made mandatory by the district registration committees. The meeting also authorised the imposition of fines on educational institutions that violated government directives during the summer vacation period. Furthermore, it was decided that a third-party evaluation would be conducted to assess the structural integrity of private educational institution buildings. For this purpose, a committee has been constituted under the supervision of the additional deputy commissioner (Social Services), comprising the CEO (Education), the executive engineer (Buildings), and the Deputy Director (Development). The meeting was attended by District Education Authority Chief Executive Officer Yasin Khan Baloch, Member of the District Registration Authority Abrar Ahmed Khan, representing the District Monitoring wing Muhammad Imran and Waqas Akhtar, In-charge of the DRA branch, along with Sohail Ahmed from Private Schools. District Education Authority Chief Executive Officer Yasin Khan Baloch told Dawn after the meeting that the education authority was conducting the survey of 7,000 private schools and 1,300 government-run schools in the district for the safety measures and dangerous building. “It completed survey of 5,000 schools and 300 private schools and 143 government run schools had been asked to complete the safety measures within a week time. The survey will complete within one week and action against those institutions will be initiated who failed to complete the safety measures to avoid any untoward situation,” he said. During the proceedings, Javed Khan, Member of the District Registration Authority, Rawalpindi, expressed concern regarding the issuance of notices—by certain officials of the Tehsil Municipal Administration—demanding the commercialisation of building premises while safety audits of private educational institutions were underway. He urged the additional deputy commissioner (Social Services) to take immediate cognizance of the matter and direct the officials concernedto halt such actions, thereby ensuring that private educational institutions can complete their safety audits without hindrance and proceed with fulfilling the necessary legal requirements. Abrar Ahmed Khan emphasised the necessity of ensuring the registration of all unregistered educational institutions. He further noted that achieving this requires clear guidelines, a defined timeframe, and effective coordination among the relevant departments, enabling educational institutions to complete both their registration and safety audits within the stipulated period. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Naqvi highlights staff shortage at NCCIA
description: LAHORE:  Acute shortage of staff in the newly-formed National Cyber Crime  Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has forced Federal Interior Minister Mohsin  Naqvi to seek Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s help in addressing the  matter. Expressing concern at the growing number of cybercrime  cases, Mr Naqvi said on Friday that the NCCIA was struggling to cope  with the workload because of a “severe shortage of investigators”. Talking  to journalists at the NCCIA Lahore headquarters, he said: “Thousands of  cases are being reported and some matters require decisions within days  rather than weeks or months. I will raise the issue of the shortage of  personnel with the prime minister.” If an investigating officer is  given 3,000 to 4,000 cases, how could they work, he asked, highlighting  the pressure on the cybercrime investigation system. Transactions  ranging from Rs10,000 to millions of rupees had been reported in such  cases, he said. The minister said Punjab had a population of  around 140 million while the NCCIA had only 61 officers across the  province. He said the government was also pursuing cooperation with  other countries and maintaining daily contact with embassies to address  cybercrime-related matters. He stressed the need for a nationwide  awareness campaign, particularly to protect women and girls from online  blackmail. He advised people, especially young women, not to share  personal photographs with others online, saying authorities had  encountered cases in which victims shared their pictures and were  subsequently blackmailed. “Cases involving girls being blackmailed are among the most common complaints,” he said. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Lahore Cantt railway station gets new computerised signalling system
description: LAHORE: In a bid to ensure safe train operations, the Lahore Cantt Railway Station has finally been equipped with a computer based interlocking (CBI) signalling system, while the Lahore Railway Station will also get the same system in the next couple of months, replacing the decades-old manual point system (kanta). Talking to Dawn on Friday, Railways (PR) Lahore Divisional Superintendent Inamullah Khan said: “The replacement of the old kanta system with the modern CBI system in Lahore division started from the Shahdara Station. Later, other stations, such as Raiwind and Okara Cantt were also equipped with this facility.” He explained that PR teams were working to install the CBI system at other stations and they would replace the manual point system at the Lahore Railway Station too. He said the installation of the CBI system at the Cantt Station was required as a priority due to the station’s yard complexity. Pakistan Railways has been undertaking efforts to modernise its signalling infrastructure through the introduction of the CBI system, aimed at improving train operations and enhancing safety. The system is designed to replace conventional mechanical and relay-based signalling arrangements with computer-controlled technology that manages railway signals, track points and train routes. Under the new system, operators can control signals and track points through a computerised interface. The system checks availability of selected routes, position of track points and conflicting train movements are prevented before a train is permitted to proceed. In the event of a fault, the fail-safe design is intended to place signals in a restrictive state, helping reduce the risk of accidents caused by conflicting routes or signalling failures. After installation, testing and commissioning (ITC) of the system, it was opened for trial operations on Oct 21 at the Cantt Station. During initial trials, various trains passed safely through the newly-commissioned system. “It is a fully automated system that sets the route, ensures safe train operations and records all operational activities related to interlocking, operators etc. It enables PR to check the on-duty operators and their activities,” the DS maintained. Talking to Dawn, an official of the CBI system project said the system had been installed at all railway stations from Shahdara to Lahore except Lahore’s main station and the Khanewal Railway Station. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: ‘Illegal appointment and promotion’: PU suspends two senior faculty members on Punjab Assembly body’s direction
description: LAHORE: On the direction of the Punjab Assembly’s Standing Committee on Higher Education, Punjab University has suspended two professors —Azhar Naeem and Kamran Abid — from service, allegedly on their illegal appointment and promotion. The standing committee had issued the direction following a motion moved by MPA Raja Shaukat Bhatti, demanding the university authorities to finalise a comprehensive inquiry against the two teachers and submit a report within two weeks. The committee meeting, which was presided over by MPA Sumaira Saeed and attended by the Punjab University vice chancellor and registrar, focused on the controversial appointments and promotions of the two faculty members in 2014. Raising serious questions about their academic eligibility, Mr Bhatti asserted that the professors faced severe allegations of bypassing syndicate decisions and securing appointments and advancements with the alleged connivance of the former university administration. MPA Rana Arshad stressed the need for scrutinising all recruitment and promotion records of the varsity, determining the exact role played by the PU management. The committee instructed that administrative officers and other officials found involved in the irregularities must be clearly identified, with their names explicitly incorporated into the final inquiry report. Under the directives, proceedings against both professors are to be conducted strictly under the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability (Peeda) Act, with the administration mandated to present all facts and compliance measures before the standing committee within a fortnight. The controversy originates from an adjournment motion previously tabled in the house by Mr Bhatti regarding alleged unlawful advancement, specifically naming Azhar Naeem for securing an unmerited promotion, alongside a disputed scholarship. Although the initial motion highlighted a single professor, Bhatti noted that Kamran Abid’s case was identical, leading the committee to reach a unanimous decision to initiate formal disciplinary action. Rana Arshad confirmed that the directives for investigation and enforcement have been formally communicated to the vice chancellor. In a separate political development, Punjab governor has summoned the 46th session of the Punjab Assembly. Scheduled for Monday (Oct 26) at 2pm, the session will be presided over by Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan. A formal notification has already been issued by the assembly secretariat.Meanwhile, according to suspension notifications issued on Oct 23, Prof Dr Azhar Naeem and Prof Dr Kamran Abid were suspended from service with immediate effect, until further orders. The action followed a meeting of the standing committee on October 22, which took up adjournment motion No 406/26 regarding the alleged illegal appointments of the two professors. The suspension orders were issued by PU Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Muhammad Ali Shah under Section 15(3) of the University of the Punjab Act, 1973, subject to approval by the university’s syndicate. Dr Azhar Naeem is a professor at the Institute of Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering, while Dr Kamran Abid is the institute’s director. Both have been directed to report to the registrar’s office and will receive subsistence allowance under the rules. In a separate order, Associate Professor Dr Fainan Hanif was assigned responsibility for handling the routine affairs of the director’s office as a stop-gap arrangement until further orders. PUASA: The Punjab University Academic Staff Association (PUASA) has called for an inquiry into alleged illegal appointments and promotions at the university. PUASA President Dr Amjad Abbas Magsi welcomed the standing committee’s intervention and its direction for an inquiry. He said the Lahore High Court (LHC) had also ordered an inquiry into the appointments.PUJAC: The Punjab University Joint Action Committee (PUJAC) has accused the administration of withholding facts and presenting a “one-sided” account before the standing committee. It also alleged that the administration had failed to disclose the LHC’s ruling on the appointments. PUJAC said it would pursue legal remedies and hold a meeting on Monday to review the matter and decide its next course of action. Separately, the affectees of Punjab University’s Town III housing project also welcomed the suspensions and called for investigations into the appointments and promotions of the two professors. Town III affectees’ president Dr Khurram Shehzad alleged that the assets of the two professors increased substantially since the launch of the Town III project. He said Dr Azhar Naeem and Dr Kamran Abid served as secretary and member, respectively, of the project’s management committee. He said the affectees had been waiting for their plots for the last 10 years and called for accountability under the law. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Robbers kill man who tried to save cop’s family in Karachi
description: KARACHI: A man was shot dead while trying to save a policeman’s family from robbers near Sohrab Goth late on Thursday night, police and a relative said on Friday. Police said Rahimullah, 40, a passer-by, was shot dead when three robbers opened fire as they attempted to flee after committing a robbery near Shafiq Mor. The police registered an FIR against three unidentified suspects on the complaint of Mohammed Danish Iqbal. In his complaint, Mr Iqbal said he was a constable posted to the investigation wing of the East police and lived in Ahsanabad. He said he had gone with his family to attend a wedding ceremony near Sakhi Hasan Chowrangi. While they were returning, their car broke down near Shafiq Mor. As they pulled over and checked the vehicle, three robbers on a motorcycle arrived and snatched purses and mobile phones from the complainant and his relative. In the meantime, a man, later identified as Rahimullah, ran towards the robbers who panicked and opened fire on him. They then fled with the looted valuables. The wounded was taken to the Abbasi Shaheed Hospital where doctors pronounced him dead. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Aseefa reaffirms commitment to polio-free Pakistan
description: KARACHI: On World Polio Day being observed globally on Saturday (today), First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari reaffirmed the commitment to a polio-free Pakistan, where every child can grow up healthy and protected from this preventable disease. In her message released here on Friday, she paid tribute to frontline polio workers, particularly women vaccinators, who reach children in challenging conditions and said their dedication deserved all respect and support. “The security personnel who protect vaccination teams also serve an essential role. Attacks on those working to protect our children must not deter us from this national effort.” She said Pakistan has made progress in the fight against polio, but the work is not yet complete. “Every child who misses vaccination remains at risk. We must ensure that no child is left behind, particularly in communities where reaching families can be difficult.” She said a polio-free Pakistan is within reach, but it will require sustained effort and the participation of every one of us. Rotary International pledges support Rotary International has reaffirmed its support for Pakistan’s efforts to stop the spread of the wild poliovirus in the country. In a statement, Rotary International President Olayinka Hakeem Babalola, who helped lead eradication efforts in Nigeria on Africa’s road to wild poliovirus-free certification in 2020, said, “We have contributed more than $3bn — including $1.3 million from Rotary members in Pakistan — and invested more than half a billion of these funds and countless volunteer hours to protect over 45 million children in Pakistan from this paralysing disease.” “Africa’s achievement demonstrates that with collaboration and political and financial support, ending polio in Pakistan and eradicating it globally is possible,” he added. Rotary members also advocate for government support and raise awareness around polio immunisation, a critical function in Pakistan given that vaccine refusals remain an obstacle to reaching every child. “Pakistan is demonstrating strong progress with only a handful of reported cases this year, and in order to safeguard our credibility and maintain trust, we are continuing to address other community needs,” said Aziz Memon, chair of Rotary’s Pakistan National PolioPlus Committee. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Notices issued on petition for holding student union elections at Karachi University
description: KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Friday issued notices to the chief secretary and others on a petition seeking student union elections at the University of Karachi (KU). A two-judge constitutional bench of the SHC headed by Justice Riazat Ali Sahar also directed the registrar of KU to appear in person on Nov 12. Citing the chief secretary, secretary universities & boards department, secretaries of education and law departments and vice chancellor as well as the registrar of KU as respondents, Ali Sher   Muhammad Haris had petitioned the SHC and submitted that they were students of law at the university and have been directly affected by the non-implementation of the Sindh Students Union Act. The counsel for petitioners Usman Farooq advocate argued that the law has provided a framework for the establishment and functioning of student unions in educational institutions across the province and such institutions were bound to formulate regulations and procedures for conducting student union elections within two months after the enactment of such regulations. SHC summons varsity registrar for Nov 12 He also submitted that the University of Karachi Act, 1972 also has a provision about the student union at the university, but the KU has not framed any regulation or procedure for the election of student union despite the fact that the law was enacted around four years ago. The counsel further contended that student organisations and unions had existed on the campuses across the country since independence and played an active role in its political and social life, the same were banned in 1984 through martial law orders issued by the administrators of the various zones, while such ban was lifted in 1988-89 after the provincial Assembly had repealed such order. He maintained that the universities & boards department has framed the draft rules under the act, but the same had not been finalised or notified and petitioners have also filed an application with the department concerned for placing the rules draft before the cabinet and notifying the same. He argued that the KU was also bound under Section 3(3) of the Act for framing regulations and arranging student union elections, but the prolonged non-implementation of the statute and administrative inaction have caused a blanket ban on all students irrespective of individual conduct. The lawyer also submitted that the continued inaction of the respondents has violated the petitioners’ rights as guaranteed in Articles 4 (right to be dealt with in accordance with law), 16 (freedom of assembly), 17 (freedom of association), 19 (speech and expression) and Article 25 (equality before law) of the Constitution, while the respondents were public functionaries and bound to perform the duties as required by law within a reasonable time as a statutory duty with a fixed time limit cannot be left unperformed for years. He further maintained that in an identical petition, filed last year in the SHC, the universities & boards department in its comments said that all educational institutions were empowered to frame their own regulations but no institution has yet finalised its regulations while the draft rules, shared with all universities including the KU in 2024, were undergoing legal vetting by the law department and thereafter would be submitted to the provincial cabinet. The petitioners pleaded for directions to the respondents to complete the vetting of the Sindh Students Union Rules, place the same before the provincial cabinet within 30 days and notify in the official gazette. They also sought directives for the VC and registrar of KU to frame regulations and procedures, constitute an election commission and make all arrangements to hold student union elections at the university. After a preliminary hearing, the bench in its order said, “Let at first, notices be issued to the respondents as well as advocate general Sindh, who shall file their respective comments. The respondent No.6 registrar of Karachi University shall be in attendance on the next date of hearing”. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Untreated waste discharged from 537 locations in Sindh termed serious health threat
description: KARACHI: Speakers at a seminar said that untreated industrial, medical and municipal waste discharged from 537 locations across Sindh is posing serious threats to the environment, aquatic ecosystems and public health in the province. Addressing the seminar titled ‘Climate Resilience and Management of Water-Dependent Ecosystems in Sindh’ organised by the Pakistan Red Crescent Society (PRCS) Sindh, former Supreme Court judge Justice Amir Hani Muslim highlighted shortcomings in wastewater treatment and environmental regulation. Referring to Karachi’s wastewater infrastructure, he said only one of the city’s four treatment plants was partially functional. He raised concerns about the use of funds allocated for a treatment plant near Mauripur, stressing the need for effective project oversight and accountability. The former judge, who also once headed a Supreme Court-formed water commission, expressed concerns over the disposal of hazardous medical waste, saying that the lack of functional incinerators in major hospitals had resulted in such waste being mixed with ordinary municipal garbage. Ex-SC judge raises concerns over use of funds allocated for treatment plant near Mauripur He called for strict enforcement of environmental laws, effective action against industries discharging untreated waste, and the installation of mandatory effluent treatment facilities in factories. He emphasised that policies alone could not resolve the environmental crisis without practical implementation, monitoring and accountability. Retired Justice Amir Hani Muslim also stressed the importance of public awareness and tree plantation in protecting the environment and maintaining ecological balance and urged individuals and institutions to contribute to a greener and more sustainable future. PRCS Sindh Branch chairman Rehan Hashmi said the protection of water-dependent ecosystems was essential for strengthening climate resilience, promoting sustainable water resource management and safeguarding vulnerable communities from climate-related risks. He underscored the need for coordinated efforts and effective strategies to address environmental challenges. Provincial Secretary of PRCS-Sindh Kanwar Waseem in his welcome remarks, highlighted the importance of bringing together experts, institutions and stakeholders to address environmental challenges through coordinated action, effective policymaking and practical implementation. Other speakers included Brig Dr Nasim, President of the Pakistan Academy of Engineering and Advisor for SIFC Karachi; Nouman Saigal, former provincial minister for environment and chairman of the Standing Committee on Climate Change at the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI); and Emilio Teijeira, Regional Head of the German Red Cross (GRC), Asia Pacific. The speakers highlighted the importance of inter-institutional collaboration in strengthening environmental protection and addressing climate-related challenges. The dialogue also examined implementation barriers under the Sindh Water Policy, priority actions for 2027 and beyond and opportunities to strengthen ecosystem-based climate adaptation. The participants called for practical measures to control pollution, conserve water resources and promote sustainable environmental management across Sindh. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: CM Bugti sees smaller units as key to good governance
description: • Says Rakhni is being developed as a model division to strengthen province’s development landscape • Praises security forces for foiling an attempt to target a construction company in Gwadar QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti has said that the establishment of smaller administrative units is essential to ensure the delivery of government services to people at their doorsteps. He said that alongside the creation of new provinces, there was also a need to establish smaller divisions and districts to facilitate public access to civil administration and government departments. The chief minister expressed these views while speaking to the media at a press conference in North Dera Bugti on Friday. He said all divisional posts for Koh-i-Suleman Division had been approved and that officers and staff would be appointed to these positions soon. CM Bugti said the debate on establishing smaller administrative units had only recently begun at the national level, whereas he had initiated work on the matter two years ago, keeping in view Balochistan’s unique circumstances and the needs of its people. He stressed that the administrative structure must be designed to bring state institutions and civil administration closer to the public so that people would not face difficulties in accessing government services. The chief minister said efforts were underway to develop Rakhni as a model division of Balochistan and give it a prominent place in the province’s development landscape. He observed that Rakhni should have been granted divisional status much earlier, but the development process had now begun. He said strict instructions had been issued to ensure that development projects in Rakhni remained free from corruption, corrupt practices and commission-based dealings. The communications and works department was directly implementing the development schemes to ensure transparency, he added. CM Bugti said the government was committed to maintaining complete transparency in the development projects in the town. Referring to the terrorist incident in Gwadar, the chief minister praised the timely response of security forces for foiling an attempt to target the building of a construction company. He said the sacrifices and operations of the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and police in the fight against terrorism in Balochistan were commendable. The chief minister said a decline in terrorist incidents in the province since August was a positive development resulting from the sustained efforts of the security forces. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Non-communicable diseases account for 60pc of deaths, say speakers
description: ISLAMABAD: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) account for around 60pc of deaths in Pakistan, while more than 35 million people are living with diabetes. This was stated by President Pakistan National Heart Association (Panah) retired Maj Gen Masudur Rehman Kiani. He was speaking to participants of an event organised to sensitise masses regarding warning labels on ultra-processed foods. He claimed that consumers cannot make healthy choices without clear information about excessive sugar, salt and unhealthy fats in packaged products. The event was organised by Panah along with its coalition partners. Representatives of the Pakistan Kidney Patients Association, HeartFiles, Pakistan Medical Association and Pakistan Association of Family Physicians attended the event. They formed a lawyers forum to strengthen legal and policy advocacy for mandatory Front-of-Pack Warning Labels (FOPWLs) on ultra-processed products. Mr Kiani said: “Consumers have a fundamental right to know what they are eating,” calling for stronger measures to address the growing burden of diet-related diseases. Stronger measures urged to address growing burden of diet-related diseases Panah general secretary Sanaullah Ghumman said mandatory warning labels could help consumers identify products containing excessive amounts of sugar, salt and unhealthy fats and encourage healthier food choices. He urged the government and regulatory bodies, particularly the Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority (PSQCA), to expedite implementation of FOPWL regulations without allowing commercial interests to undermine public-health measures. Senior Supreme Court advocate Akhlaq Awan, speaking for the newly formed Lawyers Forum, said access to accurate food information was a consumer right and a matter of public interest. The participants called for easily understandable warning labels and immediate regulatory action, particularly to protect children and young people from preventable diet-related diseases. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

title: No change to 2024 constituencies: Election Commission of Pakistan
description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has ‘re-described’ constituencies following administrative changes made by the provincial government, and has not redrawn constituency boundaries in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In a statement explaining its move a day earlier, the commission claimed that it has the power to ‘re-describe’ constituencies under Rule 15 of the Election Rules 2017 following changes to administrative divisions, adding that this has been done before. The provincial government of Khyber Pakht­unkhwa had made changes to administrative units in various districts, including the formation of new districts and tehsils, as well as changes to certain tehsils, it said. The ECP maintained that existing constituency boundaries would not change, and they remain the same as they were during the 2024 general elections. The commission also maintained that Section 22 of the Elections Act 2017 — which makes it mandatory for the ECP to invite and hear representations over its proposed alterations — does not apply in this instance, as no constituency has been redrawn. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: PM sets indicative wheat price at Rs4,500 per maund for 2027
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday set the illustrative price for wheat at Rs4,500 per maund for 2027, raising the procurement price set last year by Rs1,000. “In view of the increase in production costs, the price had been raised by Rs1,000 per maund compared to last year,” a statement by the PM’s Office (PMO) said. It quoted the premier as saying that the decision was taken with the guidance of President Asif Ali Zardari and PML-N President Nawaz Sharif and in consultation with the chief ministers of Punjab and Sindh. The PMO statement added that the prime minister’s decision was aimed at “promoting agriculture sector in the country, protecting farmers’ economic interests and increasing wheat production next year”. Moreover, the statement quoted PM Shehbaz as saying that the government’s objective behind increasing the proposed wheat procurement price was to provide relief to farmers amid rising production and fuel costs, as well as inflation pressure. “Providing farmers with an incentive to cultivate wheat is among the key objectives of the decision,” the prime minister said. He expressed hope that the new proposed price would help farmers cover their production costs and earn profit. “Over the past years, farmers have faced financial difficulties due to inflation and rising agricultural expenses while Pakistan has also had to import wheat in the last two years,” he said, adding that the decision to increase the illustrative price would prove to be an important step forward in “strengthening the country’s food security, encouraging local production, and bringing stability to the agriculture sector”. “The government expects that the determination of the proposed price will generate greater interest among farmers in wheat cultivation, resulting in ample sowing of wheat in the upcoming season and brighter prospects for increased national production. “This step taken by the prime minister will prove to be an important milestone in the efforts to improve the economic well-being of farmers, stabilise the agricultural economy and make the country more self-reliant in meeting its nutritional needs. It is hoped that 2027 will bring positive results for Pakistan’s agricultural sector and its farmers,” the PMO statement said. It added that the prime minister expressed gratitude to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for her cooperation in the consultative process for the decision, as well as to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah for his cooperation. The proposed price of Rs4,500 is still Rs500 less than the price demanded by farmers. Last month, the Pakistan Kissan Ittehad demanded a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price for wheat, warning that farmers may not sow wheat for the next season if the government delays announcing crop policies. The association had maintained that the farmers were unable to afford balanced fertiliser use because they were not recovering production costs. In early October, Sindh CM Murad had approved the release of government wheat at the rate of Rs12,500 per 100kg bag from Oct 15 in order to stabilise flour prices and ensure its availability in the province. On Oct 13, PM Shehbaz chaired the first National Agricultural and Food Security Council meeting and reaffirmed that the government wanted farmers to get a fair price for wheat and consumers to have affordable wheat. During the meeting, he declared that wheat was available in abundant quantities to meet domestic needs, and vowed no leniency for hoarders.

title: Pakistan calls for fairer global order at UN
description: WASHINGTON: Pak­istan has called for a more representative international order and consistent application of international law during a series of debates at the United Nations this week. Its interventions covered Security Council reform, military artificial intelligence (AI), weapons of mass destruction, radiation safety, human rights and conflicts in the Middle East, highlighting the need to balance international security with accountability and the interests of developing countries. Addressing the General Assembly on Thursday, Pakistan’s acting permanent representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, opposed creating additional permanent seats on the Security Council, arguing that this would perpetuate existing inequalities. “The question is not whether the Council should be reformed, but how to make it more representative, democratic, transparent and accountable,” he said. Pakistan favoured expanding elected, non-permanent membership through regular elections and fair regional rotation, while seeking adequate representation for Africa and other underrepresented regions. On military AI, Mr Jadoon called for inclusive, UN-led governance, warning that the technology could accelerate military decision-making and increase escalation risks, particularly in situations involving nuclear weapons. He also stressed the need for meaningful human control over autonomous weapons systems. At the General Assembly’s First Committee, Counsellor Syed Atif Raza warned that advances in AI, synthetic biology and the life and chemical sciences were creating new security risks. He called for safeguards against the misuse of scientific developments without restricting developing countries’ access to peaceful applications. Pakistan reaffirmed its commitments under the biological and chemical weapons conventions, stressing the importance of verification and international cooperation. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: New York’s city council votes to ban Central Park horse carriages
description: NEW YORK: New York’s city council voted on Thursday to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, signalling the end of a tourist ritual that’s been subject to years of heated debate. Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who must sign the measure into law, had previously voiced support for such a ban, but has also expressed concern regarding protection for workers in the industry. If the mayor signs it, the ban will go into effect in June 2028. The lead-up is meant to help the approximately 150 active carriage drivers find new employment, a city council spokesperson told journalists. The Transport Workers Union representing those labourers have vowed court action. Legislative battles over the fate of the cultural tradition that’s nearly as old as Central Park itself have been ongoing for nearly two decades. Critics say the animals suffer, pointing to deadly collapses and dangerous escapes, while advocates point to the jobs they create and the heritage they uphold. The rides, enshrined in film including Robert Redford and Jane Fonda’s scene in Barefoot in the Park, or a dramatic ride in Sex and the City, currently run for $150 for 45 minutes and up to several hundred dollars for a marriage proposal. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Alleged online sadist arrested after teen’s suicide in US
description: BERLIN: German police acting on an FBI tipoff arrested an alleged online sadist accused of driving a 14-year-old US girl to hang herself, prosecutors said on Friday. The suspect was linked to an online group called  “Nefarious Maniac Kult”, or “NMK”, part of a global network known by the labels “764” or  “COM”, the Hamburg public prosecutor’s office said. The case echoes others in a dark online subculture where predators manipulate, exploit and extort young victims -- a category of crime that has been labelled “nihilistic violent extremism”. The 18-year-old German was arrested in Hamburg on Thursday, accused of being the indirect perpetrator of murder and grievous bodily harm. Between September and October, the suspect allegedly “exerted influence” via the social network Discord over the girl from Indiana state, whom prosecutors described as “psychologically fragile”. The suspect allegedly pressured the girl to cut herself and write the letters “NMK” on a wall in her own blood, and had her send him video recordings of these acts. A few days later, she hanged herself in her bedroom, prosecutors said. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Russia, Ukraine agree to Oleshky ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump, White House says
description: US First Lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said on Friday. Residents of the southern Ukrainian town, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis. “Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway,” a White House statement said. The development comes as Melania’s husband, President Donald Trump, pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war, which began when Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Melania has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families. “The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” Melania said in the statement. The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed American media organisation accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said. Oleshky , located across the Dnipro River from Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to 2,000 people, primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children, down from roughly 24,000 before the war, the White House said. About 90 per cent of the city was flooded following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House. The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire. “Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” Melania Trump said.

title: Brent crude hits more than five-month high on concern over Middle East escalation
description: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures gained $1.40, or 1.2 per cent, to $114.57 a barrel by 1138 GMT (4:38pm PKT), having earlier reached $115 for the highest level since May 4. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.48, or 1.5pc, to $100.95. The Brent benchmark is on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, of 4.2pc, while WTI is poised to finish 0.5pc down on the week. Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported, as fighting intensified between the world’s largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis. “The market remains concerned about a potential escalation, which, in a worst-case scenario, could trigger renewed supply disruptions,” said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that volatile oil flows and elevated freight rates have left the market undersupplied. Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government have raged since the Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandab , a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea. “The key factors to monitor now are the extent of actual disruption and the time needed to restore operations, as these will ultimately determine how much of a supply risk premium the market is willing to pay,” said XS.com analyst Linh Tran. “If attacks persist and delay deliveries, elevated prices will have a firmer foundation.” An oil spill from a tanker was detected off the coast of Umm Al Quwain, prompting containment operations and environmental assessments, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said on Friday. The ministry did not say what caused the spill, and authorities have not identified the tanker involved. In Libya, an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port was shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday. Meanwhile, the first Russian diesel bound for the US since a surprise agreement between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed today. Trump announced the deal this month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of US midterm elections next month.

title: New Greece law bans social media for under-15s
description: Greece’s parliament passed a law on Friday banning children under 15 from social media, joining a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people’s use of the apps. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced plans for the ban in April, taking to TikTok — one of the most popular social networks with young people in Greece — to explain the “difficult but necessary” measure. After a heated debate in a parliamentary session that started on Thursday and stretched into Friday, Mitsotakis’s conservative New Democracy party used its majority to pass the bill, which no other parties backed, the Ana news agency reported. The opposition socialist Pasok party abstained after seeking an alternative bill that would have banned social media for under-13s and parental controls for 13- and 14-year-olds. Other left-wing and nationalist parties voted against. The bill, set to take effect on January 1, will require age verification on social networks and impose harsh penalties if companies fail to comply. Australia last year became the first country to introduce such a social media ban for kids, barring under-16s. More than 20 countries have passed similar laws, according to an AFP tally. Critics say social networks use addictive algorithms to keep kids glued to their screens, and warn excessive scrolling can damage their mental health. Bans have faced pushback from free-speech advocates, and sceptics question how well they will work.

title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, nearly 1,000 flights cancelled
description: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, and though the storm is weakening it could still make direct landfall on the island. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph near its centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 220 km east of Taiwan, the CWA said. The storm’s forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan. One person was killed and 171 were injured in Taiwan, where the government said 2,639 people had been evacuated from mountainous areas. Taipower said more than 77,000 homes had lost power, though electricity had already been restored to most. Typhoon Champi swirls over the Philippine Sea, as seen from space on October 23, 2026 in this screengrab taken from a handout GIF image. —CSU/CIRA and JMA/JAXA/Handout via Reuters CWA forecaster Liu Pei-teng told Reuters that landfall could not be ruled out if it “stalls, loops, or wobbles from side to side” on approach to Taiwan. “The storm’s wind radius is quite large, among the bigger ones in recent years,” Liu said. “If the storm slows down, the strong winds will affect Taiwan for longer.” Coastal towns received mobile phone alerts warning of gusts exceeding 150 kph and urging residents to seek immediate shelter, while nearly a metre of rain was forecast for northern mountain areas, including around Taipei. In the northeastern county of Yilan, where strong winds and heavy showers were intensifying and the typhoon was forecast to pass close by later on Friday, authorities distributed sandbags and put amphibious vehicles and inflatable rescue boats on standby. A pedestrian holds an umbrella in strong winds as Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan on October 23, 2026. —Reuters “When necessary, the military will come in to help people, including using amphibious vehicles for evacuations or disaster relief,” said Lee Ming-chen, head of the port town of Suao, which was badly flooded in previous typhoons. In the northern port city of Keelung, boat owners hurried to secure their vessels. “It’s not that severe; I’m just worried that there will be flooding. Keelung has seen a lot of flooding this year,” said construction worker Liu Yu-en, 18. Huge radius Taiwan forecasters said the storm’s radius was around 320 km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days. Taiwan’s financial markets also closed on Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal. A fisherman walks among fishing nets at a fishing port as Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan on October 23, 2026. —Reuters The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with 717 international ones. The north-south high-speed rail service was operating as usual. In the capital Taipei there were squally showers, but public transport including the subway was working, albeit with reduced service. Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too. The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan’s westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.

title: West Bank attack wounds 5 Israelis as Netanyahu cancels events
description: An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and triggered a shootout that left two Palestinians dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections. An AFP journalist who witnessed the firefight saw two Palestinian men in casual attire and armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city of Hebron. The journalist reported that Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers. The Israeli military said soldiers had rushed to the Judea Junction area, also known as the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint, after the early-morning shooting attack. “Israel Defence Forces (IDF) soldiers eliminated two terrorists and continue searches in the area,” it claimed in a statement. Netanyahu claimed Israel had prevented a “major attack” after soldiers killed the two armed Palestinians. He added that he had instructed the military to “impose a cordon on the city of Hebron and to prepare for a full closure of the entire West Bank starting today”. Open-source Telegram groups reported that many checkpoints in the area had already been closed The initial shooting wounded five people, two of whom were in critical condition, said Magen David Adom, Israel’s emergency medical rescue service. The Magen David Adom said one of the victims was a man in his 20s in “very serious condition” with gunshot wounds. Netanyahu, running for a new term in elections on Tuesday, called for all political meetings to be cancelled Friday due to the attack. Israeli National Security Minister and far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir, who has been rising in the polls, called for the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority to be dismantled because of the attack. No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority, the Palestinian government in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, was connected to Friday’s attack. Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief who is Netanyahu’s top rival in the election, praised the response by troops. “Like all Israelis, I pray for the complete and quick recovery of the injured,” he said. The incident comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters , and days ahead of Israeli elections. According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed 1,113 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023. Israeli figures show at least 49 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.

title: Leghari warns Discos against arbitrary billing
description: ISLAMABAD: Energy Minister Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari has warned electricity distribution companies (Discos) against imposing excessive or unjustified detection bills, saying no arbitrary charges will be levied on consumers. Detection bills are issued by Discos to recover past dues estimated to be unpaid due to slow meters, theft or other technical reasons. At a meeting with Discos’ boards of directors on Friday, the minister issued formal directives to implement a stringent, comprehensive reform framework. He underlined that while curbing electricity theft remains an unquestionable national priority, arbitrarily burdening innocent citizens will not be tolerated under any circumstances. Under this framework, the discretionary authority of field staff is being strictly regulated to protect consumers while ensuring that no hurdle is created for honest officers performing their duties against power theft. In light of the minister’s directives, the Power Division is mandating that all Discos issue detection bills exclusively through the centralised online portal developed by Power Information Technology Company (PITC). The Power Division has enforced a complete ban on issuing manual and discretionary detection bills by field staff or SDOs. Issuing manual bills will be officially treated as severe misconduct, liable to strict disciplinary proceedings and major penalties against the responsible officials and staff. Under this framework, comprehensive proposed amendments to the Consumer Service Manual (CSM) will be submitted in the coming days to bind every process within clearly defined timelines. Under the new framework, replacing defective or burnt meters immediately, or within a maximum of two billing cycles, will be mandatory, and average billing during this period will be restricted to a maximum of two months. In cases where a meter is established to be running slow or fast, recovery or credit adjustments will be confined strictly to the preceding two billing cycles. Similarly, to bring detection billing under strict regulation, the chargeable period for illegal abstraction by general consumers is proposed to be fixed at three billing cycles. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Govt unveils 170 tweaks to Companies Act
description: ISLAMABAD: Around 170 amendments have been made to the Companies Act 2017 to facilitate company registration and business operations and to modernise Pakistan’s corporate regulatory framework. Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan disclosed this at a news conference on Friday, alongside Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain and members of his cabinet. The adviser said the complexity of the regulatory framework and the difficulties of doing business had been major factors discouraging foreign investment in Pakistan. “Over the past 78 years, laws and regulations have been introduced to meet various needs. However, over time, unnecessary complexities and overlapping requirements have accumulated, making it difficult for businesses to operate efficiently,” the adviser said. Haroon Akhtar says reforms to simplify registration, cut compliance costs and attract investment He highlighted that 170 amendments have been approved by the federal cabinet and the relevant bill has been forwarded to parliament. Mr Khan said that regulatory reviews were underway in several sectors, including dairy, maritime, beverages, oil refineries, pharmaceuticals and restaurants. The objective is to identify redundant requirements, streamline procedures and ensure that regulations serve legitimate public and economic interests without imposing unnecessary burdens on businesses. According to Mr Khan, the government studied international regulatory systems, particularly those of Delaware in the US, the UK and Canada, as benchmarks for the proposed reforms. He explained that the government was conducting a comprehensive review of regulators and of laws and regulations affecting businesses across the country. The reform process has made substantial progress, with approximately 60-70 per cent of the overall work completed. Reform proposals submitted by various institutions recommend eliminating, on average, 70-75pc of unnecessary or duplicative regulations. Highlighting the proposed Asaan Karobar Act, Mr Khan said the government was working to establish a business environment aligned with international best practices. The initiative aims to simplify regulatory procedures, reduce compliance costs, and create a more predictable, investor-friendly framework for businesses operating in Pakistan. The government has also engaged a senior international consultant with experience in regulatory reform across 135 countries to support the process. Mr Khan said the government was undertaking historic reforms to simplify the business environment, remove unnecessary regulatory hurdles, and promote domestic and foreign investment in Pakistan. He emphasised that effective reforms required close coordination between the federal government and provincial and regional administrations. The government was working to advance reforms not only at the federal level but also in coordination with the provinces, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. “We want to ensure that federal and provincial reforms are aligned so that businesses across Pakistan can operate in an environment that is simpler, more transparent and more consistent,” he said. Industrial inspections Regarding industrial inspections, Mr Khan noted that businesses often faced multiple inspections from different departments, including those responsible for labour, environmental protection, fire safety, buildings, and boilers. Overlapping procedures could disrupt operations and create avoidable compliance costs. He said the proposed reforms would bring greater transparency and consistency to the inspection system, protect the rights of businesses and industrialists, and reduce unnecessary difficulties while maintaining essential regulatory safeguards. The government was considering international best practices to develop a more efficient and balanced inspection framework. The adviser also outlined plans for an integrated, single-window digital portal where businesses can submit applications and connect with relevant provincial authorities and regulatory bodies. The proposed platform is intended to reduce the need for businesses to visit multiple departments and help them complete necessary regulatory procedures through a single point of access. “Our objective is to make investment easier, reduce the cost of doing business and restore the confidence of both domestic and foreign investors. Businesses should be able to focus on production, innovation and expansion rather than navigating unnecessary procedural hurdles,” he said. Mr Khan reiterated that the government was committed to creating an enabling environment in which investors could make decisions with confidence, industries could expand, and new employment opportunities could be generated. He concluded that simplifying business regulations, strengthening domestic industry, and attracting investment were essential to sustainable economic growth, industrial development, and job creation in Pakistan. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Karachi Industrial Park approved as federal Special Economic Zone
description: ISLAMABAD: The federal government has approved Karachi Industrial Park (KIP) as a federal Special Economic Zone (SEZ) to attract export-oriented industrial investment, promote technology transfer and value addition, and generate employment. The decision was taken at the 11th meeting of the Board of Approvals for SEZs here on Friday. Chai­­red by Finance Mini­ster Muhammad Aurang­zeb, the meeting discussed measures to facilitate industrial investm­ent, improve infra­struc­ture provision and ensure the effective utilisation of industrial land. According to an official announcement, the board approved the application for KIP to be designated as a federal SEZ. The proposed zone aims to attract export-oriented industrial investment, encourage technology transfer and value addition, and create jobs. The board also approved the General Eligibility Criteria for providing utilities and allied services up to the designated zero point of privately established SEZs through government funding under the SEZ Act, 2012. The criteria establish a framework for considering the provision of road access, utilities and other essential facilities at government expense on a case-by-case basis. In addition, the board approved the Land Lease Policy for Public Sector SEZs and Industrial Estates in Punjab. The policy seeks to promote industrial investment through long-term leasing, reduce upfront land costs and ensure the optimal use of public-sector industrial land, while encouraging investment in key sectors and emerging industries with high export potential. The decisions reflect the government’s continued focus on facilitating industrialisation, improving the investment climate and strengthening the SEZ framework. The measures are intended to support greater private-sector participation, encourage export-oriented production and ensure the effective utilisation of public resources and industrial land. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

title: Rising flour prices fuel weekly inflation
description: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose to 11.85 per cent year-on-year in the week ending October 22, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday. The index, which comprises 51 items whose prices are collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services. Short-term inflation has remained in double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum prices. The data showed that of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, the prices of 19 commodities (37.72pc) increased, while those of 12 items (23.53pc) declined. Meanwhile, the prices of 20 items (39.22pc) remained unchanged from the previous week. The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly increased by 0.65pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items. Unwilling to ease the petroleum levy , the government has continued to raise petrol and diesel prices on a daily basis. The surge in energy costs is not only fuelling inflationary pressures but also indirectly boosting sales tax collections through higher prices of goods and services. This is cost-push inflation, in which rising energy costs are followed by increases in food prices. As a result, households are under pressure from higher consumer prices. The items whose prices increased the most over the previous week included liquefied petroleum gas (22.44pc), chicken (12.20pc), onions (4.19pc), shirting (1.86pc), plain bread (1.66pc), wheat flour (1pc), garlic (0.74pc), firewood (0.71pc), georgette and one kilogramme of vegetable ghee (0.59pc each), beef (0.31pc) and pulse mash (0.30pc). The items whose prices declined week-on-week included tomatoes (21.99pc), petrol (3.63pc), banana (2.42pc), diesel (1.68pc), potatoes (1.38pc), pulse gram (0.93pc), eggs (0.58pc), powdered milk (0.38pc) and broken rice basmati and sugar (0.35pc each). On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included LPG (107.12pc), onions (72.81pc), electricity for Q1 (58.59pc), petrol (44.17pc), diesel (41.56pc), chicken (38.99pc), wheat flour (36.49pc), chilies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.66pc), beef (12.10pc), bread plain (10.82pc) and tea prepared (8.36pc). In contrast, tomato prices fell by 71.72pc, followed by potatoes (40.75pc), sugar (25pc), eggs (22.14pc), salt powder (14.86pc), pulse masoor (9.08pc), gur (8.98pc) and pulse moong (7.05pc). Last week, short-term inflation rose to 11.38 per cent year-on-year, driven largely by higher food prices , data from PBS showed.
